steps: Soaking the beans: Put the 500g white beans in a bowl with plenty of cold water and leave them overnight (8-10 hours). Soaking hydrates the beans, drastically cuts the cooking time, and helps them soften evenly without splitting their skins.

First boil and skimming: Drain the beans, put them in a pot with fresh cold water, and boil for 10 minutes. IMPORTANT: skim off the white foam that rises to the surface carefully — it contains the compounds that cause bloating and cloud the broth. Discard this first water for a cleaner, more digestible bean soup.

Adding the vegetables: Cut the 2 carrots into rounds, and finely chop the 2 celery stalks and the 1 onion. Add them to the pot with the beans, the 2 bay leaves, and enough fresh hot water to cover by 2-3 finger-widths. Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes so the vegetables gradually release their sweet aroma into the broth.

Tomato and oil: Add the 200g grated tomato and the 4 tbsp olive oil. IMPORTANT: don't salt too early — salt toughens the skins and the beans stay undercooked. Salt only now, once they have already begun to soften.

Finishing the cooking: Continue simmering gently for another 20 minutes until the beans are completely tender and the soup thickens slightly. For a thicker result, mash a ladleful of beans with a fork and stir them back in — this gives natural body without flour.

Serving: Serve the fasolada hot and drizzle with a little raw olive oil right at serving time — raw oil keeps its full aroma and adds freshness. Accompany with Kalamata olives and country-style bread.
fasolada.plate: Deep bowl, raw olive oil, 2-3 olives.

steps: Preparing the tomatoes: Wash 3 large ripe tomatoes and cut them into thick slices or large chunks (about 3-4 cm). Thick pieces hold their juices and won't fall apart, while ripe tomatoes give the natural sweetness that defines a horiatiki salad.

Cutting the cucumber: Wash the cucumber and cut it into thick rounds about 1 cm. If the skin is tough or waxed, partially peel it in strips. IMPORTANT: don't cut the cucumber too far ahead, as it releases water and dilutes the oil and juices of the salad.

Onion and pepper: Cut 1 onion into very thin slices (half-moons) so it doesn't overpower the flavor, and 1 green pepper into rings. If the onion is very sharp, rinse it briefly under cold water to remove the harsh bite.

Arranging on the platter: Layer the tomatoes on the bottom first, then the cucumber, onion, and pepper on top. This order lets the tomato juices collect at the bottom and become a natural dressing together with the olive oil.

The feta: Place 150g feta as a WHOLE slab in the middle of the salad. IMPORTANT: never crumble the feta in a horiatiki salad — kept whole, it retains its texture and moisture and doesn't dry out or dissolve into the juices.
Olives and seasoning: Scatter 80g Kalamata olives around the edges, drizzle with 3 tbsp good olive oil, and sprinkle salt and plenty of oregano over the feta. Oregano on the oil releases its aroma.

Serving: Do NOT toss the salad before it's served at the table. Tossing early draws out liquid and softens the vegetables. Serve immediately with fresh bread to dip into the juices (the classic "paparo").
horiatiki.plate: Feta left whole, like an island.

steps: Preparing the marinade: In a bowl, mix the juice of the 2 lemons, their zest, 4 tbsp olive oil, 4 mashed garlic cloves, oregano, and thyme. The zest gives a strong lemon aroma without making the dish overly sour.

Marinating the chicken: Put the 1.5kg chicken pieces into the marinade and leave them in the fridge for at least 1 hour. IMPORTANT: the lemon's acidity tenderizes the meat fibers and infuses flavor, so the longer it marinates (ideally 2-3 hours), the juicier it turns out.
Preparing the potatoes: Cut the 600g potatoes into evenly sized wedges so they all roast together. Arrange them in the roasting pan alongside the chicken.

Arranging in the pan: Spread the chicken and potatoes in a single layer and pour over all the marinade. Season generously with salt and pepper. Not crowding the pieces helps them brown instead of stewing in their own juices.
Roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 55-60 minutes. For the first 40 minutes you can cover with foil if needed to prevent drying out.

Turning and browning: At 40 minutes, turn the pieces for even cooking and a golden color on all sides. IMPORTANT: if the pan has dried out by the end, add a little hot water so the potatoes don't burn.
Resting and serving: Let the chicken rest 5-10 minutes out of the oven before serving, so the juices redistribute and it stays succulent.
kotopoulo.plate: Pieces with potatoes, lemon zest, oregano.

steps: Soaking the bread: Put the 2 slices of stale bread in a little water for 2-3 minutes, then squeeze them very well with your hands. Stale bread absorbs the meat's juices and yields fluffy meatballs, while thorough squeezing prevents the mixture from becoming watery and falling apart in the pan.

Mixing the ingredients: In a large bowl, combine the 500g ground beef, the grated onion, the squeezed bread, 1 egg, finely chopped parsley, 1 tsp mint, salt, and pepper. Mint gives Greek meatballs their characteristic aroma.
Kneading: Knead the mixture by hand for 2-3 minutes until it's homogeneous and holds together. IMPORTANT: don't overwork it, as the meat tightens up and the meatballs turn out tough instead of juicy.

Resting in the fridge: Cover the bowl and let the mixture rest in the fridge for 30 minutes. Resting firms up the mixture, lets the flavors meld, and makes the meatballs easier to shape without sticking.
Shaping: With wet or lightly oiled hands, shape small meatballs of equal size so they cook evenly. You can roll them lightly in flour for a crispier crust.

Frying: Heat olive oil well in a pan and fry the meatballs over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp all over. Don't overcrowd the pan, as the temperature drops and they'll stew instead of browning.
Draining and serving: Transfer the meatballs to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil. Serve them hot with tzatziki, potatoes, or fresh lemon.
keftedes.plate: Platter, lemon, parsley, tzatziki on the side.

steps: Boiling the pasta: Bring plenty of water (about 2 liters) to a boil with coarse salt and add the 200g spaghetti. Boil for 8-9 minutes so it stays al dente, meaning it still has some bite, since it will finish cooking in the pan.

Reserving the pasta water: Before draining, reserve 1 cup of the starchy cooking water. IMPORTANT: this water is the secret of the recipe, as the starch binds the olive oil to the pasta and creates a creamy, glossy sauce without cream.
Preparing the aromatics: Cut the 5 garlic cloves into thin slices and finely chop the 1-2 hot chili peppers, so they gradually release their aroma into the oil.

Sautéing the garlic: Warm the 60ml olive oil over low heat and sauté the garlic and chili for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden. IMPORTANT: don't let the garlic burn, as it turns bitter and ruins the whole dish's flavor.

Combining with the pasta: Add the drained spaghetti to the pan along with a little of the cooking water and toss vigorously (shake the pan) for 1-2 minutes, so the oil emulsifies and the sauce comes together.
Serving: Add finely chopped fresh parsley and grated Parmesan, toss, and serve immediately while hot, so the sauce doesn't dry out.
aglio.plate: A nest of spaghetti, parsley, Parmesan.

steps: Preparing the shrimp: Clean the 500g raw shrimp, removing the shell and the dark vein along the back, but leave the tail on for presentation. Pat them very dry with paper towels. IMPORTANT: dry shrimp brown rather than boiling in their own liquid.
Sautéing the shrimp: Heat olive oil over high heat and sauté the shrimp for 1-2 minutes per side, until they turn golden and pink. Remove them immediately so they don't toughen from overcooking.
Sauce base: In the same pan, sauté the 2 garlic cloves for 30 seconds until fragrant without browning, as burnt garlic turns bitter. Add the 200g grated tomato and oregano.
Simmering the sauce: Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until it loses its excess liquid and thickens, concentrating the tomato flavor.
Flaming with ouzo: Deglaze with the 2 tbsp ouzo and let the alcohol evaporate for 1 minute. Ouzo gives a characteristic anise aroma that pairs beautifully with seafood.
Finishing: Return the shrimp to the sauce and scatter the 100g feta over the top in chunks.
Gratinating: Place the pan (or transfer to an ovenproof dish) under the grill for 3-4 minutes until the feta softens. Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve immediately, hot.
garides.plate: Served straight from the pan, parsley, bread.

steps: Preparing the vegetables: Finely chop 1 onion, grate or slice the 2 carrots into rounds, and mash the 2 garlic cloves. This way the aromatics release their flavor evenly as they sauté.

Sautéing the base: In a pot, heat 3 tbsp olive oil over medium heat and sauté the onion, carrots, and garlic for 5 minutes, until softened and glossy. Sautéing sweetens the onion and adds depth of flavor to the soup.

Adding the tomato: Add the 150g grated tomato and the bay leaf and let it cook for 2-3 minutes to lose its sharpness. IMPORTANT: don't add salt yet, as salt in an acidic environment toughens the lentils and slows their cooking.
Rinsing the lentils: Rinse the 400g lentils in a colander under running water to remove dust and any small stones. Small lentils don't need soaking.
Boiling: Add the lentils and water until covered by 2-3 finger-widths. Boil over low-to-medium heat for 30-35 minutes, until softened but still holding their shape. Top up with hot water if needed.
Finishing: Once softened, add the 1 tbsp vinegar, salt, and pepper. Vinegar at the end is the classic Greek secret that balances the flavor and brightens the soup. Remove the bay leaf before serving.
fakes.plate: Deep bowl, raw olive oil, vinegar, olives.

steps: Preparing the ingredients: Finely chop 1 onion and 2 garlic cloves, grate 400g tomato, and have the 100ml red wine ready. Organizing everything beforehand (mise en place) keeps you from burning something while hunting for ingredients.

Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot with a little olive oil, sauté the onion over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until glossy and softened, then add the garlic for 30 seconds. IMPORTANT: don't let the garlic brown, as it turns bitter.

Browning the meat: Raise the heat and add the 500g ground beef. Break it up with a spoon and let it brown well for 6-8 minutes without stirring constantly, so it caramelizes and develops depth of flavor instead of stewing in its own liquid.
Deglazing with wine: Add the 100ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 1-2 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot to release the caramelized bits that carry flavor.
Simmering the sauce: Add the grated tomato, a little cinnamon, allspice, and salt. Simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes until the sauce thickens and the flavor becomes sweeter and rounder.

Boiling the pasta: Boil the 400g pasta in plenty of salted water for 8-10 minutes, so it stays slightly firm (al dente) with some bite. IMPORTANT: keep a cup of the cooking water to loosen the sauce if needed.
Serving: Drain the pasta, divide it among the plates, spoon the meat sauce over it, and sprinkle with plenty of grated kefalotyri, which melts slightly from the heat.
kima.plate: Deep plate, rich sauce, grated cheese.

steps: Preparing the vegetables: Cut the tops off the 6 tomatoes and the 4 peppers without detaching them completely, so they can be put back on as lids. Carefully scoop out the tomato flesh with a spoon, and IMPORTANT: keep all the juices and pulp — this will be the liquid that cooks the rice from within and gives deep flavor. Stand the vegetables upright in a roasting pan.
Sautéing the onion: Finely chop the 2 onions and sauté them in a little of the olive oil until glossy and softened. Sautéing sweetens the onion and removes its raw sharpness from the filling.

The filling: In a bowl, combine the 300g rice (uncooked), the sautéed onion, finely chopped parsley and mint, the reserved pulp and juices, the 1 tsp sugar, and the 5 tbsp olive oil. The sugar balances the tomato's acidity. Season with salt and pepper.

Filling the vegetables: Fill the tomatoes and peppers only three-quarters full. IMPORTANT: don't overfill — the rice expands during baking, and if filled to the top it will overflow and split the vegetables. Cover with their lids.

Baking: Pour a little water into the bottom of the pan (about one glass) so nothing sticks and steam can form. Bake at 180°C for 60-70 minutes, until the rice has swelled and the vegetables have caramelized at the edges.

Resting and serving: Remove from the oven and let stand for at least 15-20 minutes before serving. Resting allows the rice to absorb the last of the liquid and the stuffed vegetables to firm up so they don't fall apart on the plate.
gemista.plate: With lids on, basil, olive oil.

steps: Preparing the spinach: Wash 600g spinach very well in plenty of water to remove dirt and grit, then chop it finely. IMPORTANT: drain it very well, as excess water dilutes the dish and throws off the liquid-to-rice ratio.

Sautéing the onions: In a pot, heat 4 tbsp olive oil and sauté 1 finely chopped onion along with 4 finely chopped spring onions over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, until softened and glossy without taking on color. This sweetens them and adds depth of flavor.
Wilting the spinach: Add the spinach and stir over high heat for 3-4 minutes until it wilts and reduces in volume. The spinach releases its own liquid, which will help cook the rice.
Adding the rice: Add the 150g rice and stir for 1 minute to coat the grains in oil (they'll turn glossy), so the rice stays separate and fluffy. Add 350ml hot water and salt.
Simmering: Lower the heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, until the rice has absorbed the liquid and softened. Don't stir constantly, so it doesn't turn mushy.

Finishing: Remove from the heat and add the juice of 1 lemon and plenty of fresh chopped dill. IMPORTANT: the lemon and dill go in at the end, off the heat, to preserve the freshness and aroma that would otherwise be lost through cooking.
Serving: Let it rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with feta on the side, whose saltiness pairs with the lemon's acidity.
spanakoryzo.plate: Deep plate, lemon, feta on the side.

steps: Preparing the eggplant: Cut the eggplants into slices about 1 cm thick. Salt them generously and let them sit in a colander for 30 minutes — the salt draws out bitterness and excess moisture, so they won't soak up oil and turn the moussaka watery. Rinse and pat them very dry with paper towels.

Roasting the vegetables: Brush the eggplant and the potatoes (sliced 0.5 cm thick) with a little olive oil and roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until softened and lightly browned. Roasting instead of frying keeps the dish lighter. Set aside.

Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot, heat 2-3 tbsp olive oil over medium heat and sauté the finely chopped onion for 5-6 minutes until glossy and softened — don't let it burn, we want sweetness, not bitterness.

Browning the meat: Raise the heat, add the ground beef, and break it up with a spoon. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until its liquid evaporates and it browns — this stage builds depth of flavor as the meat's sugars caramelize.

Meat sauce: Deglaze with half a glass of wine (optional) and let it evaporate for 1-2 minutes. Add the grated tomato, a cinnamon stick (or 1/2 tsp ground), salt, pepper, and a little sugar to cut the acidity. Simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes until it thickens and stops releasing liquid.

Béchamel: Melt 80g butter in a pot, add the flour, and stir for 1-2 minutes to cook it (making a roux — it must not brown). Gradually add the hot milk, whisking constantly so it doesn't lump. Cook until it thickens to a custard-like consistency. Remove from heat, add a little nutmeg, and once slightly cooled, whisk in 2 eggs and a handful of grated kefalotyri.

Assembly: In a baking pan, layer the potatoes first (the base that holds the juices), then half the eggplant, all the meat sauce, the remaining eggplant, and finally all the béchamel spread evenly. Sprinkle cheese on top.

Baking & resting: Bake at 180°C for 50-60 minutes, until the béchamel turns golden and forms a crust. IMPORTANT: let the moussaka cool for at least 20-30 minutes before cutting it — otherwise it will fall apart. Cut into squares and serve.
Cutting the meat: Cut the 600g pork neck into 2-3 cm cubes of even size. Uniform pieces cook at the same rate and don't dry out unevenly.

Marinade: Mix 3 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and 2 mashed garlic cloves. IMPORTANT: don't add salt to the marinade early on, as it draws out the liquid and dries out the meat — salt just before grilling instead.
Marinating: Let the meat sit in the marinade for at least 1 hour in the fridge. The lemon and olive oil tenderize and deeply flavor the pork.
Skewering: Thread the cubes onto skewers without packing them too tightly. Leaving small gaps between the pieces lets air circulate so they brown all over.

Grilling: Grill over a well-heated grill or barbecue for 10-12 minutes, turning regularly every 2-3 minutes for even browning. IMPORTANT: the grill must be very hot before you add the meat, so a crust forms and the skewers don't stick.
Resting: Let the skewers rest 2-3 minutes before serving so the juices settle.
Serving: Serve in warm pita bread with tzatziki, tomato, and onion.
souvlakia.plate: In pita or on a plate with potatoes.

steps: Meat sauce: Sauté the finely chopped onion in a little oil until softened, add the 500g ground beef, and sauté until browned. Add the 300g grated tomato and a little cinnamon and simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens. Cinnamon gives pastitsio its characteristic aroma.

Boiling the pasta: Meanwhile, boil the 500g thick pasta in salted water for 9-10 minutes, slightly firm (al dente) so it still has bite. IMPORTANT: don't overcook it, as it will keep cooking in the oven and turn mushy.

Making the béchamel: Melt the 80g butter, add the 4 tbsp flour, and stir for 1-2 minutes to cook the flour. Gradually add the 1 liter milk, whisking constantly so it doesn't lump, until the mixture thickens into a custard.

Finishing the béchamel: Remove from heat and add eggs and part of the kefalotyri, mixing quickly. IMPORTANT: add the eggs only after the béchamel has cooled slightly, otherwise they'll curdle and scramble.

Layering: In a greased baking pan, layer half the pasta, sprinkle with cheese, spread all the meat sauce over it, then the remaining pasta, and finally the béchamel. Sprinkle with the remaining kefalotyri for a golden crust.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 45-50 minutes, until the top is well browned. Let the pastitsio cool for 15-20 minutes before cutting, so it sets and the pieces hold together.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g spaghetti in salted water until al dente, slightly firm. Reserve a cup of the cooking water before draining, as it will help the sauce come together.
Browning the bacon: Cut the 150g bacon into strips and brown it in a dry pan (no oil) over medium heat until crisp, so its fat renders and flavors the dish.
Egg mixture: In a bowl, whisk the 3 eggs together with the 2 yolks, the 80g grated kefalotyri or pecorino, and plenty of freshly ground pepper, until smooth and creamy.

Combining off the heat: IMPORTANT: remove the pan from the heat before adding the egg. Add the hot spaghetti to the bacon, then the egg mixture and a little cooking water, stirring quickly and constantly.
Forming the cream: Stir vigorously so the residual heat turns the egg into a smooth, velvety cream. If it starts to set like scrambled egg, the heat was too high.
Serving: Serve immediately with extra grated cheese and fresh pepper on top, as carbonara is eaten hot and loses its creamy texture if it cools.
karbonara.plate: On a warm plate, pepper, grated kefalotyri.

steps: Browning the chicken: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil and brown the 4 chicken thighs on all sides over high heat. IMPORTANT: good browning seals in the juices and adds depth of flavor to the dish.
Sautéing the onion: Remove the chicken and sauté the 1 finely chopped onion in the same oil until glossy and softened, absorbing the chicken's juices.
Sauce with spices: Add the 300g grated tomato, the cinnamon stick, and the 3 cloves. These spices give the classic aromatic note of a red (kokkinisto) sauce.
Simmering the chicken: Return the chicken to the pot, add water to almost cover it, and simmer covered for 30 minutes until the meat softens and the sauce thickens.
Adding the hilopites: Remove the chicken and keep it warm. Add the 300g hilopites into the sauce and stir well so they're coated all over. Add hot broth if there isn't enough liquid.
Cooking the hilopites: Cook the hilopites for 12-15 minutes, stirring regularly, until they absorb the sauce and turn al dente. IMPORTANT: stir often so they don't stick to the bottom.
Serving: Place the thighs on top of the hilopites and sprinkle with plenty of grated kefalotyri, which melts from the heat and ties the dish together.
hylopites_kotopoulo.plate: Deep plate, chicken on top, kefalotyri cheese.

steps: Preparing the aromatics: Cut the 4 garlic cloves into thin slices and finely chop the 1-2 hot chili peppers. Thin garlic slices release aroma without burning easily.

Sautéing: In 4 tbsp olive oil over medium heat, sauté the garlic and chili for about 2 minutes, until fragrant. IMPORTANT: be careful not to burn the garlic, as it turns bitter and ruins the whole sauce.
Sauce: Add the 400g grated tomato and a little salt. Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, until it thickens, turns glossy, and loses its raw acidity.
Boiling the pasta: In plenty of boiling salted water, cook the 200g penne al dente, meaning slightly firm, 1-2 minutes less than the package instructions. It will finish cooking in the sauce.
Cooking water: Before draining, reserve a cup of the starchy cooking water. This water binds the sauce to the pasta and helps it become velvety.
Tossing: Add the penne to the sauce along with a little cooking water and stir for 1-2 minutes over high heat so it's well coated. Add fresh basil.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, and sprinkle with Parmesan if desired. Arrabbiata-style pasta is best eaten freshly made, so the sauce doesn't dry out.
Preparing the mushrooms: Clean the 300g mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of water, then slice them. IMPORTANT: don't wash them, as they'll soak up water and end up boiling instead of browning.

Browning the mushrooms: Over high heat with a little olive oil, add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them without stirring too often, until golden, 5-6 minutes, so they caramelize instead of releasing all their liquid.
Deglazing with wine: Add the 60ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 1 minute, scraping the bottom of the pan to gather the flavors.
Cream sauce: Add the 2 finely chopped garlic cloves and thyme, sauté for 30 seconds, then add the 200ml heavy cream. Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g tagliatelle in salted water until slightly firm. Reserve a little cooking water before draining.
Bringing it together: Transfer the tagliatelle to the sauce with a little cooking water and toss. The starchy water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.
Finishing: Off the heat, add the 20g butter and the 50g Parmesan and stir. IMPORTANT: off the heat, so the Parmesan melts creamily and the sauce doesn't split.
pasta_manitaria.plate: A nest of tagliatelle, mushrooms on top, thyme.

steps: Preparing the seafood: Clean the 200g shrimp, the 150g baby squid (cut into rings), and wash the 200g mussels thoroughly, discarding any that are already open. IMPORTANT: pat the shrimp and squid dry with paper towels — moisture prevents browning and makes them release water instead.

Quick searing: In hot olive oil over high heat, sauté the shrimp for just 1 minute and the squid for 1 minute. Remove them immediately. Seafood needs minimal cooking — any longer and it turns rubbery.

Sauce base: In the same pan, add the 3 finely chopped garlic cloves and sauté briefly until fragrant. Deglaze with the 100ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate — this leaves the aroma and acidity without any harshness.

Mussels and tomato: Add the mussels to the sauce and cover for 3-4 minutes until they open. IMPORTANT: discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking — they aren't safe to eat. Add the 200g grated tomato and salt, and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g linguine in salted water until al dente, slightly firm. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining — the starchy water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.

Combining and serving: Add the linguine to the sauce along with all the seafood and toss for 1 minute over high heat with a little cooking water. Add finely chopped parsley and raw olive oil. Serve immediately while hot and fragrant.
pasta_thalassina.plate: Deep plate, seafood on top, parsley.

steps: Browning the lamb: In a pot or clay dish, heat a little oil and brown the 1kg lamb pieces on all sides over high heat. IMPORTANT: good browning (caramelization) seals in the juices and gives the final dish deep color and flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: In the same pot, sauté 1 finely chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves until softened, scraping up the caramelized bits from the bottom, which hold concentrated flavor.

Sauce and cooking the meat: Add the 400g grated tomato, a cinnamon stick or a pinch of ground cinnamon, salt, pepper, and enough hot water to cover. Bake covered at 180°C for 50 minutes, until the lamb begins to soften.

Adding the orzo: Add the 300g orzo and stir it into the liquid. IMPORTANT: there must be plenty of hot liquid (about double the volume of the orzo), as the pasta absorbs a lot and would otherwise stay raw or stick.
Second bake: Continue baking at 180°C for another 30 minutes, stirring once halfway through so the orzo cooks evenly and doesn't stick at the edges.
Resting: Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes. The orzo finishes swelling and the sauce settles.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot and saucy, with plenty of grated kefalotyri on top, which melts and adds a salty punch.
giouvetsi.plate: In the baking dish, plenty of cheese.

steps: Cleaning and scoring: Clean the 500g sea bream and dry it well. Make 2-3 diagonal cuts on each side. The scoring helps it cook evenly and lets the flavor penetrate into the flesh.

Salting and aromatics: Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle oregano inside and outside the fish. IMPORTANT: dry the skin thoroughly with paper towels before salting, as moisture prevents the skin from crisping up.
Filling the cavity: Place lemon slices and garlic inside the cavity along with a little thyme. This flavors the fish from within as it roasts.
Preparing the potatoes: Cut the 300g potatoes into thin slices and arrange them on the bottom of the roasting pan. Place the fish on top so the potatoes cook in its juices.
Drizzling: Pour 3 tbsp olive oil and the juice of the remaining lemon over the fish and potatoes.
Roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes. IMPORTANT: don't overcook it — it's ready as soon as the flesh separates easily from the bone, otherwise it dries out.
Serving: Serve immediately with fresh lemon juice and a little olive oil on top.
Cleaning and cutting: Clean the 500g of squid and cut into rings about 1 cm thick. Even cutting means even frying.
Drying: Pat the rings very dry with paper towels. Important: this is a crucial step for a crisp result, since moisture causes hot oil to spatter and makes the flour coating clump and turn soggy.
Flouring: Mix 1 cup of flour with salt and pepper. Dredge the rings in the flour and shake off the excess, so a thin, crisp crust forms without any clumps of flour.
Heating the oil: Heat plenty of olive oil in a deep pan until very hot (about 175-180°C). The hot oil instantly seals the crust so the squid doesn't soak up oil and stays crisp.
Frying: Fry the squid in small batches for 2-3 minutes until golden. Don't overcrowd the pan, as this drops the temperature and results in rubbery rather than tender squid.
Draining and serving: Transfer to paper towels to drain, season lightly with salt, and serve immediately with fresh lemon while still hot and crisp.

Desalting: Soak the salt cod (600g) for 24-36 hours in cold water, changing the water 3-4 times a day. Important: frequent water changes are essential to remove the excess salt, otherwise the fish will remain unbearably salty.
Drying: Drain the cod well and pat dry with paper towels, so the coating adheres properly and doesn't cause the oil to spatter during frying.
Boiling the potatoes: Boil the 3 potatoes in their skins until tender, then peel them while still hot so the skordalia purées more easily and smoothly.

Skordalia: Mash the potatoes together with the 5 garlic cloves, gradually adding olive oil and the 2 tbsp of vinegar, until creamy. Important: add the oil gradually so the mixture emulsifies and doesn't split.
Coating and frying: Dust the cod with the cup of flour and fry in hot olive oil for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp.
Serving: Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the skordalia on the side and olives, for the classic flavor combination.
bakaliaro.plate: Cod with skordalia, olives, and greens.

steps: Cooking the octopus: Place the 1kg octopus in a pot with no water over low heat. It will release its own liquid. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Important: cooking it in its own juices keeps it tender and concentrates its flavor.
Cutting: Once tender, remove the octopus and cut it into bite-sized pieces, reserving the cooking liquid to add to the sauce later.
Sautéing the onion: Sauté the 2 finely chopped onions and 3 garlic cloves in olive oil until softened and sweet.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with 200ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 2-3 minutes, so only the rich flavor remains without the sharp acidity.
Building the sauce: Add 200g grated tomato, the bay leaf, and the octopus with a little of its cooking liquid. Stir to combine everything.
Simmering: Simmer for 20-25 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns velvety. Serve hot, ideally with hilopites pasta or fresh bread.
htapodi.plate: On a platter with parsley, lemon, and rusk (paximadi).

steps: Soaking the bread: Soak the 4 slices of stale bread (crusts removed) in water for a few minutes until softened. Stale bread binds better and gives the taramosalata a light, fluffy texture.
Squeezing: Squeeze the bread very well with your hands to remove all the water. Important: if any water remains, the taramosalata will turn out watery and won't come together.
Base in the blender: Place the 100g tarama, the squeezed bread, and the 1 small grated onion in the blender and blend until combined into a smooth paste.

Adding oil and lemon: Pour in the 150ml olive oil in a very thin stream, alternating with the 2 tbsp lemon juice, while the blender runs continuously. The slow stream of oil creates an emulsion and keeps the mixture combined.
Whipping until fluffy: Continue blending until it becomes a fluffy, uniform cream. Taste and adjust the lemon to your liking.
Resting in the fridge: Refrigerate the taramosalata for at least 1 hour before serving. The chilling firms up the texture and lets the flavors meld.
taramosalata.plate: In a bowl with olive oil and olives, lagana bread on the side.

steps: Preparing the syrup: In a pot, combine 3 cups water, 2 cups sugar, and cinnamon, and bring to a boil, keeping in mind the classic 1-2-3-4 ratio (oil-semolina-sugar-water). Once it boils and the sugar dissolves, lower the heat and keep it warm.

Toasting the semolina: In another pot, heat the 1/2 cup olive oil and add the 1 cup coarse semolina. Stir constantly over medium heat until golden, about 8-10 minutes. Important: stir continuously, as semolina burns very easily and turns bitter.
Adding the dried fruit: If desired, add the raisins and pine nuts along with the semolina during the last few minutes of toasting, so they become fragrant without burning.
Combining with the syrup: Remove the semolina from the heat and carefully pour in the hot syrup. Important: be careful, as it will hiss and sputter, so pour it slowly and away from your face.
Setting the halva: Return to low heat and stir for 5 minutes until the semolina absorbs all the syrup and the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Molding and resting: Pour into a mold, press down lightly, and let rest for 15 minutes to firm up. This helps the halva hold its shape when sliced.
Serving: Invert the mold onto a serving platter and dust with cinnamon. Serve warm or cold.
halvas.plate: Unmolded onto a platter, dusted with cinnamon and raisins.

steps: Activating the yeast: Dissolve the 7g dry yeast in the 300ml lukewarm water (not hot, around 35°C). Important: if the water is too hot it kills the yeast and the dough won't rise. Let sit for 5 minutes until it foams lightly, a sign the yeast has come alive.

Kneading: In a bowl, mix the 500g flour with the salt, add the yeast mixture and the 3 tbsp olive oil. Knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough becomes smooth and elastic — good kneading develops the gluten that gives a light, airy crumb.
First rise: Cover the bowl with a towel and let the dough rest in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled in size. Rising develops flavor and makes the lagana light.

Shaping: Spread the dough on parchment paper into a thin, flat shape, fairly elongated as traditional lagana is. Using wet fingers, press dimples all over the surface — these hold the shape and keep it from rising too much.
Sprinkling with sesame: Lightly brush the surface with water or oil and generously sprinkle with sesame seeds. The moisture helps the sesame stick and keeps it from falling off during baking.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 220°C for 20-25 minutes until it develops a golden, crisp crust. The high temperature browns the outside quickly while keeping the inside light and airy.
lagana.plate: Serve with taramosalata, olives, and halva.

steps: Boiling the fish and vegetables: In a large pot, place the whole 1kg grouper together with 4 potatoes, 2 carrots, 1 onion, and celery, cover with cold water, and season with salt. Boil over medium heat for 30 minutes. Important: start from cold water and skim off the foam, so the broth comes out clear and clean.
Boning: Carefully remove the fish and vegetables. Bone the grouper, removing all the bones, and set the flesh aside so it doesn't cool completely.
Straining the broth: Strain the broth through a fine sieve to remove any small bones. The clean broth is the base of the soup.
Cooking the rice: Bring the broth back to a boil and add rice or hilopites pasta. Boil for 15 minutes until tender, making sure enough liquid remains for the avgolemono.

Preparing the avgolemono: In a bowl, whisk 2 eggs with the juice of 2 lemons until frothy. Gradually add a ladleful of hot broth while whisking constantly. Important: slowly diluting the mixture gradually raises the temperature of the eggs and keeps them from curdling.
Thickening the soup: Remove the pot from the heat and pour in the avgolemono, stirring gently. Do not bring back to a boil, or the eggs will curdle and split.
Serving: Return the fish flesh to the soup, check the seasoning, and serve immediately while hot, with extra lemon if desired.
psarosoupa.plate: In a deep bowl, with the fish inside and lemon.

steps: Making the broth: Place the whole chicken in a pot with cold water along with the 2 carrots and celery, and boil for 45 minutes. Important: skim off the foam that rises at the start with a slotted spoon, so the broth stays clear and clean-tasting.
Boning: Remove the chicken, let it cool slightly, and bone it into bite-sized pieces. Strain the broth to remove any small bones.
Cooking the rice: Bring the broth back to a boil and add the 100g rice. Boil for 15 minutes until tender. Taste and adjust the salt.
Whisking the avgolemono: Whisk the 2 eggs with the juice of 1 lemon until frothy. Whisking well makes the avgolemono light and prevents it from curdling.

Tempering: Gradually add ladlefuls of hot broth to the egg-lemon mixture, whisking constantly. Important: this step is crucial for gradually raising the temperature of the mixture, because if the eggs go straight into the hot broth they will curdle and form lumps.
Combining off the heat: Remove the pot from the heat and pour in the avgolemono, stirring. Do not return it to a strong boil, or it will curdle.
Serving: Add the boned chicken, sprinkle with fresh dill, and serve hot.
kotosopa.plate: In a deep bowl, with chicken and dill.

steps: Cooking the broth and rice: Bring the 1.5L chicken broth to a boil, add the 100g rice, and cook for about 15 minutes until tender. A good broth is the foundation of flavor in the soup.
Whisking the eggs: In a bowl, whisk the 3 eggs well until frothy and gradually add the juice of 2 lemons while whisking. Whisking well gives a light, velvety avgolemono.

Tempering: Slowly add a few ladlefuls of hot broth into the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Important: the broth is added slowly with continuous whisking so the temperature of the eggs rises gradually and they don't curdle.

Combining with the soup: Lower or turn off the heat and pour the avgolemono into the pot, stirring gently. Important: do not boil the soup again after adding the avgolemono, or the eggs will curdle and ruin the texture.
Adjusting the seasoning: Taste and add salt, pepper, or a little extra lemon as preferred. The balance of tartness and salt gives the characteristic freshness.
Serving: Serve the soup immediately while hot and frothy, with freshly ground pepper on top. The avgolemono thickens over time, so it's best enjoyed fresh.
avgolemono_soupa.plate: With fresh bread. Classic Greek comfort food.

steps: Preparation: Clean and slice the 500g mushrooms, finely chop the onion and the 2 garlic cloves, so they sauté evenly.
Sautéing the aromatics: Melt the 2 tbsp butter in a pot and sauté the onion and garlic until translucent, without browning, so they sweeten.

Cooking the mushrooms: Add the mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes until their liquid evaporates. Important: let them release and evaporate all their moisture, as this concentrates their flavor and keeps the soup from being watery.
Adding the broth: Pour in the 700ml vegetable broth and the thyme, and simmer for 15 minutes so the flavors meld.
Puréeing: Blend the soup with an immersion blender until velvety and smooth, with no lumps.
Finishing: Add the 200ml heavy cream, season with salt and pepper, and warm through a little longer without boiling, so the cream doesn't split. Serve hot.
soupa_manitarion.plate: With whole sautéed mushrooms on top and fresh bread.

steps: Soaking: Soak the 500g chickpeas in plenty of water overnight (8-12 hours). Important: soaking softens the skins, reduces the cooking time, and makes them more digestible.
Par-boiling: Drain the chickpeas, place them in fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes, skimming off the foam that rises to the surface, as it can cause the dish to become bloated.
Preparing the baking dish: Drain and transfer the chickpeas to an earthenware dish along with the 2 coarsely chopped onions, the 6 tbsp olive oil, and the rosemary.
Adding water: Pour in hot water to cover the chickpeas by 2-3 finger-widths, so they have room to cook slowly without drying out.
Slow baking: Bake at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours, covered at first and uncovered toward the end. Important: slow baking at a low temperature makes them buttery and creamy.
Finishing: As soon as they come out of the oven, add the juice of 1 lemon, which freshens the flavor and balances the sweetness of the onion. Serve hot.
revythada.plate: In a deep bowl with raw olive oil and rosemary.

steps: Cutting the vegetables: Slice the 3 zucchini, 2 eggplants, 3 potatoes, 2 bell peppers, and 3 tomatoes into rounds of equal thickness, and finely chop 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves. Important: equal thickness ensures even cooking.
Arranging in the pan: Spread all the vegetables in a large baking pan, mixed together so the flavors combine. Reserve a few tomato slices to layer on top.

Seasoning: Drizzle with the 6 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with salt, pepper, and herbs (oregano or thyme). Toss well with your hands so every piece is coated in oil, which helps them cook without drying out.
A little water: Pour half a glass of water into the bottom of the pan so the vegetables don't dry out at the start of baking and can release their own juices.
Baking: Bake at 190°C for 60-70 minutes. Halfway through, stir gently so everything cooks evenly and doesn't stick to the edges.
Finishing: The briam is ready when the potatoes have softened and the vegetables have caramelized at the edges. Serve warm with feta on top, which balances the sweetness of the vegetables.
briami.plate: On a platter with basil and feta.

steps: Preparing the grape leaves: Blanch the 40-50 grape leaves in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until softened and they change color, so they roll easily without tearing. Drain and trim the stems.

Preparing the filling: In a bowl, mix 250g rice, 2 finely chopped onions, chopped parsley and mint, the juice of 1 lemon, and the 5 tbsp olive oil. The rice stays raw, as it will cook inside the leaf.

Rolling: Place a little filling at the base of each leaf (shiny side down), fold in the edges, and roll into a tight cylinder. Important: don't overfill, as the rice expands and the dolmades could burst.
Arranging in the pot: Line the bottom of the pot with a few leaves and place the dolmades tightly side by side, so they don't unroll while cooking.
Cooking: Add water until it almost covers them, along with the juice of 1 lemon and a little olive oil. Place an inverted plate on top to keep them from moving around.
Simmering: Simmer over low heat for 40-45 minutes until the rice swells and the liquid is absorbed. Taste one to make sure the rice has softened.
Resting and serving: Let the dolmades cool in the pot for 15-20 minutes to firm up, and serve warm or cold with lemon.
dolmades.plate: Served cold or warm with yogurt.

steps: Draining the cucumber: Grate the 1 large cucumber on the coarse side of a grater, salt it lightly, and let it sit for 10 minutes. Important: squeeze it very well with your hands or in a clean towel to remove all the moisture — this is the secret to a thick tzatziki that doesn't turn watery.
Preparing the garlic: Mash the 2-3 garlic cloves into a paste with a little salt. The salt breaks down the fibers of the garlic and distributes its flavor evenly without leaving strong chunks.

Mixing: In a bowl, combine the 500g strained yogurt, the squeezed cucumber, the mashed garlic, the 1 tsp vinegar, and salt. Mix well until smooth. The vinegar adds freshness and balances the richness of the yogurt.
Flavoring: Add chopped dill and the 2 tbsp olive oil and stir gently. The olive oil binds the mixture and gives it a velvety texture.
Resting: Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. Resting lets the flavors meld and mellows the sharpness of the raw garlic, giving a rounder result.
tzatziki_dish.plate: In a bowl, with a spiral of olive oil and dill.

steps: Soaking: The night before, soak 400g gigantes beans in plenty of cold water for at least 8 hours. Important: soaking hydrates the beans, drastically reduces cooking time, and aids digestion.
Par-boiling: Drain and boil the beans in fresh water for 30-40 minutes, until tender but not falling apart. Don't salt the cooking water, as salt toughens the skins. Drain.
Sautéing: In a pan with part of the 4 tbsp olive oil, sauté 2 finely chopped onions, 3 garlic cloves, and 1 grated carrot until softened and sweet.
Sauce: Add 400g grated tomato, 1 tsp honey, salt, pepper, and spices. Simmer for 5 minutes. Important: the honey balances the tomato's acidity and rounds out the sauce's flavor.
Assembling in the pan: In a baking dish, combine the drained beans with the sauce and the remaining olive oil. Add a little hot water so they stay juicy and don't dry out in the oven.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until a crust forms on top and the sauce thickens. If they dry out early, add a little hot water.
Serving: Let cool slightly before serving, as gigantes plaki are best enjoyed warm or at room temperature, with fresh olive oil and bread.
Rinsing: Rinse the 300g Santorini fava under water until it runs clear. This removes the dust and the foam it would otherwise produce during cooking.

Boiling: Place the fava in a pot with plenty of cold water along with 1 chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves. Boil for 30-35 minutes until completely broken down. Important: skim off the foam at the start and add salt toward the end, since early salting toughens the legume.
Checking the liquid: While it boils, top up with hot water if needed so it doesn't dry out or stick to the bottom of the pot.
Puréeing: Transfer the fava to a blender with 5 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, and salt. Blend until it becomes a velvety cream. The olive oil emulsifies and gives it a smooth, soft texture.
Adjusting the texture: If it's too thick, add a little of the cooking water. Important: fava thickens as it cools, so leave it a bit thinner than you want the final result to be.
Serving: Spread onto a plate, drizzle with raw olive oil, and garnish with capers and freshly chopped spring onion for an authentic Santorini flavor.
fava.plate: In a bowl, with a spiral of olive oil and capers.

steps: Cooking the beans: Boil the 500g black-eyed peas for 20-25 minutes until tender. Black-eyed peas don't need overnight soaking like other legumes, which is why this is a quick dish.
Draining: Drain the beans well, reserving a little of the cooking water in case you need to thin the sauce later.
Sautéing the onion: In a pot, heat a little of the olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion until glossy and softened. Sautéing adds sweetness and depth of flavor.
Adding the tomato: Add the 2 finely chopped tomatoes, the celery leaves, and the drained beans. Season with salt and pepper. The celery gives the dish its characteristic fresh aroma.
Simmering: Simmer for about 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the liquid reduces slightly. Important: add the main portion of salt toward the end, since adding it earlier can toughen the bean skins.
Finishing: Off the heat, add the lemon juice and the remaining raw olive oil. The raw oil and lemon added at the end preserve a fresh aroma and flavor that would be lost with cooking. Serve warm.
mavromatika.plate: With olive oil, lemon, and fresh spring onion. A Lenten dish.

steps: Washing: Wash the 100g arugula thoroughly and drain or pat dry with paper towels, so the dressing clings to the leaves and the salad doesn't turn watery.
Cutting the cherry tomatoes: Halve the 100g cherry tomatoes and arrange them with the arugula on a serving platter.
Parmesan: Shave the 60g Parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler. Important: never grated, as thin shavings give a better texture and a more pronounced presence of flavor in every bite.
Dressing: Drizzle the salad with the 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar and the 2 tbsp olive oil, so the acidity balances with the oil.
Serving: Grind fresh pepper on top and serve immediately, as arugula wilts quickly once the dressing is added.
salata_rokka.plate: Parmesan shaved into curls — that's what makes the difference!

steps: Meat mixture: In a bowl, mix the 400g ground beef, the 100g rice, the 1 grated onion, 1 egg, and salt. Knead well with your hands until combined and the mixture binds together.
Shaping: Shape into walnut-sized balls. Important: don't pack them too tightly, as the rice expands during cooking and the giouvarlakia could split.
Boiling: Bring the 1.5L chicken broth to a boil and carefully drop in the meatballs one by one, so they don't stick together.
Simmering: Simmer covered for 25-30 minutes until the rice inside the giouvarlakia is cooked and they've softened. Gently shake the pot occasionally instead of stirring, so they don't break apart.
Preparing the avgolemono: Whisk the 2 eggs in a bowl with the juice of 2 lemons until frothy.
Thickening the avgolemono: Gradually add ladlefuls of hot broth to the mixture while whisking constantly. Important: this tempering step gradually warms the eggs so they don't curdle.
Finishing: Pour the avgolemono back into the pot off the heat, swirling gently to distribute it. Do not boil again, or the avgolemono will curdle. Serve immediately.
giouvarlaakia.plate: In a deep bowl with parsley and lemon.

steps: Kneading the mixture: In a bowl, combine the 600g ground beef, the 1 grated onion, the 1 grated garlic clove, 1 tsp mustard, oregano, salt, and pepper. Knead well with your hands to combine the ingredients into a uniform mixture.
Resting in the fridge: Cover the mixture and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Important: resting binds the meat and firms up the mixture, so the patties don't fall apart while cooking.
Shaping: Shape into round or oval patties about 2 cm thick. With wet hands, shaping becomes easier and the surface comes out smooth.
Preheating the grill: Heat the grill or pan very well. The hot surface immediately caramelizes the meat and seals in the juices, so the patties stay juicy.
Cooking: Grill for 4-5 minutes per side, without pressing the patties with the spatula, as this releases the juices and dries them out.
Resting and serving: Let the patties rest for 3-4 minutes before serving, so the juices redistribute. Serve with potatoes or salad.

Marinating: In a bowl, mix the juice of 3 lemons, 4 tbsp olive oil, 6 crushed garlic cloves and oregano. Rub the mixture all over the 1.5kg leg of lamb and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (ideally overnight), so the acidity of the lemon tenderizes the meat and the flavors penetrate deeply.
Preheating the oven: Preheat the oven to 190°C with top-bottom heat, so the meat cooks evenly.
Preparing the pan: Cut the 600g potatoes into wedges and arrange them in the roasting pan around the lamb. Pour over the marinade and add a little water so they don't dry out.
Roasting: Cover with foil and roast at 190°C for 75-80 minutes total. The initial covering keeps the juices in and cooks the meat until tender.

Turning halfway: At the 50-minute mark, turn the meat and potatoes and remove the foil, so they brown and develop a crispy crust. Important: if the liquids have dried up, add a little hot water so the potatoes don't burn.
Checking doneness: The lamb is ready when the meat pulls away easily from the bone. If needed, leave it a few more minutes.
Resting and serving: Remove the pan and let the meat rest for 10 minutes so the juices redistribute, then serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

Marinating the night before: Open up the 10-12kg lamb and rub it thoroughly, inside and out, with coarse salt, pepper, plenty of oregano and thyme, the 10 garlic cloves, the juice of the 4 lemons and the 200ml olive oil. Important: marinating overnight lets the salt and aromatics penetrate deep into the meat, so the flavor isn't just skin-deep.

Trussing on the spit: Run the spit along the spine and tie the lamb very tightly with wire at the legs, shoulders and body. Tight trussing keeps the meat from hanging loose and turning unevenly over the fire, ensuring it cooks evenly.

Lighting the fire: At 8:00 in the morning, light the charcoal and let it burn down to embers with no flames before you start. Important: never roast over an open flame — it will char the outside while leaving the inside raw. You want steady heat from hot embers.
Steady turning: Position the lamb about 30cm from the fire and begin continuous, slow turning. This distance ensures slow cooking that renders the fat gradually and keeps the meat juicy.
Basting during roasting: Every 30-40 minutes, baste the lamb with a mixture of olive oil and lemon. This keeps the surface moist, helps it brown evenly and adds flavor with every layer.

Checking doneness: After about 3.5 hours the lamb should be evenly browned with a crispy skin. Cut into the thickest part of the thigh — if the juices run clear, it's ready. If they're pink, continue roasting.

Resting and carving: Take the lamb off the spit and let it rest for 15 minutes before carving. Resting allows the juices to redistribute through the meat, so they don't all run out as soon as you cut it, keeping it juicy.
arni_souvia.plate: Whole lamb, lemon, oregano. An Easter tradition!

steps: Cutting the meat: Cut the 1kg pork shoulder and 1kg ribs into even chunks about 4-5cm, cut the 4 chicken thighs into pieces, and keep the 4 country sausages whole. Uniform size ensures everything cooks at the same rate.

Marinade: Toss the meats with 100ml olive oil, plenty of oregano, spices, salt and pepper. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours (ideally overnight). Important: the oil carries the aromatics into the meat and keeps it juicy during the long roasting time.

Skewering: Thread the pork, chicken and sausage alternately onto the large spit, pressing the pieces together tightly. Important: alternating fatty and lean meats keeps the whole thing juicy, while tight packing keeps the pieces from spinning loose on the spit.
Setting up the fire: Light the charcoal and wait until it turns to ash (moderate heat, no flames). High heat would char the outside and leave the inside raw.
Roasting: Roast for 2 to 2.5 hours over moderate heat, turning the spit frequently for even cooking and a crispy crust. Salt periodically as it cooks.
Checking doneness: Make sure the pork and chicken are cooked through in the center (clear juices, no pink at all), since this involves pork and poultry.
Serving: Cut into bite-sized pieces and serve immediately with warm pita, tzatziki and freshly chopped onion.
kontosouvi.plate: Platter with pita, tzatziki, tomato. A feast!

steps: Cleaning the artichokes: Clean the 6 artichokes, removing the tough outer leaves and the fuzzy choke. Place them immediately in water with lemon juice. Important: the lemon water prevents oxidation, so the artichokes don't turn black before you cook them.
Preparing the vegetables: Cut the 4 carrots and 4 potatoes into thick pieces and shell the peas if using fresh ones (300g).
Sautéing: Sauté chopped onion in part of the 4 tbsp olive oil until softened and glossy, without taking on color. This sweetens it and builds a flavor base for the dish.
Adding the ingredients: Add the artichokes, carrots, potatoes and peas. Add water until nearly covered, along with the lemon juice and the remaining olive oil.

Slow cooking: Simmer over low heat for 35-40 minutes until the vegetables soften and the dish is left with its signature lemony sauce. Important: shake the pot instead of stirring with a spoon, so the artichokes and potatoes don't fall apart.
Finishing and serving: At the end, let the liquids reduce slightly. Add plenty of fresh dill and a little more lemon, then serve warm.

Blind baking the crust: Roll out the tart dough into the pan, prick the base with a fork and blind bake (with pie weights or dried beans) for 15 minutes, then another 5 minutes without weights at 180°C. Important: blind baking keeps the dough from puffing up and keeps the base crisp so it doesn't get soggy from the cream.
Cooling the base: Let the base cool completely before adding the cream. If it's still warm, the pastry cream will melt and turn runny.
Spreading the cream: Spread the cold pastry cream evenly over the base with a spatula, so each slice has an even layer.
Arranging the strawberries: Slice the 400g strawberries and arrange them attractively in circles or concentric rings over the cream. An even arrangement gives an impressive appearance.
Glazing: Gently brush fruit glaze over the strawberries for a glossy finish and to keep the fruit from oxidizing and drying out.
Chilling and serving: Refrigerate the tart for 1 hour so it sets and slices cleanly. Just before serving, dust with powdered sugar.
Cleaning the offal: Wash the 500g lamb offal very well and boil for 10 minutes. Drain and finely chop. Important: the initial boiling and skimming cleans the offal and removes its strong odor.
Sautéing: Melt the 2 tbsp butter and sauté the 8 finely chopped spring onions until softened and sweet.
Cooking: Add the offal, the 100g rice, the 6 shredded lettuce leaves, the dill and enough hot stock to cover. Simmer for 20 minutes until the rice softens.
Preparing the egg-lemon sauce: Whisk the 3 eggs with the juice of 2 lemons until frothy, so the soup thickens evenly later.

Thickening with avgolemono: Important: off the heat, gradually add a few ladles of hot broth into the egg-lemon mixture while whisking, then pour the mixture back into the pot, so the eggs don't curdle.
Serving: Serve hot, traditionally after the Resurrection service, as the first dish that breaks the Lenten fast.
Boiling the potatoes: Boil the 4 large potatoes whole, skin-on, in salted water until tender. The skin keeps the potatoes from absorbing too much water and becoming watery.
Peeling: Peel the potatoes while still hot. Important: hot potato mashes evenly and binds better with the oil, while cold potato becomes gluey.
Crushing the garlic: Crush the 6-8 garlic cloves with a little salt in a mortar until it becomes a paste. The salt helps grind the garlic and releases its aromatics.
Combining: Add the hot potatoes and mash them together with the garlic in the mortar, or briefly in a blender, until you have a smooth base.
Emulsifying: Add the 150ml olive oil and the 2 tbsp vinegar alternately, in small amounts, beating continuously until the skordalia becomes creamy and fluffy.
Finishing: Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar. Important: don't overwork the potato in the blender, as it releases starch and turns gluey like paste.
skordalia.plate: Bowl, olive oil, olives. With salt cod.

steps: Marinating the night before: The night before, mix the 100ml olive oil, the juice of 3 lemons, the 8 crushed garlic cloves, oregano, thyme and coarse salt, and rub it all over the 3-4kg suckling pig. Important: marinating overnight in the fridge soaks the meat and makes it aromatic and juicy.
Bringing to room temperature: Take the meat out of the fridge about 1 hour before roasting, so it cooks evenly and isn't cold in the center.
Starting to roast: Place the suckling pig in a roasting pan and roast at 180°C. Cover loosely with foil at first so the surface doesn't dry out.

Potatoes and basting: Cut the 1kg potatoes and arrange them around the meat after the first hour. Total roasting time is 2.5-3 hours, basting with the pan juices every 45 minutes, which keeps the meat juicy and flavors the potatoes as they roast.
Crispy skin: For the last 30 minutes, raise the temperature to 220°C and remove the foil, so the skin turns crispy and golden.
Resting: Remove the meat and let it rest for 15 minutes before carving. This lets the juices redistribute so the meat stays tender. Serve with the potatoes.

Preparing the stuffing: In a pan, sauté 1 chopped onion with a little of the 100g butter and add the 400g ground beef, browning it well for 6-8 minutes so it caramelizes and adds depth of flavor to the stuffing.

Finishing the stuffing: Add the 200g rice, the 300g chopped chestnuts, the 100g raisins and the 100ml wine. Cook for 15 minutes until the liquids are absorbed. Important: let the stuffing cool before putting it inside the turkey, for food safety.
Stuffing the turkey: Fill the cavity of the 4-5kg turkey without overpacking it, and close the opening by sewing it shut or tying the legs, so the stuffing doesn't spill out during roasting.
Buttering: Rub the remaining butter all over the surface and season generously with salt and pepper. The butter helps the skin turn golden and crispy.
Roasting: Roast at 160°C for 3.5-4 hours, covered initially with foil. The low temperature and long cooking time keep the meat juicy and tender.
Basting: Every 45 minutes, baste the turkey with the pan juices so the breast doesn't dry out. For the last 30-40 minutes, remove the foil so it browns.
Checking and resting: It's ready when the juices run clear and the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Important: let it rest for 20-30 minutes before carving, so it stays juicy.
galopoula.plate: Stuffing on the side, sauce from the pan juices.

steps: Drying and browning the meat: Pat the 1kg rabbit pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels and brown them in olive oil over high heat on all sides. Important: don't crowd the pieces in the pot — if packed too tightly they'll release liquid and steam instead of browning. Browning caramelizes the surface and gives depth of flavor.

Deglazing with wine and vinegar: Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and 2 tbsp vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pot to release the caramelized bits. Let the alcohol evaporate for 2-3 minutes so the flavor remains without the bitterness.

Tomato and spices: Add the 200g grated tomato, the 5 garlic cloves, cinnamon, cloves and allspice. Add a little hot water to just cover the meat and simmer, covered, for 45 minutes. The warm spices are the soul of stifado and need time to meld in.

Adding the onions: Add the 500g pearl onions whole into the sauce. Important: leave them whole and add them in the second half of cooking, so they soften without falling apart, staying sweet and intact.

Finishing: Continue simmering gently for another 30 minutes until the rabbit is meltingly tender and the onions have sweetened. The sauce should thicken and turn glossy — if it's too thin, remove the lid for the last few minutes to reduce it.
Serving: Serve the stifado hot, ideally with hilopites pasta, mashed potatoes or bread to soak up the rich sauce.

Preparing the spinach: Wash the 100g baby spinach in cold water and dry it very well, ideally with a salad spinner. Important: the leaves must be completely dry, otherwise the water will dilute the dressing and it won't cling to the leaves.

Cleaning the pomegranate: Cut 1 pomegranate in half and release the seeds by tapping the skin from above with a spoon over a bowl. To avoid staining, do this with the pomegranate submerged in water, where the membrane floats up and the seeds sink.
Toasting the walnuts: Toast the 60g walnuts in a dry skillet (no oil) over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring. Toasting releases their oils and intensifies both aroma and crunch.
Dressing: In a bowl, whisk the 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1 tsp honey and 2 tbsp olive oil with a pinch of salt until emulsified and well combined. The honey balances the acidity of the balsamic.
Assembling: On a platter, arrange the spinach, scatter the pomegranate seeds, the toasted walnuts and 80g crumbled feta on top.
Serving: Drizzle with the dressing just before serving and toss gently. Important: add the dressing at the last moment, otherwise the spinach will wilt and lose its freshness.
Sautéing the base: Sauté the 2 chopped onions, 4 garlic cloves and chopped celery in part of the 5 tbsp olive oil until softened. This aromatic base gives depth of flavor to the sauce.
Tomato sauce: Add the 3 grated tomatoes and salt, and let it simmer for 10 minutes until it thickens slightly and loses its acidity.

Arranging the fish: Place the 800g fish (sea bass or cod) in a roasting pan. Season with salt and pepper. Important: pat the fish thoroughly dry before placing it in the pan, so it doesn't dilute the sauce with water.
Pouring over: Spread the sauce over the fish, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and a little lemon juice.
Roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 180°C for 35-40 minutes. Important: don't overcook it, as fish dries out easily — it's done when the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily.
Serving: Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve warm or at room temperature, as is traditional for plaki-style fish.
psari_plaki.plate: In the roasting pan, plenty of sauce, parsley.

steps: Draining: Drain the 200g Kalamata olives and the 200g mixed pickled vegetables well from their brine. Thorough draining keeps the oil from being diluted and the mixture from turning watery.
Preparing the aromatics: Finely chop or crush 1 clove of garlic. The garlic adds a strong aroma that pairs well with the olives and pickled vegetables.
Mixing: In a bowl, toss the olives and pickled vegetables with the 2 tbsp olive oil, a little oregano, the garlic and 1 tsp vinegar. The vinegar lifts the freshness and balances the saltiness.

Resting for flavor: Let the mixture sit for about 30 minutes so the flavors meld. Important: if the olives are already very salty, avoid adding extra salt and be careful with the vinegar so the mixture doesn't become too sour.
Serving: Serve on small plates as a meze, ideally with ouzo and lagana bread. It's a simple, traditional meze that comes together in minutes.

Browning the meat: Heat olive oil in a pot and brown the lamb pieces (1kg) on all sides over high heat. Important: good browning caramelizes the surface of the meat and gives depth of flavor to the sauce.
Sautéing the aromatics: Add the 2 chopped onions and 4 garlic cloves and sauté until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Pour in the 150ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 2-3 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot to incorporate the caramelized bits.
Adding the tomato: Add the 400g grated tomato, the cinnamon, the allspice and salt, and stir.
Simmering: Cover and simmer for 70-80 minutes until the meat is tender and falling apart. Add a little hot water if needed so it doesn't dry out.
Serving: Serve hot with potatoes, rice or hilopites pasta, letting the sauce thicken slightly before serving.
Preparing the butter: Melt the 100g butter over low heat or in the microwave and let it cool slightly, so it spreads easily over the phyllo sheets.
Filling: In a bowl, mix the 500g grated feta, the 3 eggs, the 100ml milk and pepper. Important: taste before adding salt, as feta is already salty and you risk over-seasoning.
Layering the bottom sheets: Grease the baking pan and layer 6-8 sheets of phyllo, brushing each one with melted butter. The butter between the sheets makes them crisp and puffed when baked.
Spreading the filling: Spread the filling evenly over the sheets, so each piece gets an equal amount of cheese.
Sealing: Cover with another 6-8 sheets, buttering each one again. Fold the edges inward so the filling doesn't escape.
Scoring: Score the pie into pieces with a knife before baking, so it cuts easily afterward without breaking the crisp phyllo. Sprinkle sesame seeds on top.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until golden and crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
tyropita.plate: Warm pieces, salad on the side.

steps: Preparing the spinach: Wash the 1kg spinach very well and chop it finely. Salt it lightly and knead it with your hands so it releases its liquid.
Squeezing: Squeeze the spinach very well to remove as much water as possible. Important: the drier the spinach, the crispier the pie — moisture softens the phyllo.

Filling: In a bowl, mix the spinach with the 400g grated feta, the 6 chopped spring onions, the dill, the 3 eggs and the 4 tbsp olive oil. Add pepper and taste before salting, as feta is already salty.
Layering the bottom sheets: Butter the baking pan and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with melted butter (from the 80g). The butter between the sheets gives crispness and color.
Filling and sealing: Spread the filling evenly and cover with the remaining sheets, buttering each one again. Fold the edges inward.
Scoring: Score the surface into pieces with a knife, without cutting through to the filling. This lets the pie be cut easily afterward and allows steam to escape while baking.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 50-55 minutes, until the phyllo browns and turns crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
spanakopita.plate: Warm, with yogurt on the side.

steps: Sautéing: In a pot, sauté 2 chopped onions until softened, then add the 600g ground beef and brown it well, breaking it up, so it caramelizes rather than stewing in its own liquid.
Meat sauce: Add the 200g grated tomato, cinnamon, allspice and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until almost dry. Important: the filling must be dry, otherwise it will make the phyllo soggy.
Cooling: Let the meat cool slightly, so the eggs don't cook as soon as you add them.
Finishing the filling: Mix the meat with 150g grated kefalotyri and 2 eggs. The eggs bind the filling so it doesn't fall apart when sliced.
Layering the sheets: Butter the baking pan and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing each one with melted butter (from the 80g) to make them crisp and puffed.
Filling and sealing: Spread the filling, cover with the remaining buttered sheets and seal by folding the edges inward. Score the surface into pieces, so it can be cut easily after baking.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 55-60 minutes until golden and crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

Washing and boiling the greens: Wash the 1kg greens (chard, spinach, fennel greens) very well and boil for 5 minutes in a little water until wilted. The brief boiling softens the greens and removes some of their bitterness.

Draining: Drain the greens and, importantly, squeeze them extremely well with your hands or in a towel to remove all the water — this is the secret to a crispy pie, since moisture soaks the phyllo and makes the filling watery.

Filling: Finely chop the greens and mix them with the 4 chopped spring onions, the 300g crumbled feta, the 2 eggs, chopped dill and parsley, and the 5 tbsp olive oil. The eggs bind the filling and the feta adds saltiness — so be careful with extra salt.
Layering the sheets: Oil the baking pan and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing with olive oil between each one. The oil between the sheets creates layers and crispness when baked.

Sealing the pie: Spread the filling evenly and cover with the remaining sheets, oiling again between each one. Important: score the pie into pieces before baking, so the crispy phyllo doesn't break when you portion it afterward.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes until the phyllo turns golden and crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting, so the filling firms up.
hortopita.plate: With yogurt or feta on the side.

steps: Draining the zucchini: Coarsely grate the 1kg zucchini, salt it and let it sit for 15 minutes. Then squeeze it very well with your hands or in a clean towel. Important: removing the liquid is the key to a crispy pie, since moisture would soak the phyllo and leave the filling underbaked.
Sautéing the onion: In a little of the olive oil, sauté 1 chopped onion until softened and sweet, and let it cool before adding to the filling so it doesn't cook the eggs.
Filling: In a bowl, mix the squeezed zucchini, 300g crumbled feta, 3 eggs, the onion and plenty of chopped dill and mint. Taste for salt, remembering that feta is already salty.

Layering the bottom sheets: Melt 80g butter and mix it with a little olive oil. Butter the baking pan and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing each one individually with the butter mixture. Important: buttering each sheet separately gives many crispy, airy layers.
Filling and sealing: Spread the filling evenly and cover with the remaining sheets, brushing with butter again. Fold the edges inward to seal the pie.
Scoring: Score the surface into pieces with a sharp knife and sprinkle with a little water so the phyllo doesn't puff up too much. Scoring helps the steam escape and makes it easy to cut afterward.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 50-55 minutes, until the phyllo browns and turns crispy. Let it set for 10 minutes before cutting.
Washing the leeks: Wash the 1kg leeks very well and chop them finely. Important: leeks hide dirt between their layers, so split them open and rinse leaf by leaf, otherwise the pie will be gritty.
Sautéing: Sauté the leeks in 4 tbsp olive oil for 8-10 minutes until softened and reduced in volume. This drives off moisture and makes the flavor sweeter.
Cooling: Let the leeks cool completely. Important: if you add the eggs to warm leeks they will cook and curdle, so wait for the filling to cool.
Filling: Mix the leeks with 400g crumbled feta, 3 eggs, grated nutmeg and pepper. Be careful with the salt, since the feta is already salty.
Layering the sheets: Layer half the phyllo sheets in a buttered baking pan, brushing each sheet with melted butter (from the 80g). The butter in each layer makes the pie crispy and light.
Sealing and scoring: Spread the filling, cover with the remaining buttered sheets and score the surface into pieces. Scoring makes it easy to cut after baking and lets steam escape.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 50-55 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the filling sets.
Prepping the eggplants: Pierce the 3 large eggplants in several places with a fork so steam can escape and they don't burst while roasting.

Roasting: Roast the eggplants directly over an open flame or under the oven grill for 15-20 minutes, turning them, until the skin is charred all over and the flesh inside is completely softened. Roasting over fire gives the salad its characteristic smoky aroma.
Peeling: Let the eggplants cool slightly, then peel them carefully, removing all the charred skin so no bitterness remains.

Draining the liquid: Squeeze the flesh well or let it drain in a colander to remove excess liquid. Important: this is the secret to keeping the eggplant dip from turning watery and giving it a thick, creamy texture.

Mixing: Finely chop or mash the flesh with a fork and mix with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp lemon juice, the 3 tbsp olive oil, and salt. Add the olive oil gradually while stirring so it emulsifies and becomes light and fluffy.
Serving: Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with fresh bread or pita. Taste and adjust salt or lemon to preference.
melitzanosalata.plate: In a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, garnish with parsley, serve with bread.

steps: Roasting the pepper: Roast the red Florina pepper under the grill or directly over the flame, turning it until the skin is charred all over, so the flesh cooks through and the skin loosens.
Peeling: Place the charred pepper in a bag or a covered bowl for 10 minutes. Important: the trapped steam loosens the skin so it peels off easily by hand.
Blending the feta: Put the 300g feta, the 100g strained yogurt, and the 2 tbsp olive oil in a blender and blend until it forms a light, creamy paste.
Adding the pepper: Cut the peeled pepper into small pieces and stir it into the mixture. Optionally add a little finely chopped hot pepper for a spicy kick.
Serving: Serve in a small dish, sprinkle with oregano, and drizzle with a little olive oil. Pairs ideally with warm bread or rusks.
htipiti.plate: In a bowl, drizzled with olive oil, garnished with pepper, served with whole-grain bread.

steps: Choosing the ingredients: Let the cheeses come to room temperature so they blend more easily and evenly in the blender.
Blending the cheeses: Put the 200g feta, the 150g anthotyro or katiki cheese, the 3 tbsp olive oil, and the 1 clove of garlic in the blender. Blend until it forms a smooth, creamy paste.
Prepping the peppers: Finely chop the 2-3 hot peppers. Important: remove the seeds and membranes if you want less heat, since that's where most of the capsaicin is concentrated.
Combining: Fold the chopped peppers into the creamy mixture with a spoon (not in the blender), so bits remain and the spicy feta dip keeps some texture.
Adjusting the seasoning: Taste and add salt and pepper if needed, keeping in mind that the feta is already salty.
Resting: Refrigerate the spicy feta dip for at least 30 minutes before serving, so the texture sets and the flavors meld.
tirokafteri.plate: In a bowl, drizzled with olive oil, garnished with hot pepper, served with pita.

steps: Prepping the ingredients: Make sure the 1 egg is at room temperature. Important: a room-temperature egg is the secret to success, since it binds with the oil more easily into a stable emulsion.
Base in the jar: Crack the egg into the tall cup of an immersion blender and add the 1 tbsp lemon juice, the 1 tsp Dijon mustard, salt, and white pepper.
Adding the oil: Pour in all the oil on top — the 200ml sunflower oil and the 50ml olive oil — without stirring. The oil will rise and settle above the egg.

First blend: Place the immersion blender's shaft at the bottom of the cup, right over the egg, and blend on high speed without moving the shaft for about 10 seconds. This is how the emulsion starts to set from the bottom up.
Raising the blender: Very slowly begin raising the shaft, gradually incorporating the oil. You'll see the mayonnaise thicken and set into a white cream.
Adjusting and storing: Taste and adjust the salt and lemon. Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, since it contains raw egg.
mayoneza.plate: In a bowl, a thin drizzle of olive oil on top for presentation.

steps: Melting the butter: Melt the 60g butter in a small saucepan over low heat, so it doesn't burn and turn bitter.
Sautéing the garlic: Add 3 cloves of chopped garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes, just until fragrant. Important: don't let it brown, as burnt garlic turns bitter and ruins the sauce.
Adding the lemon: Add the 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp zest, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, and thyme or oregano. The zest adds intense aroma without extra acidity.
Thickening the sauce: Stir and simmer for 2-3 minutes until it thickens slightly and the flavors come together. The mustard helps emulsify the sauce.
Seasoning: Taste and add salt and pepper as needed, keeping the lemon's acidity in mind.
Finishing and serving: Remove from the heat, add chopped parsley, and pour immediately over the hot chicken. Important: serve it hot, since the heat releases the aromas and brings the dish to life.
saltsa_kotopoulo.wine: Dry white or a light rosé.
saltsa_kotopoulo.plate: Pour over fillet or thigh, garnish with lemon peel and thyme.

steps: Prepping the tomatoes: Grate the 2 ripe tomatoes or chop them very finely. Ripe tomatoes have more sweetness and juice, which forms the base of the dish.

Sautéing the tomato: Sauté the tomato in the 2 tbsp olive oil for 3-4 minutes until the liquid evaporates. Important: the tomato needs to dry out well and reduce into a sauce before you add the eggs — otherwise the dish turns watery and the eggs won't set properly.
Beating the eggs: Beat the 3 eggs with salt and pepper. Light beating incorporates air, giving a fluffier result.

Cooking the eggs: Lower the heat, pour the eggs over the tomato, and stir gently until they set lightly but stay moist. Important: take them off the heat just before they fully dry out, since they continue cooking from the residual heat of the pan.
Serving: Optionally crumble 50g feta on top and serve hot immediately with fresh bread. The feta gives a salty contrast to the tomato's sweetness.

Cutting the potatoes: Peel 3 medium potatoes and cut them into cubes about 1 cm. Even-sized pieces cook at the same rate. If you like, rinse and dry them well to remove excess starch and make them crispier.

Frying the potatoes: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a pan and fry the potatoes over high heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and soft inside. Important: don't stir constantly, so they have time to form a golden crust on the surfaces touching the pan.
