Onion (optional): If you like, add 1 chopped onion and sauté for 2 minutes along with the potatoes until soft and sweet, for extra flavor.
Adding the eggs: Lightly beat 3 eggs with a little salt and pour them over the potatoes, lowering the heat to medium.
Setting: Stir gently until the eggs set but remain moist, without drying out. Important: remove from the heat just before they're completely dry, since they keep cooking from the pan's residual heat.
Serving: Sprinkle with oregano, salt, and pepper, and serve hot immediately with fresh bread.
patates_avga.plate: Straight from the pan, with bread.

steps: Cutting the vegetables: Finely chop the half onion, 1 pepper, and 1 tomato. Even, fine chopping helps them sauté quickly and cook together.
Sautéing: Sauté the vegetables in 2 tbsp olive oil for 3-4 minutes until softened. Important: let the tomato release its liquid so the omelet doesn't turn watery while cooking.
Beating the eggs: Beat the 4 eggs with salt, pepper, and the 30g grated cheese until combined. A little beating incorporates air and makes the omelet fluffier.
Adding the mixture: Pour the beaten eggs into the pan over the vegetables, over medium-low heat. High heat burns the bottom before the top cooks.
Cooking: Cover the pan for 3-4 minutes until the surface sets. The lid traps steam and cooks the omelet from the top as well.
Flipping and serving: If you like, flip the omelet for a few seconds on the other side and serve hot immediately.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the 200g pasta or penne in plenty of salted water, according to the package time, preferably al dente. Well-salted water seasons the pasta itself.
Reserving water: Before draining, reserve about ½ cup of the cooking water. Important: the starchy cooking water is the secret to thickening the sauce and making it creamy without needing any cream.
Draining: Drain the pasta but don't rinse it, so it keeps the starch that helps the butter and cheese cling to it.
Mixing with butter: Return the pasta to the pot, add the 30g butter and a little of the cooking water, and stir vigorously until the butter melts and turns glossy.
Adding the cheese: Gradually add the 50g grated kefalotyri or Parmesan, stirring constantly, so it melts evenly into a smooth cream instead of clumping.
Serving: Serve immediately with plenty of freshly ground pepper and a little extra cheese on top. The dish is best enjoyed hot while the sauce is still creamy.
Cutting: Peel the 4 medium potatoes and cut them into thick slices or cubes, so they stay crispy outside and fluffy inside.
Drying: Important: dry the potatoes very well with paper towels, since moisture causes the oil to spatter and prevents them from crisping.
Frying: Heat plenty of oil over high heat and fry the potatoes for 12-15 minutes, turning them so they brown evenly on all sides.
Draining: Remove them with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Salting and serving: Salt with coarse salt immediately while hot, so the salt sticks, and sprinkle with oregano if you like. Serve immediately.
tiganites_patates.plate: Piping hot, with oregano, alongside tzatziki or ketchup.

steps: Cutting the sausage: Cut the 100g sausage (or apaki) into slices about half a centimeter thick, so they brown evenly.
Frying the sausage: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and fry the slices for 2-3 minutes until browned and their aromatic fat renders out, which will flavor the eggs.
Cracking the eggs: Carefully crack the 4 eggs in next to the sausage. Important: crack each egg into a cup first if you're worried about breaking the yolk, then slide it gently into the pan.
Lowering the heat: Lower the heat so the whites set slowly without burning at the edges while the yolks stay runny.
Cooking: Cook for 2-3 minutes for a runny yolk or 4 minutes for well done. You can cover the pan to set the surface of the whites.
Serving: Sprinkle with salt and pepper at the end and serve immediately with fresh bread for dipping the yolk.
Rinsing the rice: Rinse the 150g rice under running water until it runs clear, to remove excess starch so the grains don't clump together.

Boiling: In a pot, combine the rice with the 300ml water (a 1:2 ratio) and a little salt. Once it comes to a boil, lower the heat and cover. Important: don't lift the lid while it's cooking, so the steam cooks the rice evenly.
Cooking time: Simmer over low heat for 15-18 minutes, until all the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Resting: Remove from the heat and let the rice rest covered for 5 minutes. This resting period makes it fluffy and separates the grains.
Adding the butter: While it's still hot, stir the 20g butter into the rice. The heat of the rice melts the butter and coats it evenly, giving a rich flavor.
Serving: Serve immediately with plenty of the 40g grated cheese or kefalotyri on top, which melts slightly over the hot rice.
ryzi_voutirou.plate: Hot, with extra butter and cheese.

steps: Prepping the bread: Lightly butter one side of each of the 4 bread slices using the 10g butter or margarine. The butter helps the outside turn crispy and golden.

Filling: Divide the 80g gouda or Emmental cheese and the 80g ham between the slices. Important: place cheese both above and below the ham, so that as it melts it seals the sandwich shut and it doesn't fall apart.
Closing the sandwich: Close the sandwich with the buttered side facing out, so it makes contact with the hot surface and browns.
Grilling: Grill in a sandwich press or a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side, until the cheese melts and the bread turns crispy and golden.
Serving: Cut the sandwich diagonally and serve immediately while the cheese is melted and the outside is crispy.
Prepping the potatoes: Cut the 800g potatoes into thick wedges and spread them over the bottom of the roasting pan. The potatoes underneath soak up the chicken's juices and roast up tastier.

Placing the chicken and marinade: Place the 1.5kg chicken pieces over the potatoes. Mix the juice of 2 lemons, 5 tbsp olive oil, 5 cloves of garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper, and pour it over everything. Important: rub it well underneath the chicken skin, so the aromatics reach the meat and not just the surface.
Adding the stock: Pour the 100ml chicken stock into the bottom of the pan. The stock keeps moisture in, prevents the potatoes from drying out, and adds extra flavor to the dish.
Covered roasting: Cover the pan with foil and roast at 180°C for 50 minutes. Covering traps the steam so the chicken cooks through and stays juicy without drying out.

Browning: Remove the foil, raise the temperature to 200°C, and roast for another 25-30 minutes until the skin browns nicely and the potatoes turn crispy. Important: uncovering it at the end is what gives the crispy, golden crust.
Serving: Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before serving, so the juices redistribute through the meat instead of spilling onto the plate.
kotopoulo_fournou.plate: Chicken and lemony potatoes, pan juices spooned over the top.

steps: Soaking the bread: Soak 2 slices of stale bread in a little water and squeeze them out very well. Important: the bread needs to be well squeezed, since excess moisture softens the meat mixture and the soutzoukakia fall apart while frying.

Kneading: In a bowl, combine 500g ground beef, 1 egg, the squeezed bread, 2 cloves of grated garlic, 1 tsp cumin, a little cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Knead vigorously for 5 minutes. Thorough kneading binds the mixture together so it holds its shape.
Resting the mixture: Let the meat mixture rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes so it firms up and the flavors meld, especially the cumin and cinnamon that define Smyrna-style soutzoukakia.
Shaping: Shape into oblong, sausage-like patties, with slightly wet hands so the mixture doesn't stick.
Browning: Fry the soutzoukakia in a little olive oil over medium-high heat until browned all over. They don't need to cook through completely at this stage, since they'll finish cooking in the sauce.
Sauce: In the same pan, add the 400g grated tomato, a little cinnamon, salt, pepper, and a little water. Simmer for 5 minutes to thicken slightly.

Simmering: Return the soutzoukakia to the sauce and simmer for 20 minutes over low heat. Important: slow simmering lets the soutzoukakia soak up the sauce and become soft and juicy. Serve with rice or potatoes.
soutzoukakia.plate: With rice or mashed potatoes, tomato sauce spooned on top.

steps: Room temperature: Take the 2 chops (400g) out of the refrigerator 15 minutes beforehand. Important: meat at room temperature cooks more evenly and doesn't stay cold in the center while burning on the outside.
Seasoning: Pat the chops dry well and rub them with salt, pepper, oregano, thyme, and olive oil on both sides. Dry meat browns better and forms a crust.
Heating the pan: Heat a pan or grill very well over high heat before adding the meat. The high temperature gives a golden crust and seals the juices in.
Cooking: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side. Important: DO NOT move or flip the chops often — let them form a crust before turning, otherwise they won't brown and will stick.
Resting: Remove the chops and let them rest for 3-5 minutes before cutting. This lets the juices redistribute and keeps the meat juicy.
Serving: Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and serve immediately.
Prepping the meat: Cut the 600g pork neck into evenly sized strips and pat them dry with paper towels, so they brown instead of stewing in their own juices.

Browning the pork: Heat the olive oil well and fry the pork over high heat until browned all over, then remove it. Important: cook it in batches over high heat, since overcrowding the pan makes the meat release liquid and stew instead of caramelizing.

Sautéing the vegetables: In the same pan, sauté the onion and the 3 peppers, cut into strips, for about 5 minutes until slightly softened but still holding their color. Add 2 cloves of garlic and sauté for 1 more minute.
Returning the meat and deglazing: Return the pork to the pan and deglaze with the 100ml white wine, scraping the bottom. The wine dissolves the caramelized bits and adds depth to the sauce.
Simmering: Add oregano, salt, and pepper, and simmer for about 10 minutes until the alcohol evaporates and the meat softens as the flavors come together.
Serving: Serve the pork stir-fry hot with fresh bread to mop up the sauce, and a little extra oregano on top.
Browning the meat: Heat olive oil and brown the 800g beef on all sides over high heat, then remove it from the pot. Important: browning locks in the juices and gives the sauce a rich flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: In the same oil, sauté the 2 chopped onions and the 3 cloves of garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Add the 150ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate, scraping the bottom to release the caramelized bits.
Adding the remaining ingredients: Add the 400g grated tomato, the cinnamon stick, the 3 cloves, the 2 bay leaves, and a little water, then return the meat to the pot.
Simmering: Cover and simmer for 75-80 minutes until the meat is fork-tender, adding hot water if needed so it doesn't dry out.
Finishing: Season with salt and pepper at the end, remove the bay leaves and cinnamon stick, and serve with potatoes or pasta.
mosxari_kokkinisto.plate: With pasta or rice, plenty of sauce.

steps: Browning the chicken: Heat olive oil over high heat and brown the 1.5kg chicken pieces on all sides. Important: thorough browning creates a caramelized crust that gives the dish depth of flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: Remove the chicken and sauté the 1 chopped onion and the 2 cloves of garlic in the drippings, until softened and sweet.
Deglazing: Deglaze with 100ml red wine and scrape the bottom of the pot to release the caramelized bits. Let the alcohol evaporate for 1-2 minutes.
Sauce: Add the 400g grated tomato, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper. The warm spices give the dish its traditional character.
Returning the chicken: Return the chicken to the pot and stir to coat it in the sauce on all sides.
Simmering: Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened. Add a little hot water if needed. Serve with rice or potatoes.
kotopoulo_kokkinisto.plate: With hilopites (Greek egg noodles) or rice, kefalotyri cheese.

steps: Bringing to room temperature: Take the 600g lamb chops out of the refrigerator 20 minutes beforehand, so they cook evenly and don't stay cold in the center.

Marinating: Mix the 3 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, oregano, the 2 cloves of garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper, and rub it over the chops. Let them marinate for 15 minutes so the meat absorbs the aromas. Important: don't marinate too long with lemon, as the acid can toughen the meat.
Hot grill: Heat the grill or pan very well over high heat. The high temperature caramelizes the surface and seals the juices in.
Cooking: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, so they stay pink and juicy inside. Lamb chops dry out easily if overcooked.
Resting: Let the chops rest for 5 minutes before serving, so the juices redistribute and they stay tender.
Serving: Sprinkle with fresh oregano and squeeze a little lemon over them just before serving, which brightens the flavor.
paidakia.plate: On the grill, with roast potatoes.

steps: Marinating: Mix the juice of 1 lemon with 4 crushed garlic cloves, oregano, thyme and olive oil. Rub the mixture over the 1.2kg lamb shoulder pieces and let them sit for at least 1 hour, so the flavors penetrate and the meat becomes more tender.
Preparing the vegetables: Cut 4 potatoes, 2 peppers and 2 tomatoes into thick chunks so they hold together during the long roasting time.
Building the parcel: On a large sheet of parchment paper, arrange the lamb, potatoes, peppers, tomatoes, 4 garlic cloves and the 100g kefalotyri. Season with salt and pepper.

Sealing: Close the parchment tightly into a parcel, perhaps with a second layer or foil. Important: a tight seal traps the steam so the meat slow-cooks in its own juices and becomes wonderfully tender.
Slow roasting: Roast at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours. The low temperature and long cooking time make the meat so tender it melts in your mouth.
Browning: In the last 20 minutes, open the parchment on top so the meat browns and any excess liquid evaporates.
Serving: Serve the kleftiko right in the opened parchment with all its juices, so it stays hot and aromatic.
arni_kleftiko.plate: In the parchment, with melted kefalotyri and oregano.

steps: Browning the beef: Pat dry the 800g beef, cut into pieces, and brown on all sides over high heat in olive oil. Set aside. Important: a good sear creates a caramelized crust that gives deep, rich flavor to the finished dish.
Sautéing the onions: In the same pot, sauté the 500g whole pearl onions until golden. Light caramelization sweetens the onions and balances the acidity of the sauce.

Deglazing and spices: Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and the 2 tbsp vinegar, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Add the 400g grated tomato, the 3 garlic cloves, the cinnamon stick, the 4 cloves and the 2 bay leaves. Let the alcohol evaporate so the wine loses its bitterness.
Slow cooking: Return the meat to the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 70-80 minutes over low heat. Slow cooking breaks down the beef's connective tissue and makes it melt in your mouth.

Reducing the sauce: Season with salt and pepper toward the end. Important: if the sauce is too thin, remove the lid for the last 15 minutes so the liquid evaporates and the sauce turns glossy and clings to the meat.
Serving: Serve the stifado hot with the onions whole, alongside hilopites (Greek egg noodles) or mashed potatoes that soak up the sauce beautifully.
mosxari_stifado.plate: With rice or bread, plenty of sauce.

steps: Preparing the okra: Carefully trim the stem ends of the 500g okra without piercing the pods, sprinkle with 2 tbsp vinegar and let sit for 30 minutes. Important: the vinegar removes the okra's sliminess, keeping the pods whole and preventing them from turning the dish mushy.
Browning the beef: In a pot with a little olive oil, brown the 600g cubed beef on all sides over high heat. Caramelization seals in the juices and adds depth of flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: Add 1 finely chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves and sauté until softened, scraping up the caramelized bits from the bottom.

Simmering the meat: Add the 400g grated tomato and a little hot water, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the beef begins to become tender. The meat needs more time to cook than the okra.

Adding the okra: Rinse the vinegar off the okra and lay the pods over the meat. Important: from this point on, don't stir with a spoon — just gently shake the pot, since stirring will break up and mash the okra.
Finishing: Continue cooking for another 25 minutes over low heat (or in the oven), until the okra is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serving: Let the dish rest briefly and serve lukewarm, as bamies and other olive-oil-based dishes taste best not piping hot, with fresh bread and feta.
mosxari_bamies.plate: In a deep plate, okra on top, with bread.

steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the 600g chicken breast into strips and season with salt and pepper. Even strips cook quickly and evenly.

Browning the chicken: Brown the chicken in part of the 30g butter for 4-5 minutes per side, then remove. Important: don't overcrowd the pan, or the chicken will steam instead of browning — cook in batches if needed.
Sautéing the mushrooms: In the same pan, sauté the 400g mushrooms over high heat until browned and their moisture has evaporated. This develops flavor and keeps the sauce from becoming watery.
Aromatics: Add 1 finely chopped onion, 2 garlic cloves and thyme, and sauté until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the 100ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate, scraping up the bottom of the pan. The caramelized bits left behind add depth to the sauce.

Finishing the sauce: Pour in the 200ml cream, return the chicken to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Important: keep the heat low after adding the cream, as a hard boil can cause it to split.
Serving: Taste, adjust salt and pepper, and serve hot.
kotopoulo_manitaria.plate: With rice or mashed potatoes, mushrooms on top.

steps: Preparing the meat: Cut the 700g pork shoulder into evenly sized cubes and pat dry, so they brown properly when seared.
Browning and sautéing: Heat olive oil and brown the cubes on all sides over high heat to seal in the juices. Add the onion and 2 garlic cloves and sauté for 3 minutes.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the 150ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate. The wine adds aromatic acidity and depth to the sauce.
Adding the tomato: Add the 200g grated tomato, 2 bay leaves, salt and pepper, and simmer for about 25 minutes until the meat starts to become tender.
Adding the leeks: Slice the 4 leeks into rounds and add them to the pot. Important: the leeks go in later so they don't dissolve completely and keep their texture on the plate.
Finishing: Simmer for about another 15 minutes until the leeks soften and the meat becomes tender and glazed. Remove the bay leaves, taste for salt and serve hot.
Frying the sausages: Slice the 300g country-style sausages into rounds and fry in a little olive oil until browned all over, then remove. This renders their fat and flavors the oil.
Sautéing the vegetables: In the same pan, sauté the 3 peppers cut into strips, the finely chopped onion and the 2 garlic cloves for about 5 minutes until softened.
Adding the tomato: Add the 200g grated tomato, oregano, salt and pepper, and let the sauce thicken.
Combining: Return the sausages to the pan. Important: add them back toward the end so they don't toughen from prolonged cooking.
Simmering: Simmer for 10 minutes until the flavors meld and the sauce thickens.
Serving: Serve immediately while hot, ideally with fresh bread to mop up the sauce.
loukanka_piperies.plate: With bread or rice, oregano on top.

steps: Marinating: In a bowl, mix the 3 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, the 3 crushed garlic cloves, the 1 tbsp mustard, oregano, thyme and salt. Rub the mixture thoroughly over the 1.2kg ribs and let marinate for 30 minutes. Important: the lemon's acidity and the mustard tenderize the meat and flavor it deeply.
Preheating the grill: Heat the grill or grill pan well over medium-high heat before adding the meat, so it sears immediately and develops nice grill marks.
Cooking the first side: Grill the ribs for 8-10 minutes on one side without moving them repeatedly, so they brown properly.
Cooking the second side: Turn and grill for another 8-10 minutes until cooked through and juicy with a crispy exterior.
Resting: Let the ribs rest for 5 minutes before serving. Important: resting allows the juices to redistribute, so the meat doesn't dry out when cut.
Serving: Serve with fresh lemon and lemon potatoes for a complete traditional dish.
xoirina_paidakia.plate: With fried potatoes, lemon and mustard.

steps: Browning the chicken: In a pot with olive oil, brown the 1kg chicken pieces on all sides over high heat. Browning seals in the juices and adds depth to the sauce.
Aromatics: Add the 2 finely chopped onions and the 3 garlic cloves and sauté until softened. Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate, leaving behind a rich aroma.

Spices and tomato: Add the 400g grated tomato, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, salt and pepper. Important: the sweet spices (cinnamon, cloves, allspice) are the signature note of Corfiot pastitsada — don't leave them out.
Slow cooking: Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 60-70 minutes, until the chicken is very tender and the sauce reduces to a thick, rich red sauce.
Cooking the pasta: Boil the 500g shell pasta in salted water until al dente, so it stays slightly firm and doesn't turn mushy when mixed with the sauce.
Serving: Serve the pasta with the rich sauce and chicken pieces, sprinkled generously with grated kefalograviera cheese.
pastitsada.plate: Classic Corfiot style. With kefalograviera or Parmesan.

steps: Cleaning the mussels: Thoroughly clean the 1kg mussels, scrubbing the shells and removing the beards. Important: discard any mussels that are open and don't close when tapped, as they are not fresh.
Opening the mussels: In a covered pot with a little water, cook the mussels over high heat for 3-4 minutes until they open. Discard any that don't open, as they aren't safe to eat.
Preparing the sauce: In a pan with olive oil, sauté 2 garlic cloves, then add the 200g grated tomato and a little finely chopped hot pepper.
Deglazing with ouzo: Add the 3 tbsp ouzo and let the alcohol evaporate, leaving behind only the anise aroma that pairs so well with seafood.
Simmering the sauce: Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly and the flavors meld.
Combining: Add the mussels to the sauce and stir gently to coat them, adding a little of their liquid for extra flavor.
Finishing and serving: Grate the 80g feta over the top and sprinkle with parsley. Serve immediately while piping hot, so the mussels stay juicy.
mydia_saganaki.plate: Deep plate or saganaki pan, with fresh bread.

steps: Cleaning the cuttlefish: Clean the 800g cuttlefish, removing the bone and innards, and cut into pieces. If you like, save the ink for a darker, more flavorful version. Pat dry thoroughly before frying.

Frying the cuttlefish: Fry the cuttlefish over high heat for 2-3 minutes. Important: they will initially release liquid — let it evaporate, otherwise the cuttlefish will boil instead of searing and turn out bland.
Aromatic base: Add the 1 finely chopped onion and the 2 garlic cloves and sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Deglaze with the 150ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate.

Sauce and slow simmering: Add the 200g grated tomato, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 30-35 minutes until the cuttlefish becomes completely tender. Important: cuttlefish needs patience — either a very brief sear or a long slow simmer, because anything in between leaves it tough and rubbery.
Spinach and finishing: If using the 200g spinach, add it in the last 5 minutes so it wilts while keeping its color and nutrients. Finish with chopped dill for freshness and serve hot.
soupies.plate: With rice or fresh bread, dill.

steps: Cleaning: Clean the 500g fresh sardines, removing the innards and, if you like, the heads, and rinse very well under cold water. Important: dry them very thoroughly with paper towels, since moisture prevents browning and causes the oil to spatter in the pan.
Salting: Salt the sardines just before cooking. Salting too early draws out their moisture and dries them out.
Flouring (optional): For a crispier crust, dust them lightly with flour and shake off the excess, so they don't pick up too much flour and become heavy.
Cooking: Cook on a hot grill or in a pan with 3 tbsp olive oil for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and the flesh turns opaque. Avoid turning them repeatedly so they don't fall apart.
Lemon-oil dressing: Mix the juice of 2 lemons with a little olive oil and oregano for a fresh dressing that cuts through the fish's richness.
Serving: Serve immediately while hot, drizzled with the lemon-oil dressing, oregano and coarse salt.
sardeles_lemonates.plate: With lemon, olives and fresh bread. The essence of Greek summer.

steps: Cutting the octopus: Cut the 1kg octopus into bite-sized pieces. No water is needed for cooking, as the octopus will release its own liquid.

Sautéing: Sauté the octopus with 1 onion in 3 tbsp olive oil for about 5 minutes until it releases its liquid and browns lightly. Important: let the octopus cook in its own juices before adding other ingredients, as this tenderizes it naturally.
Deglazing: Deglaze with the 200ml red wine and the 2 tbsp vinegar and let the alcohol evaporate. The vinegar tenderizes the octopus and balances the flavor.

Adding tomato and spices: Add the 400g grated tomato, cinnamon, allspice and bay leaf. The warm spices give the dish its characteristic 'krasato' (wine-braised) character. Be careful with the salt, as the octopus is already salty.

Slow cooking: Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 60-70 minutes until the octopus becomes tender and the sauce thickens. Important: if it dries out too soon, add a little hot water — octopus needs time to become tender.
Serving: Remove the bay leaf, let it rest briefly and serve with bread or hilopites.
htapodi_krasato.plate: With hilopites or bread to soak up the sauce.

steps: Preparing the fish: Clean the 2 mackerel and score them diagonally in 2-3 places on each side. The scoring helps the fish cook evenly and lets the aromatics penetrate the flesh.
Salting and aromatics: Sprinkle salt, pepper and oregano inside and out, and tuck finely chopped garlic into the slits. This way the aroma reaches the whole flesh, not just the surface.
Oiling: Drizzle the mackerel with olive oil so they don't stick to the grill and develop a nice crispy skin.

Grilling: Grill on a well-heated grill or barbecue for 6-8 minutes per side. Important: turn the fish only once, and only when it releases easily on its own, otherwise the skin will tear and the flesh will fall apart.
Finishing: Once cooked, drizzle with fresh lemon juice and sprinkle with chopped parsley. The lemon balances the mackerel's richness.
Serving: Serve the mackerel immediately while hot and juicy, ideally with a village salad or boiled greens.
kolios.plate: With boiled potatoes or skordalia (garlic dip).

steps: Cleaning: Trim the ends and any strings from the 700g fresh green beans and wash them well.
Sautéing: Heat the 4 tbsp olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion and the 2 garlic cloves for 3 minutes until softened and sweetened.
Adding the rest: Add the 300g grated tomato, the 2 potatoes cut into cubes, salt, pepper, parsley and a little water, then add the green beans.
Simmering: Cover and cook over medium heat for 35-40 minutes until the green beans become tender. Important: don't stir constantly so they don't fall apart — gently shake the pot if needed.
Finishing: Drizzle in a little extra olive oil at the end of cooking for a richer flavor typical of ladera (olive-oil-based) dishes.
Serving: Let it rest briefly before serving, as ladera dishes taste best lukewarm. Best served with feta and bread.
fasolakia.plate: Deep plate, raw olive oil drizzled on top, feta on the side.

steps: Cutting the potatoes: Peel the 1kg potatoes and cut into thick wedges of equal size, so they cook evenly. Arrange them in a single layer in a baking pan.
Preparing the marinade: In a bowl, mix the 5 tbsp olive oil, the juice of 2 lemons, the 4 garlic cloves, oregano, salt, pepper and the 150ml stock or water.
Pouring over: Pour the marinade over the potatoes and toss to coat them all over. Important: the liquid should reach about halfway up the potatoes so they cook without drying out.
Roasting: Roast at 180°C for 60-65 minutes. The lemon gives the dish its characteristic bright flavor and the garlic perfumes the dish.
Turning: Halfway through roasting, turn the potatoes once so they brown on both sides.
Finishing: Roast until golden outside, soft inside, and having absorbed almost all the liquid, leaving a thick lemony sauce at the bottom.
patates_lemonates.plate: Pan served straight to the table, with feta and olives.

steps: Cleaning the okra: Clean the 750g okra by carefully trimming the conical stem without opening the pod. Important: if you cut too deep, the okra will open up and become slimy during cooking.
Vinegar and sun: Sprinkle the okra with 1 tbsp vinegar and let sit in the sun for 30 minutes. The vinegar reduces the sliminess and helps them stay firm during cooking.
Sautéing the onion: In a pot or baking pan, heat the 4 tbsp olive oil and sauté the 1 finely chopped onion until softened and translucent.
Adding the okra: Add the okra on top of the onion without stirring, so the pods don't break and keep their shape.
Tomato and seasoning: Add the 400g grated tomato, half a teaspoon of sugar, salt and pepper. The sugar balances the tomato's acidity.
Slow cooking: Simmer over low heat for 40 minutes without stirring, only gently shaking the pot, so the okra doesn't fall apart. Serve lukewarm with fresh bread.
Sautéing the onions: In a pot with 4 tbsp olive oil, sauté the 2 finely chopped onions over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until softened and translucent, so they sweeten and build a flavor base.
Adding the vegetables: Add the 2 carrots cut into rounds and the 750g peas and stir for 2-3 minutes to coat them in the oil.
Adding the tomato: Add the 3 grated tomatoes, salt, pepper and 100ml water. Stir gently. Important: stir gently so the peas don't fall apart and keep their shape.
Slow cooking: Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes until the peas become tender and the liquid reduces into an olive-oil-rich sauce.
Checking the liquid: If it dries out too soon, add a little hot water. The dish should stay juicy but not watery.
Finishing: At the end, add plenty of chopped fresh dill and stir, so it keeps its fresh aroma.
Serving: Let the peas rest for 10 minutes off the heat and serve lukewarm with feta and bread, as ladera dishes taste best not piping hot.
arakas_laderos.plate: With white bread and feta. A classic Greek olive-oil dish.

steps: Preparing the eggplants: Slice the 4 long eggplants lengthwise without cutting all the way through, to create a pocket for the filling. Fry lightly in olive oil until softened and arrange them open in a baking pan.
Draining the oil: Important: after frying, lay the eggplants on paper towels to drain off the excess oil. Eggplants soak up a lot of oil, and if not drained, the dish turns out heavy and greasy.

Filling: In a pan, sauté the 3 finely chopped onions and the 4 garlic cloves until softened, then add the 4 grated tomatoes, chopped parsley, salt, pepper and olive oil. Simmer for 10 minutes until the filling thickens.
Sweetening the tomato: Add the 1 tsp sugar to the sauce. The sugar balances the tomato's acidity and brings out the natural sweetness of the onions, which is characteristic of imam baildi.
Filling and baking: Fill the eggplants with the mixture and spoon a little extra tomato on top. Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until completely soft and the juices caramelize.
Serving: Let the imam baildi rest and serve cold or lukewarm — this dish improves in flavor as it rests, as the aromas of the olive oil and onions meld together.
imam_baialdi.plate: Cold or warm, with bread on the side.

steps: Cutting: Wash the 4 zucchini and slice into rounds about 0.5cm thick. Even thickness ensures even frying and crispiness.

Salting and drying: Salt the slices and let sit for 10 minutes to release their liquid, then pat them very dry with paper towels. Important: if they aren't dried, the water will make the oil spatter and the zucchini will turn out soft instead of crispy.
Flouring: Dredge the slices in flour mixed with salt and pepper and shake off the excess. Too much flour makes for a heavy, floury taste and clouds the oil.

Oil temperature: Heat plenty of olive oil over high heat. The oil is ready when a slice dropped in immediately releases bubbles. Important: if the oil isn't hot enough, the zucchini will soak up oil and won't turn crispy.
Frying: Fry in batches for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden, without overcrowding the pan so the temperature doesn't drop.
Draining and serving: Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil and serve immediately, ideally with tzatziki or a little feta.

Preparing the mushrooms: Clean the 400g mushrooms with a damp cloth (not by rinsing in water) and leave them whole or halved. Important: mushrooms soak up water, so don't submerge them, or they'll become soggy and won't brown.

Browning: Brown the mushrooms in 2 tbsp olive oil over high heat without stirring too much, so their moisture evaporates and they caramelize. Frequent stirring lowers the temperature and causes them to boil instead.
Aromatics and deglazing: Add 2 garlic cloves and deglaze with 50ml white wine. Let the alcohol evaporate. Sprinkle with thyme, salt and pepper.
Adding the feta: Place 80g feta in pieces over the mushrooms. The feta adds a salty, creamy flavor that ties the dish together.
Melting the feta: Cover the pan for 2-3 minutes until the feta softens and starts to melt. Be careful with the salt, since the feta is already salty.
Serving: Serve immediately while hot as a meze, ideally with fresh bread to mop up the sauce.

Bolognese sauce: Sauté the onion and 2 garlic cloves, add the 500g ground beef and brown well. Deglaze with the 100ml red wine, add the 400g grated tomato and a little cinnamon, and simmer gently for 25 minutes until the sauce thickens.

Making the béchamel: Melt the 70g butter, add the 4 tbsp flour and stir for 1-2 minutes. Gradually add the 800ml milk, whisking constantly so it doesn't form lumps, until it thickens into a velvety cream.
Preparing the sheets: If the lasagna sheets need pre-boiling, follow the package instructions. Otherwise, make sure the sauce is juicy enough for the sheets to soften in the oven.

Layering: In a greased baking dish, spread a little béchamel on the bottom, then lasagna sheets, bolognese and cheese. Repeat the layers about 3 times. IMPORTANT: a little béchamel on the bottom keeps the sheets from sticking and burning.
Final layer: Finish with béchamel and plenty of grated kefalotyri, so a golden, crispy crust forms during baking.
Baking and resting: Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until the top is golden. Let the lasagna cool for 15 minutes before cutting, so the layers set and don't fall apart.
lazania.plate: Square portions, grated cheese on top.

steps: Soffritto: Finely chop the onion, carrot and celery stalk and sauté in olive oil for 5 minutes until softened. IMPORTANT: this aromatic base (soffritto) is the foundation of the bolognese's flavor.
Adding garlic and meat: Add the 2 garlic cloves for 1 minute, then the 400g ground beef, stirring until browned and its liquid has evaporated.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the 100ml red wine and let the alcohol evaporate, scraping the bottom of the pan to release the flavors.
Sauce: Add the 400g grated tomato, the 50ml milk, salt and pepper. The milk rounds out the tomato's acidity and makes the sauce more velvety.
Simmering: Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, so the sauce thickens and the flavors concentrate.
Cooking the pasta and serving: Boil the 320g spaghetti al dente, toss with the sauce and serve topped with grated parmesan.
spaghetti_bolognese.plate: Nest of spaghetti, sauce in the center, parmesan.

steps: Cooking the pasta: Bring salted water to a boil and start cooking the 200g spaghetti. IMPORTANT: reserve a cup of the pasta cooking water, as its starch will later help the sauce cling to the pasta.
Aromatic base: Sauté the 3 garlic cloves, the chili pepper and the 4 anchovies in olive oil for 2 minutes, stirring until the anchovies melt and release their umami note.
Adding the sauce: Add the 400g grated tomato, the 80g Kalamata olives and the 2 tbsp capers. These salty ingredients give puttanesca its bold character.
Simmering: Simmer the sauce for 12-15 minutes until it reduces and thickens. Taste before salting, as the anchovies, olives and capers are already salty.
Combining: Drain the spaghetti just shy of al dente and add it to the sauce along with a little pasta water. Toss over high heat for 1-2 minutes to coat.
Serving: Remove from the heat, add fresh basil or parsley and a raw tablespoon of olive oil for shine and aroma. Serve immediately.
spaghetti_poutanesca.plate: Deep plate, olives and basil on top.

steps: Browning the chicken: In a pot with olive oil, brown the 800g chicken pieces on all sides and set aside. Browning gives the dish color and depth of flavor.
Sautéing the aromatics: In the same fat, sauté the finely chopped onion and the 2 garlic cloves until softened. Deglaze with the 100ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate.
Sauce and spices: Add the 400g grated tomato, cinnamon, allspice, salt, pepper and 400ml water. Return the chicken to the pot and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Adding the orzo: Add the 300g kritharaki to the sauce and stir. IMPORTANT: make sure there's enough liquid, as the orzo absorbs a lot of water — top up with hot water if needed.
Cooking the orzo: Continue cooking for 15-18 minutes, stirring regularly so the orzo doesn't stick to the bottom and cooks evenly.
Resting and serving: Remove from the heat and let stand for 5 minutes so the moisture settles. Serve topped with plenty of grated kefalotyri.
Sautéing the garlic: In a pan with extra virgin olive oil, sauté 2 finely chopped garlic cloves for 1 minute. IMPORTANT: don't let it brown, as it turns bitter and spoils the sauce.
Tomato sauce: Add 200g grated tomato, salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes until it thickens slightly and sweetens.
Adding the tuna: Add the 160g well-drained tuna, the Kalamata olives and 1 tbsp capers. Stir gently so the tuna doesn't break down into flakes.
Cooking the pasta: Boil the 200g farfalle in salted water until slightly firm (al dente), reserving a little of the cooking water.
Bringing the dish together: Transfer the farfalle to the sauce with a little pasta water and stir, so the starchy water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.
Finishing and serving: Off the heat, add fresh basil and a little raw olive oil for freshness and aroma, and serve immediately.
farfale_tonos.plate: Deep plate, basil and olive oil.

steps: Cutting the zucchini: Cut the 3 zucchini (400g) into rounds or small cubes. Pat them lightly dry so they brown rather than steam in the pan.

Browning the zucchini: Brown the zucchini in 20g butter for 5-6 minutes until golden. IMPORTANT: don't stir constantly — let them sit in the hot butter to caramelize, which gives the sauce sweetness and depth.
Garlic: Add the 2 finely chopped garlic cloves and sauté for just 1 minute until fragrant — no longer, as garlic burns easily in butter and turns bitter.
Creamy sauce: Add the 150ml heavy cream, salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. The cream coats the zucchini and creates a velvety texture.
Cooking the pasta: Boil the 200g penne al dente, meaning slightly firm. IMPORTANT: reserve a little pasta water — its starch helps the sauce cling to the penne and makes them tastier.
Combining and serving: Add the penne to the sauce with a little pasta water and stir over low heat until combined. Add the 50g parmesan and fresh basil or mint, and serve immediately.

Cooking the rice: Put the 100g rice with 200ml water in a pot and simmer gently for 10 minutes, until it has absorbed almost all the water and softened slightly. Pre-cooking in water helps the rice cook evenly before the milk goes in.
Heating the milk: Separately warm 1 liter of milk together with the 80g sugar and 1 vanilla, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Warm milk prevents thermal shock to the rice.
Combining: Add the warm milk to the rice and lower the heat. IMPORTANT: stir almost constantly so it doesn't stick to the bottom and scorch, which would give the whole rice pudding a burnt taste.
Thickening: Continue simmering for 20-25 minutes, stirring, until it thickens into a creamy texture. IMPORTANT: keep it looser than you want it, as it firms up considerably as it cools.
Portioning: Pour into individual bowls while still hot and fluid, so the surface settles smoothly.
Cooling and serving: Let it cool and set at room temperature, then in the refrigerator. Sprinkle with cinnamon just before serving.
ryzosgalo.plate: Small bowls, plenty of cinnamon on top.

steps: Heating the milk: Warm the 1 liter of milk in a pot without letting it boil. Warm milk helps the semolina incorporate without forming lumps.

Semolina custard: Gradually add the 150g semolina together with the 200g sugar, stirring constantly for 10 minutes until the custard thickens. IMPORTANT: whisk continuously so it doesn't form lumps or stick to the bottom.

Adding the eggs: Remove from the heat, let it cool slightly, then add the 4 eggs beaten with the vanilla, stirring quickly. IMPORTANT: the custard must not be scalding hot when you add the eggs, or they will cook and curdle it.
Layering the bottom sheets: Butter the baking dish and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with melted butter (from the 200g). The butter on each sheet makes the pastry crisp.
Filling and closing: Spread the custard evenly, cover with the remaining buttered sheets and score the surface into portions.
Baking: Bake at 175°C for 50 minutes until golden and crisp.

Syruping: Prepare the syrup by boiling 300g sugar with 200ml water and lemon, then let it cool. IMPORTANT: always pour cold syrup over a hot dessert (or the reverse) — the temperature difference makes the galaktoboureko absorb the syrup while staying crisp instead of soggy.
galaktoboureko.plate: At room temperature, well soaked with syrup.

steps: Preparing the filling: Mix the 300g ground walnuts with the 100g almonds, cinnamon and ground cloves. The spices give baklava its characteristic aromatic depth.

Layering the sheets: Butter 5-6 phyllo sheets one by one with melted butter and layer them on the bottom of the baking dish, then spread the filling. IMPORTANT: butter each sheet well so they turn crisp and don't stick together.
Layering: Continue alternating layers of buttered sheets and filling, keeping enough sheets for a rich top layer.
Scoring: Score the baklava diagonally into diamonds before baking. Scoring before baking is done while the sheets are still soft, so they don't shatter afterward and the syrup can soak in everywhere.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for 45-50 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. The low temperature bakes the sheets evenly without burning.
Making the syrup: Boil the 300g sugar with the 200ml water and the 3 tbsp honey for a few minutes until the syrup thickens slightly.
Syruping: Pour hot syrup over cold baklava, or cold syrup over hot baklava. IMPORTANT: never both at the same temperature, or the baklava will turn soggy and lose its crispness.
Resting: Let the baklava absorb the syrup for at least 2 hours before cutting and serving, so it soaks evenly through every layer.

Caramel: Put the 150g sugar with the 2 tbsp water in a pot and heat without stirring until it turns a red-brown color. IMPORTANT: don't stir the caramel with a spoon, as it will crystallize — just swirl the pot gently.
Lining the molds: As soon as the caramel is ready, quickly divide it among the molds before it sets, coating the bottom of each.
Custard mixture: Beat the 4 eggs with the 120g sugar and slowly pour in the warm milk (600ml) while stirring, so the eggs don't cook. Add vanilla.
Straining: Strain the mixture and divide it among the caramel-lined molds, so the custard comes out perfectly smooth without any egg clumps.
Baking in a bain-marie: Place the molds in a pan with hot water (bain-marie) and bake at 160°C for 45-50 minutes. The bain-marie ensures gentle, even baking without curdling the custard.
Chilling and unmolding: Refrigerate for 4 hours or more to set, then invert the mold onto a plate so the caramel runs over the top.
Beating the liquids: Beat the 150ml olive oil with the 100g sugar until well combined. Add the 120ml orange juice, the cinnamon and cloves, which give the festive aroma.

Adding the flour: Sift the 500g flour together with 1 tsp baking soda and gradually combine it with the liquids. IMPORTANT: knead lightly, only as much as needed to bring the dough together, since over-kneading toughens the melomakarona.
Shaping: Shape oval cookies of even size and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them as they'll puff up slightly.
Piercing: Lightly prick each cookie with a fork, so they bake evenly through and absorb the syrup better later.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden and firm. They need to be well baked so they don't turn mushy in the syrup.
Making the syrup: Boil the 200g honey with the 200ml water (1:1 ratio) for a few minutes to make a thin honey syrup.
Syruping: IMPORTANT: dip the warm melomakarona into the syrup (or hot syrup over cold cookies), 1-2 times. The temperature contrast helps them absorb the syrup without falling apart.
Finishing: Drain them and sprinkle with ground walnuts and cinnamon on top. Let them stand a few hours to fully absorb the syrup.
melomakarona.plate: On a platter, sprinkled with walnuts and cinnamon.

steps: Beating the butter: With the 250g clarified butter at room temperature, beat in the mixer for about 15 minutes until it turns pale and fluffy like a cream. The long beating incorporates air and gives the kourabiedes their light texture.
Adding the liquids: Add the 1 egg yolk, the vanilla and the 100g powdered sugar and keep beating until combined.
Toasting the almonds: If not already toasted, lightly toast the 100g almonds and chop them into small pieces. Toasting makes them crunchy and aromatic.

Kneading: Sift the 500g flour and fold it in gradually together with the almonds, kneading lightly. IMPORTANT: don't overknead and don't let the dough warm from your hands, as this melts the butter and toughens the kourabiedes.
Shaping: Shape into half-moons or stars and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving gaps between them as they puff up slightly.
Baking: Bake at 170°C for 18-22 minutes, until set without taking on much color — kourabiedes should stay pale.
Finishing: While still warm, generously dust them with the 200g powdered sugar. The warm surface makes the sugar stick and form the characteristic white coating.
kourabiedes.plate: On a platter, dusted all over like snow with powdered sugar.

steps: Preparing the eggplant: Cut the eggplants in half lengthwise and salt them. Let them "sweat" for 20 minutes — the salt draws out the bitterness. Rinse, dry, and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until softened.
Scooping out: Once slightly cooled, scoop out the flesh, leaving a 1cm border all around. The scooped-out flesh will go into the meat mixture for flavor.

Meat sauce: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes. Raise the heat, add the ground beef and brown for 8 minutes. Add the finely chopped eggplant flesh, tomato, cinnamon, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until it thickens.
Béchamel: Melt the butter, add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually add the milk, whisking. Cook until it thickens. Remove from the heat, add nutmeg and 2/3 of the cheese.
Filling: Fill the hollowed-out eggplants with the meat mixture. Cover each eggplant with béchamel and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the béchamel turns golden. IMPORTANT: let it set for 5 minutes before serving.
papoutsakia.plate: One or two eggplant halves per plate.

steps: Blanching the cabbage: Remove the core from the base and submerge the whole cabbage in boiling water for 3-4 minutes. Peel off the leaves one by one as they soften. You'll need 18-20 large leaves — pliable enough to roll without tearing.
Filling: Mix the ground beef, rice (raw), onion, parsley, mint, eggs, salt and pepper. IMPORTANT: the rice goes in raw, as it will cook inside the rolls, absorbing their juices.
Rolling: Place 1-2 tbsp of filling at the base of each leaf, fold in the sides and roll tightly like a log. Arrange them in layers in the pot with the seam facing down.
Simmering: Cover the rolls with any leftover cabbage leaves. Add stock or water until they're covered. Place a weight on top (e.g. a plate) so they don't unroll. Simmer covered for 60-70 minutes.

Egg-lemon sauce (avgolemono): Beat the eggs, add lemon juice and gradually whisk in hot broth from the pot (tempering). Pour back into the pot and swirl in circular motions — do not let it boil afterward.
Serving: Serve hot with plenty of avgolemono sauce.
lahanodomades.plate: In a deep plate with avgolemono sauce.

steps: Marinade: Mix the olive oil, lemon, grated garlic, oregano, thyme and paprika. Score the thighs with a knife so the marinade penetrates deeply.
Marinating: Coat the thighs with the marinade and let them sit at least 1 hour in the refrigerator — ideally overnight. IMPORTANT: salt only 30 minutes before grilling so the meat doesn't dry out.
Preheating: Preheat the grill or griddle to a high temperature. Clean it and brush with oil so the chicken doesn't stick.
Grilling: Grill the thighs over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes per side. Start skin-side down ("butterflied") for crispy skin.
Checking doneness: Use a meat thermometer — 75°C internal, or the juices should run clear. IMPORTANT: don't cut into it to check, as you'll lose the juices.
Resting: Let it rest for 5 minutes covered with foil before serving so the juices redistribute.
kotopoulo_sxara.plate: With lemon, oregano and lemon potatoes.

steps: Cutting: Cut the breast into 2.5cm cubes. Even size means even cooking.
Marinade: Mix olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, paprika and yogurt. The yogurt tenderizes the meat and helps keep it juicy.
Marinating: Let the cubes sit in the marinade for at least 30 minutes (2-3 hours is better). IMPORTANT: salt only lightly, just before grilling.
Skewering: Thread 5-6 cubes onto each skewer without packing them too tightly.
Grilling: Grill over a very hot grill for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes for even browning. Chicken breast cooks fast — don't overcook it.
Serving: Serve in pita or on a plate with tzatziki, tomato and onion.
Browning the chicken: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper and brown them on all sides in hot oil, 3-4 minutes per side. Browning seals in the juices and adds depth of flavor.
Sautéing: Remove the chicken, sauté the onion and garlic in the same oil for 5 minutes.
Sauce: Add the tomato, cinnamon, allspice and salt. Return the chicken to the pot. Simmer covered for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Adding the rice: Remove the chicken, measure the liquid in the pot and add stock so you have 3 cups total. Add the rice and stir.
Cooking the rice: Simmer covered for 18 minutes over low heat. IMPORTANT: do not stir while it cooks.
Serving: Place the chicken on top of the rice, cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
kotopoulo_rizi.plate: Rice as the base with chicken on top.

steps: Preparation: Take the steaks out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking so they come to room temperature — otherwise the outside cooks before the inside is done.
Drying and salting: Pat them very dry with paper towels. Salt and pepper right before cooking.
Hot pan: Heat a cast iron or heavy pan over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Add a little oil.
Searing: Sear the steaks for 2-3 minutes per side for medium rare (54-57°C internal). IMPORTANT: don't keep moving them — let a crust form.
Basting: Add butter, garlic and herbs to the pan. Tilt the pan and continuously spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 1 minute.
Resting: IMPORTANT: let the steaks rest on a board for 5-8 minutes, covered with foil. The juices redistribute and the steak stays succulent.
brizoles_mosxari.plate: Sliced on the bias against the grain.

steps: Cleaning: Score the sea bass 2-3 times on each side. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Filling: Fill the cavity with sliced lemon, garlic, parsley and thyme — they flavor the fish from within as it bakes.
Baking dish: Line the baking dish with tomato slices (the base) and place the sea bass on top. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes. IMPORTANT: the fish is done when the flesh flakes easily with a fork and has lost its translucency.
Serving: Remove the backbone and serve the fillets with the vegetables and sauce from the pan.
lavraki_fournou.plate: Whole in the baking dish, or as fillets.

steps: Preparation: Wash the marides and dry them very well. Dry fish = crispy result, wet fish = pale result.
Flouring: Salt the flour and coat the marides in a bag or sieve. Shake off the excess flour — a thin coating = crispy, a thick one = soggy.

Frying: Heat the oil to 180°C (if you dip in a fish, it should sizzle immediately). Fry in small batches for 2-3 minutes until golden. IMPORTANT: don't add too many at once — it drops the temperature and they turn out oily.
Draining: Remove with a slotted spoon onto paper towels to absorb the oil.
Serving: Serve immediately with lemon wedges — marides quickly lose their crispness.
Boiling: Put the octopus in a pot without water and simmer it in its own juices, covered, over low heat for 40-50 minutes. It becomes perfectly tender without turning tough.
Cooling: Let it cool in its own juices — if you remove it right away and grill it, it will contract and toughen.
Marinade: Mix olive oil, vinegar, and oregano. Coat the octopus and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Grilling: Grill over very high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until it develops distinctive charred lines and color.
Serving: Cut into pieces and drizzle with lemon, olive oil, and oregano. Important: serve immediately.
htapodi_sxara.plate: On a cutting board with lemon and oregano.

steps: Prep: Rinse the shrimp and pat them dry. Remove the vein if you like (the dark line along the back) — it doesn't affect flavor, only appearance.
Marinade: Mix olive oil, finely chopped garlic, lemon, and red pepper flakes. Marinate for 15-30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Grilling: Grill the shrimp over very high heat for 2-3 minutes per side until they turn pink and get grill marks. Important: don't overcook them — they become rubbery.
Serving: Serve immediately with fresh parsley and lemon. You can leave the shells on for a juicier result.
garides_sxara.plate: On a warm plate with lemon.

steps: Cleaning: Separate the body from the tentacles. Remove the transparent quill and rinse well. Finely chop the tentacles for the filling.
Filling: Sauté the onion for 5 minutes, add the tentacles and brown for 3 minutes. Add the rice (raw), tomato, parsley, wine, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Stuffing the squid: Fill each body about two-thirds full — the rice will expand. Seal with a toothpick.

Cooking: Heat oil in a wide pan and brown the stuffed squid for 2 minutes. Add tomato and a little water. Simmer covered for 35-40 minutes. Important: keep the heat low, as squid becomes tough over high heat.
Serving: Remove the toothpicks and serve with the sauce.
Cleaning the cuttlefish: Cut into strips. Wash well to remove the ink (if you don't want a dark sauce).
Sautéing: Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes. Add the cuttlefish and sauté over high heat for 5 minutes.
Deglazing: Deglaze with wine and let it evaporate for 2 minutes.
Simmering: Add a little water and season with salt and pepper. Simmer covered for 30-35 minutes until the cuttlefish is tender.
Spinach: Add the spinach (fresh or frozen) and dill. Cook for another 5-10 minutes until wilted. Important: don't overcook the spinach — it loses color and nutrients.
soupies_spanaki.plate: In a deep plate with bread.

steps: Squeezing the zucchini: Grate the zucchini on the coarse side, salt generously, and let sit for 15 minutes. Then squeeze firmly by hand or in a cloth. Important: if moisture remains, the fritters will fall apart.
Mixing: Combine the zucchini, grated feta, egg, mint, parsley, and pepper. Add flour gradually until the mixture holds together.
Shaping: Form small round or oval patties.
Frying: Fry in medium-hot oil for 3-4 minutes per side until golden.
Serving: Drain on paper towels. Serve with yogurt or tzatziki.
Pureeing: Pulse the chickpeas with onion and garlic in a food processor or mash with a fork. You don't want a smooth paste — leave small pieces for texture.
Mixture: Mix in cumin, coriander, parsley, flour, salt, and pepper. Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to firm up.
Shaping: Form small balls or patties.
Frying: Fry in hot oil for 3 minutes per side. Important: the oil needs to be quite hot, as chickpea fritters tend to soak up oil.
Serving: With tahini, lemon, or tzatziki.

ing: Kefalotyri or Graviera cheese 200g (sliced 1 cm thick)
steps: Dipping: Dip the cheese slice in cold water for 1 minute — this helps the flour adhere better.
Flouring: Lightly flour both sides. Shake off the excess.
Frying: Heat oil in a hot pan (ideally a small saganaki pan). Fry for 1.5-2 minutes per side until golden and just beginning to melt slightly inside. Important: very hot oil gives a crisp exterior.
Serving: Serve immediately in the pan, drizzled with lemon and oregano. Eat while hot.
saganaki.plate: In the pan or on a warm plate with lemon.

steps: Boiling: Place the chicken in cold water (2.5 liters) with carrots, celery, onion, and salt. Simmer over low heat for 45-50 minutes, skimming off the foam during the first few minutes.
Soup base: Remove the chicken and strain the stock. Cut the meat into pieces.
Rice: Return the stock to the pot, bring to a boil, and add the rice. Cook for 15-18 minutes.
Adding the meat: Return the chicken pieces to the pot. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Serving without avgolemono: Serve immediately in deep bowls.

Avgolemono (optional): If making avgolemono, whisk 2 eggs with the juice of 1 lemon until frothy. Gradually add 2-3 ladles of hot soup while whisking constantly (tempering). Pour back into the pot and stir in a circular motion. Important: DO NOT let it boil afterward, or the egg will curdle.
kotosoupa.plate: In a deep bowl, served hot.

steps: Soaking: Soak the trahanas in a little water for 15-30 minutes to let it swell — it cooks more evenly this way.
Sautéing: Sauté briefly in olive oil.
Boiling: Add the stock and tomato, bring to a boil, and stir. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring regularly so it doesn't stick.
Thickening: The trahanas releases starch and the soup thickens naturally. Important: if it thickens too much, add a little hot water.
Serving: In a deep bowl topped with pieces of feta — it melts slightly from the heat.
trahanas.plate: With a piece of feta and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps: Boiling the meat: Place the meat in cold water (3 liters). Boil, skimming off the foam for the first 10 minutes — the foam contains impurities and clouds the stock.
Vegetables: Add carrots, celery, onion, tomato, and salt. Simmer covered for 60-70 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Potatoes: Add the potatoes and cook for another 20 minutes.
Rice: Add the rice and cook for 15-18 minutes.
Finishing: Add lemon juice for freshness. Taste and adjust salt. Important: this soup tastes even better the next day.
kreatosopa.plate: In a deep bowl with a squeeze of lemon juice.

steps: Sautéing: Sauté the onion in olive oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and sauté for 1 minute.
Orzo: Add the orzo and stir for 2 minutes to toast it lightly — it takes on a nutty aroma.
Wine: Deglaze with wine and stir until it evaporates.
Stock: Add the hot stock gradually (not all at once), stirring like a risotto. Add a little more each time the liquid is absorbed. Important: keep the stock hot in a separate pot.
Cooking: Continue for 18-20 minutes until the orzo is al dente.
Mantecatura: Remove from the heat, add butter and Parmesan. Stir vigorously to make it creamy. Important: this is the secret to a creamy texture.
kritharoto.plate: Creamy, in a shallow bowl with grated Parmesan.

steps: Pasta: Cook in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of the pasta water.
Garlic & shrimp: Sauté the garlic in olive oil for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and sauté for 2 minutes per side. Remove the shrimp.
Sauce: In the same pan, add the canned tomato and red pepper flakes. Simmer for 8-10 minutes. Important: the sauce should thicken sufficiently.
Combining: Add the pasta to the sauce, tossing with a little pasta water if needed. Return the shrimp, and add the crumbled feta and parsley.
Serving: Serve immediately — the feta softens slightly but doesn't fully melt.
pasta_garides_feta.plate: Deep plate with extra feta on top.

steps: Batter: Dissolve the yeast in warm water (37°C) with 1 tsp sugar. Let sit for 5 minutes until it foams — a sign it's active.
Mixing: Add flour and salt, mix well. Important: the batter should be thin like a loose batter — thinner than a regular dough.
Resting: Cover and let rise for 30-45 minutes until doubled and bubbly.
Frying: Heat oil to 175°C. Drop small spoonfuls of batter into the oil. Fry for 2-3 minutes, turning for even browning.
Serving: Serve immediately with plenty of honey and cinnamon. Important: serve hot — they lose their charm once cold.
loukoumades.plate: On a plate with honey and cinnamon.

steps: Syrup first: Boil the sugar, water, and lemon for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly. Let it cool completely. Important: cold syrup on a hot cake ensures good absorption.
Whisking: Beat the butter and sugar until pale. Add the eggs one at a time. Add the yogurt and zest.
Dry ingredients: Combine the semolina, flour, and baking powder. Gently fold into the wet mixture.
Baking: Bake in a greased pan at 175°C for 30-35 minutes until golden.
Soaking: As soon as it comes out of the oven, pour the cold syrup over it. Let it absorb completely before slicing.
revani.plate: Cut into diamonds with almonds on top.

ing: Fresh yeast 40 g or dry 14 g
steps: Activating the yeast: Dissolve the yeast in lukewarm milk with a spoonful of sugar and a little flour, and leave it for 15 minutes until it foams.
Important: If it does not foam, the yeast is dead. Start again — nothing later can rescue it.
Grinding the mastic: Grind the mastic tears in a mortar with a pinch of sugar. Important: use no more than 3 tears — mastic in excess turns bitter and medicinal.
Making the dough: Mix the flour with the sugar, the mahleb, the ground mastic, the zest and the salt, then add the yeast mixture and the beaten eggs.
Kneading: Knead for 15 minutes, adding the softened butter little by little, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Important: The dough must pass the windowpane test — stretch a piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing. This is what gives tsoureki its fibrous pull.
First rising: Cover and leave in a warm draught-free spot for 2-3 hours, until it has trebled in size.
Plaiting: Divide into three ropes and plait them, tucking the ends underneath.
Second rising: Let it rise again on the tray for 1-1.5 hours. Important: skipping this second rise gives a dense tsoureki that will not pull apart in strands.
Baking: Brush with egg, scatter almonds and bake at 170°C for 40 minutes, covering it with foil if it browns too fast.
tsoureki.wine: Milk or coffee — traditionally after the Resurrection service.
tsoureki.plate: Serve in slices or torn by hand, with a red egg alongside.

steps: Whisking: Beat the butter with the sugar in a mixer for 5-7 minutes until light and fluffy.
Eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between each addition. Add the vanilla and zest.
Dry ingredients: Combine the flour with the baking powder. Add the flour and milk alternately to the mixture, folding gently.
Coin: Place the wrapped coin inside the batter.
Baking: In a greased 26 cm pan, bake at 175°C for 45-50 minutes. Test with a toothpick.
Garnish: Once cooled, dust with powdered sugar in a design (usually the year). Important: tradition — the host cuts the first piece for Christ, one for the household, then serves the rest.
vasilopita.plate: Dusted with powdered sugar; the coin brings good luck.

ing: Filling: Eggs 3, Sugar 150g, Juice of 3 lemons, Zest of 2 lemons, Butter 80g
steps: Dough: Cut the cold butter into cubes and rub into the flour and sugar until crumbly. Add the egg and knead minimally. Important: don't let the dough warm up — cold butter makes the crust crisp.
Chilling: Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Tart shell: Roll out thinly into a tart pan and prick with a fork. Line with parchment and fill with weights (beans). Blind bake at 180°C for 15 minutes, remove the weights, and bake for another 5 minutes.
Filling: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, add the lemon juice, zest, and cream. Heat over a bain-marie, stirring, until it thickens slightly (82°C). Stir in the butter.
Final baking: Pour the filling into the tart shell. Bake at 160°C for 20-25 minutes — the filling should still have a slight wobble in the center.
Cooling: Let it cool completely before slicing.
tarta_lemoni.plate: In thin slices with a little cream.

ing: Syrup: Sugar 250g, Water 250ml, Orange blossom water 2 tbsp
steps: Syrup: Boil the sugar, water, and orange blossom water for 5 minutes. Let cool.
Batter: Combine the semolina, coconut, sugar, yogurt, eggs, melted butter, and baking powder.
Baking: Spread the batter evenly in a greased pan. Sprinkle almonds on top. Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes.
Scoring: As soon as it comes out of the oven, score into diamonds or squares.
Soaking: Pour the cold syrup over it immediately. Let it absorb completely — at least 30 minutes. Important: cold syrup on a hot cake ensures perfect absorption without becoming overly soggy.
samali.plate: Cut into diamonds with almonds on top.

steps: Cooking the pasta: Boil salted water and cook the pasta al dente according to the package instructions. Reserve ½ cup of pasta water before draining — it will help bind the sauce.

Pesto: Place the basil, garlic, pine nuts, and cheese in a food processor. Blend, slowly adding the olive oil, until it forms a smooth sauce. Important: don't over-process — the pesto should retain a bit of texture.
Combining: Tip the drained pasta into a bowl. Add the pesto and 2-3 tbsp of pasta water. Toss quickly until evenly coated. The water makes the sauce creamy.
Serving: Divide among plates, drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil, and top with grated cheese and fresh basil. Serve immediately — pesto darkens if left to sit.
pasta_pesto.wine: Dry white wine (Assyrtiko or Sauvignon Blanc).
pasta_pesto.plate: With grated pecorino and fresh basil.

steps: Sautéing the mushrooms: In a pan with olive oil, sauté the mushrooms over high heat for 5-6 minutes until golden. Important: don't stir constantly — let them form a golden crust first. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Base: In the same pot, sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes, stirring — it should turn glossy and smell like toasted bread.
Wine: Add 100ml white wine and stir until it evaporates completely — 1-2 minutes.

Adding the stock: Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time (1-2 ladles each time), stirring constantly and letting each addition absorb before adding the next. Important: constant stirring releases the starch and makes the risotto creamy. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
Mantecatura: Remove from the heat. Add the butter and Parmesan and stir vigorously. Let rest for 2 minutes. Serve topped with the mushrooms and fresh thyme.
risotto_manitarion.plate: Creamy, topped with mushrooms and Parmesan.

steps: Cleaning the octopus: Wash the octopus thoroughly. Beat it against a hard surface 3-4 times to tenderize it. Cut into 3 cm pieces.

Cooking the octopus: In a pot without water, add the octopus with the bay leaves and allspice. Simmer covered over low heat for 30-35 minutes until tender. Important: the octopus releases its own liquid — no water is needed. Drain and keep the juices.
Sauce: Sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add the wine and let it evaporate. Add the grated tomato and 100ml of the reserved octopus juices. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Finishing: Add the octopus to the sauce and simmer for another 5 minutes. Boil the hylopites until al dente and toss them into the sauce. Serve with parsley.
hylopites_htapodi.plate: With fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps: Marinade: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic powder, paprika, oregano, salt and pepper. Add the wings and coat them thoroughly with the marinade. Let rest for 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge for best results).
Baking: Spread the wings in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Important: they shouldn't touch each other, so they crisp up rather than steam.
Temperature: Bake at 220°C for 35-40 minutes, flipping them halfway through, at the 20-minute mark. For a glaze, brush with honey during the last 5 minutes.
Serving: Serve with tzatziki or a yogurt sauce, and lemon on the side.
Browning the chicken: Season the thighs with salt and pepper and brown them in olive oil on all sides for 4-5 minutes. Remove and set aside. This locks in the juices.
Base: In the same pan, sauté the onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and both paprikas. Stir for 1 minute over low heat. Important: paprika burns easily over high heat and turns bitter.
Simmering: Add the tomato, thyme and ½ cup water. Return the chicken to the pan. Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Finishing: Remove the chicken. Stir the cream into the sauce and let it thicken for 2 minutes. Serve the chicken topped with the sauce, with rice or mashed potatoes.
kotopoulo_paprika.plate: With a rich paprika sauce and rice.

steps: Browning the meat: Cut the pork into 2 cm medallions. Season with salt and pepper and brown in olive oil for 3 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Sautéing: In the same pan, sauté the onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and diced apple, and cook for another 2 minutes.
Sauce: Deglaze with the white wine and let it evaporate for 2 minutes. Add the mustard and cream, and stir. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Finishing: Return the meat to the sauce and simmer covered for 8-10 minutes. Important: don't let it boil hard — the cream will split. Serve with mashed potatoes or rice.
xoirino_moutardes.wine: White Chardonnay or a light red.
xoirino_moutardes.plate: With a creamy mustard sauce and apple slices.

steps: Marinade: Mix the olive oil, juice of half a lemon, thinly sliced garlic, salt, pepper and dill. For a sweet-and-sour touch, add honey and soy sauce. Coat the fillets and let rest for 15 minutes.

Baking: Place the fillets on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes, depending on thickness. Important: the salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork and the center is still slightly pink.
Serving: Serve immediately with lemon slices, fresh dill, and rice or roasted vegetables on the side.
solomos_fournou.plate: With lemon slices and fresh dill.

steps: Stuffing the fish: Wash and pat the fish dry. Fill the cavity with rosemary, thyme, lemon slices and garlic.
Salt mixture: Mix the coarse salt with the 2 egg whites until it resembles wet sand. This helps it stay compact during baking.
Encasing: Spread half the salt mixture on a baking sheet, place the fish on top and cover completely with the remaining mixture. Important: the salt should cover the fish by 1-2 cm on all sides.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes. Crack the salt "crust" with a spoon to break it open. Serve with lemon and olive oil.
lavraki_alati.plate: With olive oil, lemon and boiled potatoes.

steps: Preparing the tomatoes: Cut the tomatoes, remove the seeds and squeeze them well to drain the liquid. Chop finely or coarsely grate them. Important: if you don't squeeze them well enough, the mixture will turn watery.
Mixture: Combine the tomato, finely chopped onion, parsley, mint, salt and pepper. Add the flour gradually until you get a thick mixture you can shape. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Frying: Heat oil in a pan. Drop spoonfuls of the mixture and press lightly to flatten. Fry for 3-4 minutes per side over medium heat until golden.
Serving: Place on paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve hot with tzatziki or yogurt.
tomatokeftedes.plate: Hot, with tzatziki or yogurt on the side.

steps: Sautéing the vegetables: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot. Sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add the diced carrot, zucchini and bell pepper, and sauté for 4-5 minutes.
Rice: Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells lightly nutty.
Cooking: Add the tomato, stock, turmeric, thyme and salt. Stir and bring to a boil. Important: immediately lower the heat, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Finishing: Remove from the heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Serve with fresh herbs.
pilafi_laxanikon.plate: With fresh parsley and grated feta.

steps: Meat filling: Sauté the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add the ground beef and cook over high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until browned. Add the tomato, cinnamon, salt and pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Eggs & cheese: Let the meat mixture cool slightly. Add the beaten eggs and grated cheese, and mix well.

Layering: Oil a 30x35 cm baking pan. Layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing with oil between layers. Spread the filling evenly. Cover with the remaining phyllo sheets, brushing with oil and scoring into portions on top.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until well browned. Important: let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting so it doesn't fall apart.
kimadopita.plate: Cut into triangles or squares, served hot.

steps: Cutting the avocado: Halve the avocado, remove the pit and cut into cubes or slices. Important: drizzle immediately with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Preparation: Halve the cherry tomatoes, cut the cucumber into half-moons, and finely chop the spring onions.
Serving: Toss everything together or arrange on a platter. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon. Season with salt, pepper and fresh herbs. Serve immediately.
salata_avokanto.plate: On a platter with fresh basil.

steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt, olive oil and the yeast water. Knead for 8-10 minutes.
Let the dough rise, covered, for 1 hour.
Roll out the dough into a round base. Spread with tomato sauce.
Top with pieces of mozzarella.
Bake at 250°C for 12-15 minutes until golden.
Remove from the oven, top with fresh basil and serve immediately.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella, sliced mushrooms and olives.
Bake at 250°C for 12 minutes.
Remove from the oven and add the prosciutto on top.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve.
Roll out the dough and spread with a little tomato sauce.
Distribute the 4 cheeses evenly.
Bake at 250°C for 12-14 minutes until the cheeses melt and turn golden.
Garnish with basil and serve.
Cut the vegetables into thin slices. Lightly sauté in a pan with a little oil.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and the vegetables.
Sprinkle with oregano and a little olive oil.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Serve hot.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and distribute all the toppings evenly.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve hot.
Fry the bacon with a little garlic until crisp.
Beat the eggs with the cream and parmesan.
Roll out the dough and spread with the egg-and-cream mixture.
Top with mozzarella and the bacon.
Bake at 230°C for 13-15 minutes.
Grind fresh pepper on top and serve immediately.
Cut the chicken into strips and marinate with mustard, paprika, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a pan until done.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella, chicken, peppers and onion.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Serve hot.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce.
Top with mozzarella and pepperoni slices.
Bake at 250°C for 12-14 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with oregano and chili flakes if desired.
Serve immediately.
Roll out the dough and spread with tomato sauce and mozzarella.
Mentally divide the pizza into 4 sections.
In each section, place one of the 4 toppings: ham, mushrooms, artichokes, olives.
Bake at 250°C for 13-15 minutes.
Sprinkle with oregano and serve.
Drain the chickpeas, reserving a little of their liquid.
Add the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy. If needed, add a little of the reserved chickpea liquid.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Serve in a bowl, drizzled with olive oil and paprika on top.
Sauté the finely chopped onion in the oil until softened.
Add the tomato, salt, pepper and sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the peas and cook for 20 minutes.
Stir in the dill at the end. Serve hot with bread.
Boil the lentils for 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain and let cool.
Cut the onion, cherry tomatoes and cucumber into small pieces.
Make a dressing with olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Toss the lentils, vegetables and dressing together.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
Mix the flour with cold butter, cut into pieces, until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the egg and a little water, and knead lightly. Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Mash the feta and anthotyro together. Add the eggs, milk and pepper.
Roll out the dough in a baking pan and spread the filling over it.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until golden.
Shred the chicken and cut it into pieces.
Sauté the onion, then add the chicken, béchamel, cheese, eggs and parsley.
Layer sheets of phyllo brushed with oil in the baking pan, then spread the filling over them.
Cover with phyllo sheets on top, score the surface and brush with oil.
Bake at 180°C for 45-50 minutes.
Cut the puff pastry into squares.
Place feta on each square and season with pepper.
Fold into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Dissolve the yeast in the water and let stand for 5 minutes.
