Mix the flour, salt, 4 tbsp of oil and the water. Knead for 8 minutes.
Let rise for 30 minutes.
Spread the dough in a baking pan, brush with oil and sprinkle with oregano and sesame seeds.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes.
Boil the beets with their skins on for 45-50 minutes. Peel and cut into small cubes.
Make a dressing with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Spread the arugula on the base of the plate and top with the beets.
Crumble feta on top along with the walnuts and dressing.
Serve immediately.
Hard-boil the eggs (10 minutes), and boil the potatoes and green beans separately.
Slice the tomatoes and cut the eggs into quarters.
Make a dressing with olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Arrange all the ingredients neatly and separately on the plate.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve.
Cut the cabbage into thin strips and the carrots into matchsticks.
Finely chop the pepper and celery.
Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar and salt.
Toss all the vegetables with the dressing.
Let marinate for 30 minutes before serving.
Grate the cabbage and carrots, or slice them very finely.
Finely chop the spring onions.
Mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing.
Chill in the fridge for 1 hour before serving.
Spread the arugula on the base of the plate.
Cut the figs into quarters and arrange them over the arugula.
Add slices of prosciutto and chopped walnuts.
Grate parmesan on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic cream, and season with salt and pepper.
Make the Caesar dressing: mayonnaise, lemon juice, grated garlic, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper.
Cut the romaine lettuce into pieces and wash thoroughly.
Toss the lettuce with the dressing.
Add the croutons and grated parmesan.
Serve immediately.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Purée with a blender until smooth.
Stir in the cream and heat through.
Serve with fresh basil and bread.
Cut the pumpkin into cubes and sauté with the onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, cumin, salt and pepper.
Cover with the stock and simmer for 25 minutes until tender.
Purée with a blender, then stir in the cream.
Serve hot with a drizzle of olive oil on top.
Sauté the onion, garlic, carrots and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato, stock, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and beans. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Serve with parmesan and basil.
Slice the onions thinly. Sauté in the butter and oil over low heat for 40 minutes until caramelized.
Deglaze with the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the stock, thyme, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Ladle the soup into individual bowls, top with a slice of bread and the cheese.
Broil in the oven for 3-4 minutes until the cheese melts.
Lightly toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Put the basil, pine nuts, parmesan, garlic and salt in a blender.
Blend, gradually adding the olive oil, until it becomes a smooth paste.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Store in a jar with a little oil on top in the fridge.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk quickly for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Gradually add the milk, whisking constantly.
Stir until it thickens (8-10 minutes).
Season with salt and pepper, and add the nutmeg.
Grate the garlic or crush it in a mortar with salt.
Mix the mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice and mustard.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Cover and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes to let the flavor develop.
Serve as a dip or accompaniment.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, oregano, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in fresh basil at the end.
Use for pasta, pizza, or as a base for other recipes.
Cut the cauliflower into florets and boil for 8 minutes. Drain.
Spread in a baking pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, until lightly golden.
Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for another 15 minutes until golden and gratinéed.
Separate the cabbage leaves and boil them for 3-4 minutes. Drain.
Sauté the onion and carrot. Add the rice, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Wrap 1-2 tbsp of filling in each cabbage leaf.
Arrange in a pot, add the tomatoes, oil, lemon, and water.
Simmer, covered, for 40-45 minutes.
Cut the eggplants into 1cm slices. Salt them and let sit for 20 minutes. Pat dry.
Coat each slice in flour.
Fry in hot oil for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Remove onto paper towels.
Serve topped with grated garlic, vinegar, and salt.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with a little oil for 3-4 minutes. Squeeze out the excess liquid.
Mix the yogurt with grated garlic, lemon, and salt.
Spread the yogurt over the base of the plate.
Top with the spinach.
Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with red pepper flakes.
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into rounds or wedges.
Mix the oil, honey, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Toss the sweet potatoes in the mixture to coat.
Spread on a baking pan. Bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes.
Serve garnished with thyme.
If using dried beans, soak them overnight and boil for 45 minutes.
Sauté the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery in oil for 8-10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, salt, pepper, and a little water.
Add the cooked beans and stir to combine.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until the liquid has been absorbed.
Serve with parsley and bread.
Slice the mushrooms and sauté with the onion and garlic for 10 minutes, until their liquid has evaporated. Important: the mushrooms must dry out well, otherwise the pie will turn soggy.
Let cool, then mix with the crumbled feta, eggs, cream, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Grease a baking pan and layer 3 phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with oil.
Spread the filling evenly.
Cover with the remaining 3 phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil. Score the surface.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until golden.
Wash and finely chop the spinach. Salt it and squeeze it very well to remove the liquid.
Mix the spinach with the crumbled feta, grated graviera, eggs, spring onions, and dill. Taste for salt.
Grease a baking pan and layer 4 phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with oil.
Spread the filling evenly.
Cover with the remaining 4 phyllo sheets, brushing each with oil. Score the top and sprinkle lightly with water.
Bake at 185°C for 45-50 minutes, until well golden.
Beat the eggs with the milk. Add the crumbled anthotyro, mint, a little salt, and pepper.
Grease a baking pan and layer 3 phyllo sheets, brushing each sheet with oil.
Spread the filling evenly.
Cover with the remaining 3 phyllo sheets, brushing with oil. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 175°C for 40 minutes, until golden brown.
Cook the bulgur according to the package instructions, or soak it in hot water for 20 minutes. Let cool.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, tomatoes, cucumber, and spring onions.
Combine the bulgur with the vegetables.
Add the oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper, and toss.
Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Rinse the quinoa and cook according to package instructions (about 15 minutes). Let cool.
Dice the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, avocado, and red onion.
Combine the quinoa with the vegetables and cilantro.
Add the oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately or chilled from the refrigerator.
Dice the apples and sprinkle with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Thinly slice the celery. Roughly chop the walnuts.
Mix the mayonnaise with the yogurt, salt, and pepper.
Combine the apples, celery, walnuts, and grapes with the dressing.
Serve on lettuce leaves.
Chop the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and garlic into pieces.
Soak the bread in water for 2 minutes, then squeeze it out.
Combine everything in a blender with the oil and vinegar. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pass through a sieve for a smoother texture (optional).
Season with salt and pepper and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Serve ice-cold with a drizzle of oil on top.
Sauté the onion and garlic in oil for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped carrots, potatoes, and celery. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini, tomato, stock, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for 25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Serve with fresh parsley and bread.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente. Reserve 150ml of the pasta water.
Toast plenty of black pepper in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add 50ml of the pasta water to the pan and stir.
Add the pasta to the pan. Important: remove from the heat before adding the cheese — the heat will cause the cheese to seize and turn clumpy.
Add the cheese gradually, stirring and adding more pasta water as needed, until the sauce turns creamy.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.
Boil the pasta until al dente (2 minutes less than the package instructions).
Sauté the onion and garlic. Add the ground meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes, salt, pepper, and basil. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Combine the pasta with the sauce and half the cheese.
Spread in a baking pan. Top with the mozzarella and remaining cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until golden on top.
Wash the zucchini blossoms carefully and remove the pistil from inside.
Parboil the rice lightly (5 minutes) — it will continue cooking inside the blossoms.
Mix the rice with the crumbled feta, finely chopped onion, dill, and mint.
Carefully fill each blossom without tearing it, and twist the tips to seal.
Arrange in a pot with oil, a little water, and salt. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and mash them. Let cool completely — warm potatoes absorb oil and the patties won't hold together.
Mix the mash with the eggs, crumbled feta, spring onions, parsley, flour, salt, and pepper.
Shape into small round patties.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until well browned.
Serve with tzatziki.
Wash the chard well and cut the stems into pieces.
Bring salted water to a boil.
Boil the stems first for 5 minutes, then add the leaves for another 5-8 minutes.
Drain well.
Serve warm with a generous drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Crush the biscuits into crumbs and mix with the melted butter. Press into the bottom of a 24cm springform pan.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar until smooth.
Add the eggs one at a time, then the cream, vanilla, and lemon juice.
Pour over the biscuit base.
Bake in a bain-marie at 160°C for 50-55 minutes. Important: the center should still wobble slightly when it comes out — it will firm up as it cools.
Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy.
Add the mascarpone and fold in gently.
Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks and fold them gently into the mixture.
Mix the espresso with the liqueur in a shallow bowl.
Quickly dip the ladyfingers (1-2 seconds per side) and arrange them in a baking dish.
Spread half the cream over the ladyfingers. Add another layer of ladyfingers, then the remaining cream.
Dust with cocoa and chill for 4-6 hours.
Melt the chocolate with the butter over a bain-marie or in the microwave. Let it cool slightly.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale. Stir into the chocolate.
Whip the heavy cream into whipped cream. Whip the egg whites into stiff peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the chocolate first with gentle movements, then fold in the meringue. Important: do not stir vigorously — the air is what gives the mousse its light, airy texture.
Divide among glasses or bowls and chill for 3-4 hours.
Serve with grated chocolate or whipped cream.

ing: For serving: strawberry or blueberry coulis
steps: Soak the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla without letting them boil (80°C).
Squeeze out the gelatin and dissolve it into the warm mixture, stirring.
Divide among molds or glasses. Chill for 4+ hours or overnight.
To unmold: dip the mold in hot water for 5 seconds and turn it out.
Serve with fruit coulis.
Melt the chocolate with the butter over a bain-marie. Let it cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with the sugar for 3-4 minutes until pale.
Stir the chocolate into the eggs.
Sift the flour and cocoa and fold them into the mixture with gentle movements. Important: do not overmix — a few small lumps are fine. Overmixing will toughen the brownies.
Pour into a greased 20x20cm baking pan. Scatter the walnuts on top.
Bake at 170°C for 22-25 minutes. The center should still jiggle slightly — that's what keeps the brownies moist and fudgy.

ing: Pork leg or shoulder 1 kg, cut into portions
Hot water or stock, about 1 liter
steps: Preparation: Wash the pork, cut it into portions, and pat it thoroughly dry with paper towels so it browns properly. Clean the celery, cutting the stalks into 4-5cm pieces and the celery root into thick slices.

Searing: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and sear the pork over high heat on all sides until nicely golden. Important: brown the meat in batches rather than all at once, otherwise the temperature drops, the meat releases its juices, and it boils instead of caramelizing.
Onion: Lower the heat slightly, add the onions, and sweat them for 3-4 minutes until they turn glossy, stirring so they don't burn.
Simmering the meat: Add hot water or stock until the meat is almost covered, season with salt and pepper, lower the heat, and simmer covered for about 1 hour until it starts to become tender.

Adding the celery: First blanch the celery for 2-3 minutes in boiling water to remove its bitterness, drain, and add it to the pot. Continue cooking for another 20-30 minutes, until the meat and celery are tender and enough broth remains for the avgolemono.

Avgolemono (egg-lemon sauce): Beat the eggs in a bowl until frothy and gradually add the lemon juice. Remove the pot from the heat and, with a ladle, slowly add a little hot broth to the egg mixture while whisking constantly. Important: the broth must not be boiling when you add the avgolemono, or it will curdle; add the hot broth gradually so the eggs' temperature rises evenly.

Thickening: Pour the avgolemono into the pot, swirl gently in circular motions (do not stir with a spoon) and set over very low heat for half a minute, without letting it boil, so the sauce thickens slightly.
Serving: Let the dish rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving, so the flavors come together and the avgolemono sets.
xoirino_selino.wine: Dry white, such as Assyrtiko or Moschofilero.
xoirino_selino.plate: Serve hot with plenty of avgolemono sauce, freshly ground pepper, and fresh bread to soak up the juices.

ing: Pork leg or shoulder 1 kg, cut into portions
Potatoes 1 kg, cut into thick wedges
steps: Preparation: Pat the pork pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper on all sides. Important: the meat must be completely dry before searing, otherwise it will boil instead of browning and won't develop the caramelized crust that gives it depth of flavor.
Searing: Heat half the olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat and brown the pork pieces on all sides, in batches so they don't crowd the pot. Remove and set aside.
Aromatics: Lower the heat, add the chopped onion and garlic, and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Simmering: Return the meat to the pot, add the mustard, half the oregano, and the stock. Cover and simmer over low heat for about 45 minutes, until the meat starts to become tender.
Adding the potatoes: Add the potatoes around the meat, pour in the remaining olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and continue cooking covered for another 30-35 minutes, stirring gently.

Lemon: When the meat and potatoes are almost tender, add the lemon juice and the remaining oregano. Important: the lemon goes in at the end, because prolonged boiling makes its acidity toughen the meat fibers and lose its fresh, bright citrus aroma.
Reducing the sauce: Leave uncovered for 8-10 minutes over medium heat so the sauce thickens and takes on the lemon flavor. Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and lemon.
Resting: Remove from the heat and let the dish rest, covered, for 10 minutes before serving, so the meat relaxes and reabsorbs its juices.
xoirino_lemonato.wine: Dry white, such as Assyrtiko or Moschofilero.
xoirino_lemonato.plate: Serve hot with the potatoes and plenty of lemon sauce, accompanied by fresh bread and a green salad.

steps: Preparing the meat: Slice each chicken fillet horizontally through the middle to make it thinner. Place the pieces between two sheets of parchment paper and pound them with a meat mallet until about 1 cm thick. Important: an even, thin thickness is the secret to a schnitzel that cooks quickly and stays juicy without the coating burning.
Seasoning: Season the cutlets well with salt and pepper on both sides. Let them come to room temperature for 10 minutes.

Setting up the breading station: Prepare three plates. Put the flour in the first, the beaten eggs with a little salt in the second, and the breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan and garlic powder in the third.

Breading: Coat each fillet first in flour (shaking off the excess), then in egg, and finally in breadcrumbs, pressing well so the coating sticks all over. Important: press the breadcrumbs on firmly by hand for an even, crisp crust.
Heating the oil: Heat the sunflower oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. It's ready when a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles immediately on contact (about 170-180°C).
Frying: Fry the cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Don't overcrowd the pan, or the temperature will drop.
Draining: Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to drain off excess oil.
Serving: Serve hot with lemon wedges for squeezing over.
kotopoulo_pane.wine: A crisp dry white or ice-cold beer.
kotopoulo_pane.plate: Serve with french fries and a refreshing green salad.

ing: Lamb offal (liver, heart, lungs, spleen) 1.5 kg
steps: Cleaning the intestines: Turn the thin intestines inside out with the help of a needle or a stick and wash them thoroughly under plenty of running water. Let them soak in water with lemon and salt for 1-2 hours to remove the odor.

Preparing the offal: Wash the liver, heart, lungs, and spleen well. Cut them into large pieces (3-4cm chunks) and season with salt and pepper. Thread the pieces alternately onto the skewer, packing them tightly side by side to form a solid, compact core.

Wrapping with the intestines: Wrap the cleaned intestines tightly around the offal, spiraling from one end to the other, binding the whole core securely. Finish by adding a little caul fat to hold it all together.
Seasoning: Mix the olive oil with the lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper. Brush the whole kokoretsi generously with the mixture before grilling.

Important: Kokoretsi is always grilled over low, steady heat with charcoal that has turned to embers (not open flame). It needs slow cooking for 2-3 hours, turning the skewer continuously, so it cooks through evenly inside without burning on the outside.
Grilling: Start turning the skewer at a distance from the embers. As it cooks, baste every 20-30 minutes with the remaining oil-and-lemon mixture to keep it juicy and let it form a crust.
Finishing: The kokoretsi is ready when the intestines on the outside turn crisp and golden-red and the interior is fully cooked. Remove from the heat and let it rest for 5-10 minutes.
Serving: Slice with a sharp knife, sprinkle with a little extra oregano, and serve hot with lemon.
kokoretsi.plate: Serve hot, sliced, with fresh lemon, oregano, and french fries.

ing: Veal, top round or shoulder, sliced 800g
steps: Preparation: Lightly pound the veal slices to tenderize them and season with salt and pepper. Dust with flour on both sides, shaking off the excess.
Searing: Heat the olive oil well in a deep skillet and sear the slices over high heat until nicely browned on both sides. Transfer to a pot.
The secret of the sauce: In the same oil, add the chopped garlic and parsley and sauté for half a minute, just until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Deglazing: Deglaze with the vinegar and wine, let the alcohol evaporate for 1-2 minutes, and pour the sauce over the meat.
Important: authentic Sofrito contains no tomato. Its characteristic white color and tangy flavor come solely from the vinegar, garlic, and parsley, so don't be tempted to add tomato paste.
Simmering: Add a little hot water so the meat is almost covered, cover with the lid, and simmer over low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours.
Thickening: The meat is ready when it becomes very tender and the sauce reduces to a velvety consistency. If needed, uncover toward the end to let the sauce thicken.
Serving: Taste for salt and serve hot, spooning the sauce generously over the top.
sofrito.wine: Dry white wine, ideally a Corfiot Kakotrygis.
sofrito.plate: Serve with mashed potatoes or fluffy rice to soak up the white sauce.

steps: Cleaning: Clean the anchovies, removing the heads and innards. Split them open along the belly and carefully remove the backbone, leaving two fillets either joined or separate. Rinse thoroughly with cold water.

Draining: Lay the fillets out on a kitchen towel to drain completely. Important: the fish must be dry before marinating, since excess water dilutes the vinegar and prevents the flesh from properly 'cooking.'
Salting: Arrange the fillets flesh-side up in a wide dish and sprinkle with the coarse salt. Let them sit for 20-30 minutes to release their liquid and firm up.
Marinating: Rinse off the salt quickly, drain, and place the fillets in a clean glass dish. Pour over the vinegar and lemon juice so they're fully submerged.
Curing: Cover and refrigerate for 3-6 hours. The anchovies are ready when the flesh turns completely white and opaque all the way through.
Draining the vinegar: Remove the fillets from the vinegar and drain them well. Discard the marinating vinegar.
Dressing: Arrange the fillets on a platter, sprinkle with the chopped garlic and parsley, and drizzle generously with the olive oil. Add a little pepper if desired.
Resting: Let the dressed fillets rest in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving, so the flavors of the garlic and olive oil meld in.
gavros_marinatos.plate: Serve cold as a meze, with fresh olive oil and slices of fresh bread.

ing: Fresh mussels in the shell 1 kg
Freshly ground pepper and salt, used sparingly
steps: Cleaning: Wash the mussels well under cold running water, scrubbing the shells and pulling out the "beards" (the fibrous threads). Discard any mussels that are cracked or open and don't close when tapped lightly.
Important: use only live mussels. Before cooking, any open shell must close with a light tap, otherwise the mussel is dead and must be discarded, as it can cause food poisoning.
Sautéing: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until softened. Add the chopped garlic and stir for a minute, until fragrant, without letting it burn.

Deglazing with wine: Pour in the white wine and let it come to a boil for 1-2 minutes so the alcohol evaporates. If using, add the grated tomato and cook for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Steaming: Raise the heat, add the mussels to the pot, and cover immediately with the lid. Shake the pot while holding the lid so the juices circulate and the mussels cook evenly.
Cooking time: Leave the mussels covered for 4-6 minutes, until all the shells have opened. Don't overcook them, or the flesh will toughen and become rubbery.

Checking: Discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking, as they are not safe to eat. Taste the broth and season with salt and freshly ground pepper sparingly, keeping in mind that mussels are naturally salty.
Finishing: Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice, and sprinkle with plenty of chopped parsley. Stir gently and serve immediately, while still hot and steaming.
mydia_axnista.wine: Dry, crisp white, such as Assyrtiko or Moschofilero.
mydia_axnista.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with their broth and plenty of fresh bread for dipping into the sauce. Accompany with a lemon wedge.

ing: Ripe tomatoes, grated, 400g (or 1 can chopped tomatoes)
steps: Cleaning: Wash the octopus well and remove the eyes and beak if present. If frozen, thaw completely. Cut the tentacles and head into 3-4cm pieces.

Releasing the liquid: Place the octopus in a wide pot WITHOUT oil or water over medium heat. It will release its own liquid. Let it simmer in its own juices for 15-20 minutes, until it has drawn out almost all of it. Important: octopus doesn't need water at the start — it cooks in its own liquid. This keeps it juicy and prevents it from toughening.
Sautéing: Add the olive oil and sauté the octopus for 2-3 minutes. Add the chopped onion and garlic and stir until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Pour in the red wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 2-3 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot.

Sauce: Add the grated tomato, the tomato paste dissolved in a little water, the bay leaves, allspice, a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper. Simmer covered over low heat for 40-50 minutes, until the octopus is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Adding water: When the octopus is almost done, add about 2-3 cups of hot water so there's enough liquid to cook the pasta.

Cooking the pasta: Add the ditalini to the sauce and stir well. Cook uncovered for 10-12 minutes, stirring frequently so it doesn't stick, until it absorbs the liquid and is left with a slightly thick sauce.
Resting: Remove from the heat, discard the bay leaves, and let the dish rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.
xtapodi_makaronaki.wine: Dry red, such as Agiorgitiko, or a crisp rosé.
xtapodi_makaronaki.plate: Serve hot in a deep plate with plenty of sauce, freshly ground pepper, and a little chopped parsley.

ing: Olive oil or sunflower oil for frying 1/2 liter
steps: Cleaning: Clean the red mullet by scaling from tail to head, gut them with a small cut in the belly, and rinse very well with cold water. Drain.

Drying: Lay the mullet on paper towels and dry them thoroughly, inside and out. Important: the fish must be completely dry before flouring, since moisture makes the oil spatter and prevents a crisp crust from forming.
Salting: Salt the mullet with coarse salt a few minutes before frying, not earlier, so they don't release liquid and soften.
Flouring: Pour the flour onto a shallow plate and roll each mullet to coat it evenly. Shake off the excess flour so it doesn't burn in the oil.
Heating the oil: Heat plenty of oil in a deep skillet over high heat (about 175-180°C). Test by dropping in a little flour: if it sizzles immediately, the oil is ready.
Frying: Fry the mullet in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Don't overcrowd the pan, or the temperature will drop.
Draining: Remove with a slotted spatula and let them drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, with plenty of lemon juice, freshly ground pepper, and chopped parsley.
barbounia.wine: Dry white, well chilled, or ouzo.
barbounia.plate: Serve with lemon wedges, boiled greens, or a refreshing village salad.

ing: Fish for stewing, such as scorpionfish or grouper, 1 kg (cleaned, sliced)
steps: Preparing the fish: Clean the fish well, cut it into thick slices, season with salt and pepper, and set aside. Bourdeto calls for firm-fleshed fish that won't fall apart during cooking.
Sautéing the onions: In a wide, shallow pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onions over low heat until wilted and sweetened, without browning. Add the garlic for one more minute.

Adding the pepper: Lower the heat and add the boukovo and paprika, stirring quickly. Important: don't let the red pepper get too hot, as it burns easily and turns bitter — the secret is to release its aroma and color into the oil without scorching it.

Building the sauce: Dissolve the tomato paste in a little hot water and add it to the pot along with the remaining hot water. Bourdeto is spicy and reddish, not tomato-based, so tomato is used minimally or not at all.
Simmering the sauce: Let the sauce come to a boil and thicken slightly for 10-15 minutes over medium heat, so the flavors combine and it becomes rich with oil.

Cooking the fish: Carefully lower the fish slices into the sauce in a single layer. Shake the pot rather than stirring with a spoon, so the fish doesn't fall apart. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Finishing: Toward the end, add the lemon juice, taste, and adjust the salt and heat. Remove from the heat and let it stand for 10 minutes before serving, so the sauce sets.
bourdeto.wine: Dry white from Corfu, such as Kakotrygis.
bourdeto.plate: Serve hot with plenty of the red sauce, fresh bread for dipping, and boiled potatoes.

steps: Preparing the cabbage: Remove the outer leaves and the tough core. Slice the cabbage thinly (julienne) and wash it well. Drain.
Sautéing: Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and sauté the chopped onion over medium heat until softened and glossy, without browning.
Wilting the cabbage: Add the cabbage and stir. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it wilts and its volume reduces significantly.
Tomato: Add the grated tomato (or tomato paste dissolved in a little water), salt, and pepper. Let it cook for 5 minutes for the flavors to come together.
Adding water: Pour in the hot water or stock and bring to a boil. Important: the liquid-to-rice ratio should be about 2 to 1, so the lahanorizo stays moist rather than dry or gummy.
Adding the rice: Add the rinsed rice, stir once, and lower the heat. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Finishing: Turn off the heat, add the dill and lemon juice. Stir gently, cover, and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.
lahanorizo.plate: Serve hot with feta cheese, olives, and fresh bread.

steps: Cleaning: Trim the leeks, remove the tough roots and outer leaves, and cut into rounds. Rinse very well in a basin of water to remove all the grit trapped between the layers.
Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the chopped onion over medium heat until softened and glossy, without browning.
Wilting the leeks: Add the leeks and stir. Simmer covered over low heat for 10-15 minutes, until wilted and they release their liquid, stirring occasionally.
Adding water: Pour in the hot water or stock, season with salt and pepper, and let the leeks come to a boil for another 5 minutes.

Adding the rice: Add the rice and stir. Important: the liquid-to-rice ratio should be about 2 to 1. Make sure there's enough liquid so the dish stays moist rather than dry, since prasorizo is served like a saucy pilaf.
Simmering: Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until the rice swells and absorbs the liquid, without stirring too often.
Finishing: Just before taking the pot off the heat, add the chopped dill and lemon juice. Stir gently and taste for salt.
Resting: Turn off the heat and let it stand covered with a towel for 10 minutes to set before serving.
prasorizo.plate: Serve hot with fresh lemon, feta cheese, and a cold olive.

steps: Preparing the vegetables: Cut the eggplants and zucchini into thick rounds, the potatoes into slices, the peppers into strips, and the onions into half-moons. Important: salt the eggplant and let it sit in a colander for 20 minutes to release its bitter liquid, then rinse and dry it, so it doesn't turn bitter or soak up too much oil.
Arranging the pan: Grease a large baking pan and spread all the vegetables out, mixed together, so they cook evenly and share their flavors.
Tomato and garlic: Grate or finely chop the tomatoes and garlic cloves and scatter them over the vegetables along with half the parsley.
Seasoning: Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with salt, pepper, and oregano, and toss gently by hand to coat everything in the oil.
Baking covered: Cover the pan with foil and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 45 minutes, until the vegetables soften and release their juices.
Browning: Remove the foil, raise the temperature to 200°C, and continue baking for another 25-30 minutes, until nicely browned and most of the liquid has been absorbed.

Resting and serving: Remove the pan from the oven, sprinkle with the remaining fresh parsley, and let it rest for 10-15 minutes. Important: tourlou tastes best served warm or at room temperature, once the flavors have settled.
tourlou.plate: Serve with feta cheese and fresh bread for dipping into the juices.

steps: Preparing the tomato: Wash the ripe tomatoes and grate them on the coarse side of a box grater, discarding the skin. Drain the pulp lightly in a strainer to remove excess liquid, so the rusk doesn't get overly soggy.
Lightly moistening the rusk: Sprinkle the barley rusk with a little water (or tomato water) for just a few seconds, just enough to soften the surface.

Important: do not dunk the rusk in water. The barley rusk should stay crisp inside and soften only on the outside. A few drops of water followed by the olive oil make the difference for an authentic dakos that doesn't turn mushy.
First drizzle of oil: Drizzle the moistened rusk with 1-2 tbsp of olive oil so it soaks in and takes on flavor.
Layering the tomato: Spread the grated tomato generously over the rusk, covering the whole surface. Season lightly with salt.
Adding the cheese: Crumble the xinomyzithra (or feta) over the top in coarse pieces, covering the tomato.
Garnishing: Sprinkle with plenty of oregano, add the Kalamata olives and capers, and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Serving: Let the dakos sit for 5-10 minutes for the flavors to come together and serve immediately, while the rusk is still crisp.
dakos.wine: Dry white from Crete, ideally Vilana.
dakos.plate: Serve on a shallow plate with a final drizzle of olive oil and fresh oregano, as a meze or a light meal.

steps: Preparation: Wash the potatoes well and put them whole, unpeeled, into a pot with plenty of cold water and a little salt.

Boiling: Boil the potatoes for about 25-30 minutes, depending on size. Important: boil them whole with the skin on so they don't absorb too much water and become soggy. They're ready when a fork slides in easily but they don't fall apart.
Peeling: Drain the potatoes and, while still warm but cool enough to handle, peel off the skins.
Cutting: Cut the potatoes into thick slices or large chunks and transfer them to a large salad bowl while still warm, so they absorb the dressing better.
Dressing: In a bowl, whisk together the olive oil, vinegar or lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt, and pepper with a fork until combined.
Mixing: Finely chop the onion and parsley, add them to the potatoes along with the dressing, and toss gently so the potatoes don't break apart.
Resting: Let the salad rest for at least 15-20 minutes for the flavors to come together. Serve warm or at room temperature, with an extra drizzle of olive oil.
patatosalata.plate: Serve warm on a shallow plate, sprinkled with fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps: Boiling the vegetables: Boil the potatoes and carrots whole, unpeeled, in salted water until tender but still firm, about 20-25 minutes. Drain and let them cool completely.
Boiling the eggs: Meanwhile, boil the eggs for 9-10 minutes until hard-boiled. Plunge them into ice water, peel, and let them cool.
Cutting: Peel the cooled potatoes and carrots and cut them into small, even cubes. Also dice the gherkins and three of the eggs.

Important: boil and cut the vegetables only after they have cooled completely. If cut while hot, they will fall apart and release moisture, making the salad watery and causing the mayonnaise to split.
Sauce: In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise with the mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Mixing: In a large bowl, combine the potatoes, carrots, drained peas, gherkins, and diced eggs. Gradually add the sauce and fold gently with a spatula so everything is coated without falling apart.
Chilling: Taste and adjust the salt. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours so the flavors combine and it chills through.
Serving: Transfer to a serving platter, smooth the surface, and garnish with slices of the last egg and chopped parsley.
rosiki_salata.wine: Dry white or a lager beer, well chilled.
rosiki_salata.plate: Serve cold on a platter, garnished with egg slices and olives, as an appetizer or side for a festive spread.

steps: Custard: In a saucepan, warm the milk with half the sugar until it just starts to steam, without letting it boil. Pour in the semolina in a steady stream, whisking constantly so it doesn't clump.
Thickening: Lower the heat and stir for 4-5 minutes until the custard thickens and turns velvety. Remove from the heat.

Eggs: Beat the eggs with the remaining sugar and the vanilla. Important: Stir a little of the hot custard into the eggs (tempering them) so they don't scramble, then fold the mixture back into the custard. This prevents the eggs from curdling.
Layering the filo: Butter a baking pan and lay half the filo sheets one by one, brushing each with melted butter and letting the edges hang over the sides of the pan.
Filling: Spread the custard evenly over the filo. Cover with the remaining buttered sheets and fold the overhanging edges inward, sealing in the filling.
Scoring: Brush the surface with the last of the butter and lightly score the portions with a knife, so it will be easy to cut after baking.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until the filo turns golden and crisp.
Serving: Let it rest for 10 minutes, cut into pieces and dust generously with powdered sugar and cinnamon. Serve warm.
bougatsa.wine: Sweet Samos wine or a hot Greek coffee.
bougatsa.plate: Serve warm, cut into squares, with plenty of powdered sugar and cinnamon on top.

steps: Preheating: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and butter a medium baking pan well, so the pie won't stick.
Warming the milk: Put the milk in a saucepan with the lemon zest and warm over medium heat until steaming, without letting it come to a boil.

Semolina custard: Slowly pour the semolina into the hot milk, whisking constantly, and add half the sugar. Important: Stir continuously over low heat until the custard thickens slightly, so the semolina doesn't clump, then remove from heat.
Eggs: Beat the eggs with the remaining sugar and vanilla until fluffy and lightly pale.
Combining: Let the custard cool slightly, then gradually fold in the beaten eggs, stirring quickly so the eggs don't cook and curdle the mixture.
Layering the filo: Lay 3 sheets of filo in the pan, brushing each with melted butter, letting the edges overhang.
Filling: Pour in the custard mixture, fold the overhanging edges inward and cover with the remaining buttered sheets, lightly scoring the surface into portions.
Baking: Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden and the custard has set. Let cool, dust with powdered sugar and serve.
galatopita.wine: Sweet Samos wine or sour cherry cordial.
galatopita.plate: Serve lukewarm or cold in pieces, dusted with powdered sugar and a little cinnamon.

steps: Drying the filo: Unroll the filo sheets and spread them out crumpled on a baking sheet or countertop for 2-3 hours, so they dry out well and become crisp. Important: Well-dried filo is the secret to authentic orange pie, as it absorbs the syrup properly and gives the characteristic spongy texture without turning soggy.
Crumbling: Crumble the dried filo by hand into small pieces in a large bowl.
Batter: In another bowl, beat the eggs with the sugar until fluffy, add the sunflower oil, the yogurt, the orange zest, and finally the baking powder. Mix until smooth.
Combining: Pour the wet batter over the crumbled filo and stir gently until fully absorbed and all the pieces are soaked.
Baking: Butter a baking pan, pour in the mixture and bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for about 40-45 minutes, until the top turns golden.
Syrup: While the pie bakes, boil the water with the sugar and orange juice for 5-7 minutes until it thickens slightly. Remove from heat and let cool to lukewarm.
Syruping: Important: Always pour a hot dessert with lukewarm syrup (or vice versa), never hot with hot, so it absorbs evenly and stays syrupy without turning soggy.
Resting: Let the orange pie absorb all the syrup for at least 2-3 hours before cutting it into pieces and serving.
portokalopita.wine: Sour cherry cordial or a sweet white wine.
portokalopita.plate: Serve cold with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a little orange zest.

ing: For the syrup: sugar 400 g, water 400 ml, 1 lemon (juice & peel), 1 cinnamon stick
steps: Preparation: Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Beat the yolks with the sugar and the butter (or olive oil) until fluffy and pale.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a separate bowl, mix the breadcrumbs, chopped walnuts, baking powder, cinnamon and cloves. Gradually fold them into the yolk mixture, stirring gently.

Meringue: Whisk the egg whites into a stiff meringue and fold them into the mixture with gentle motions from the bottom up, so they don't lose volume. Important: A well-whipped meringue and gentle folding are the secret to a light walnut cake that doesn't become heavy from the syrup.
Baking: Butter a baking pan, pour in the mixture and bake in a preheated fan oven at 170°C for about 35-40 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

Syrup: While it bakes, boil the sugar with the water, lemon peel and cinnamon stick in a saucepan for 5-6 minutes. Add the lemon juice at the end and remove from heat. The syrup should be medium-thick.

Syruping: As soon as the walnut cake comes out of the oven, slowly pour the syrup over it. Important: The cake must be hot and the syrup lukewarm (or vice versa) so it soaks in evenly without becoming soggy.
Resting: Let the walnut cake cool completely and absorb all the syrup, ideally for 3-4 hours, before cutting it into diamond shapes.
Serving: Cut into pieces and serve on a small plate, garnishing each portion with half a walnut.
karydopita.wine: Sweet Mavrodafni wine or Greek coffee.
karydopita.plate: In diamond-shaped pieces with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

ing: Sugar 200 g (150 g for the filling, 50 g for the dough)
Cinnamon 1 tsp + a little grated nutmeg
steps: Dough: In a bowl, mix the flour with the baking powder and the 50 g of sugar. Add the cold butter cut into cubes and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add 1 egg and bring the dough together without overworking it.
Important: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. The cold butter and resting time make the dough crisp and short (shortcrust) rather than tough.
Filling: Peel the apples, cut them into thin slices or cubes and immediately sprinkle with lemon juice to prevent browning. Add the zest, the 150 g of sugar, cinnamon and a little nutmeg.
Sautéing: In a frying pan, sauté the apples with the sugar for 8-10 minutes, until they soften and caramelize slightly and their liquid evaporates. Let cool and add the walnuts.
Rolling out: Divide the dough into two portions (2/3 and 1/3). Roll out the larger piece with a rolling pin and line a buttered baking pan or tin, covering the sides as well.

Filling: Pour in the apple filling and level it out. Roll out the remaining piece of dough and cover the pie, sealing the edges well. Cut 2-3 slits in the top to let steam escape and brush with beaten egg.
Baking: Bake in a preheated fan oven at 180°C for 40-45 minutes, until the top turns golden brown.
Serving: Let the apple pie cool a little so the filling sets, dust with powdered sugar and cut into pieces.
milopita.wine: Sweet Samos wine or a hot cinnamon tea.
milopita.plate: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, dusted with cinnamon.

ing: Sugar 1.5 cups with 2 tbsp cocoa (for the syrup)
steps: Preparation: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and butter or line with parchment paper a baking pan about 25x35 cm.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, sift together the flour, cocoa, baking powder, and add the sugar, mixing well.
Mixing the wet ingredients: In a second bowl, whisk the eggs with the oil, milk and vanilla until smooth.

Combining: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and whisk until the batter is smooth. Important: Don't overmix the batter, as this develops the gluten and the cake turns out dense and chewy instead of light.
Baking: Pour the mixture into the pan and bake for 30-35 minutes, until risen and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Syrup: While it bakes, boil the water with the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan for 4-5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Syruping: As soon as the cake comes out, score it into pieces and slowly pour the hot syrup over the hot cake so it soaks in evenly.
Resting: Let the chocolate cake cool and absorb the syrup for at least 2 hours before serving.
sokolatopita.wine: Sweet Mavrodafni wine or a hot coffee.
sokolatopita.plate: Serve in pieces with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

steps: Preparing the pastry: Unroll the kataifi on a clean surface and gently separate the strands by hand so it's fluffy and easy to roll. Cover with a slightly damp towel so it doesn't dry out.
Filling: In a bowl, mix the chopped walnuts with the sugar, cinnamon and ground cloves. This is the aromatic filling that goes into each roll.
Rolling: Take a strip of kataifi about 10 cm wide, place a spoonful of the filling at one end and roll it up tightly into a log. Repeat until the ingredients are used up.

Buttering: Arrange the rolls side by side in a buttered baking pan, seam-side down. Pour all the melted butter evenly over them, making sure every roll is soaked. Important: The butter should be hot and melted (ideally clarified) so it soaks deep into the strands and the kataifi turns out crisp and golden, not greasy.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for about 50-60 minutes, until well browned and a deep golden color all over.

Syrup: While it bakes, boil the sugar with the water, cinnamon stick and cloves in a saucepan for 8-10 minutes. Add the lemon juice at the end and remove from heat. Important: The rule of hot into cold or cold into hot applies: pour the cold syrup over the hot kataifi (or vice versa) so it absorbs it properly and stays crisp.
Syruping: As soon as the kataifi comes out of the oven, slowly pour the lukewarm syrup over it spoonful by spoonful, so it absorbs evenly.
Resting: Let it rest and absorb all the syrup for at least 3-4 hours before cutting and serving.
kataifi.wine: Sweet Muscat wine or Greek coffee.
kataifi.plate: Serve at room temperature with a scoop of kaimaki ice cream.

ing: Heavy cream 500 ml (for the whipped topping) and vanilla
steps: Preparing the kataifi: Loosen the kataifi by hand in a bowl so the strands separate, then pour over the melted butter, mixing well so it's soaked everywhere.
Baking: Spread the kataifi in a buttered baking pan, pressing it lightly into an even layer. Bake at 180°C for 30-40 minutes, until well browned and crisp and golden.

Syrup: Boil the sugar with the water for 8-10 minutes, add the lemon juice and let it boil for another minute or two. Important: The syrup should be hot and the kataifi hot as well, or conversely cold syrup over a hot dessert, so it absorbs properly and stays crisp without turning soggy.
Syruping: Slowly pour the syrup over the hot baked kataifi so it's absorbed everywhere. Let it cool completely.

Custard: Dissolve the cornstarch and sugar in a little cold milk, add the egg yolks and stir. Heat the remaining milk and once warm, pour in the mixture, stirring constantly until it thickens into a thick custard. Let it cool with plastic wrap pressed onto the surface.
Layering the custard: Spread the cooled custard evenly over the syrup-soaked kataifi and smooth the surface with a spatula.
Whipped cream: Whip the cold heavy cream with a little sugar and vanilla into stiff peaks and spread it generously over the custard as the final layer.
Chilling and serving: Refrigerate the ekmek for at least 3-4 hours so it sets and the layers firm up before cutting into pieces.
ekmek.wine: Sweet Samos wine or sour cherry cordial.
ekmek.plate: Serve chilled, garnished with crushed Aegina pistachios and cinnamon.

ing: Coarsely chopped walnuts or almonds 60 g (optional)
steps: Breaking the biscuits: Break the biscuits by hand into small, irregular pieces in a large bowl. Important: Don't turn them into powder in a blender. The irregular pieces are what give the cross-section its mosaic (salami) look that's characteristic of this dessert. Add the walnuts too if using.

Melting the chocolate: Melt the chocolate with the butter in a bain-marie (a bowl over a saucepan of gently simmering water, without the bottom touching the water), stirring until smooth. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Cocoa cream: In another bowl, beat the egg with the sugar until fluffy. Stir in the cocoa and evaporated milk and mix well so there are no lumps.
Combining the mixtures: Pour the melted chocolate into the egg mixture, stirring constantly, and finally add the cognac. The mixture should be smooth and glossy.
Mixing with the biscuits: Pour the chocolate cream over the broken biscuits and gently fold with a spatula until all the pieces are coated, keeping them intact.

Rolling into a log: Turn the mixture out onto plastic wrap or parchment paper and, gathering the edges, shape it into a compact log (salami shape). Roll it up tightly and twist the ends like a candy wrapper to hold its shape.
Chilling: Put the log in the refrigerator for at least 4-5 hours (ideally overnight) so it firms up completely and slices cleanly.
Serving: Unwrap, dust with a little powdered sugar if you want the salami look, and cut into slices about 1 cm thick with a sharp knife.
mosaiko.wine: Sweet Mavrodafni wine or an espresso.
mosaiko.plate: In slices on a small plate, dusted with powdered sugar.

steps: Choux pastry: Put the water, butter cut into cubes and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil, so the butter melts completely before the liquid boils.

Cooking the dough: Add all the sifted flour at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon over low heat, until the dough comes together into a ball and pulls away from the sides (about 2-3 minutes). Important: The dough must dry out well over the heat, otherwise the choux won't puff up and will stay heavy.
Incorporating the eggs: Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, until you get a smooth, glossy dough that forms a soft peak.

Baking the choux: Using a piping bag, pipe small mounds onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and bake in a preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, without opening the oven door, until puffed and golden. Let them cool completely.

Pastry cream: Heat the milk with the vanilla. Whisk the sugar with the cornstarch and a little milk, pour into the hot milk and stir over medium heat until the custard thickens. Let it cool with plastic wrap pressed onto the surface.
Chocolate sauce: Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie or with a little heavy cream, stirring until it becomes a smooth, glossy sauce.
Filling: Cut the choux buns open on the side or pierce the base and fill them with the cold pastry cream using a piping bag.
Assembly: Stack the filled choux buns in a bowl or serving dish, pour over plenty of hot chocolate sauce and serve immediately.
profiterol.wine: Sweet Samos wine or Vin Santo.
profiterol.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with plenty of chocolate sauce and a little grated dark chocolate on top.

ing: Leg or shoulder of lamb 1.5 kg
steps: Preparing the meat: Wash the lamb well and pat it dry with paper towels. Make small incisions all over the surface with a knife and insert pieces of garlic.

Marinating: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper. Rub the meat well with the mixture and let it marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the refrigerator.
Potatoes: Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices or chunks. Arrange them around the meat in a baking pan and drizzle with a little olive oil, lemon juice, oregano and salt.
Important: Add the water or stock to the pan and cover it tightly with foil for the first hours of roasting; this way the meat steams, stays juicy and becomes tender without drying out.
First roasting: Roast in a preheated oven at 160°C for about 2 to 2.5 hours, covered, until the meat is tender and comes away easily from the bone.
Uncovering and browning: Remove the foil, raise the temperature to 200°C and roast for another 30-40 minutes, turning the potatoes, until the meat and potatoes are nicely browned.
Resting: Remove the pan from the oven and let the meat rest for 10 minutes before carving, so the juices settle.
Serving: Serve the lamb carved into portions together with the potatoes, and drizzle with the pan juices.
arni_fournou_patates.wine: Xinomavro from Naoussa or another full-bodied dry red wine.
arni_fournou_patates.plate: Serve on a plate with boiled greens or Greek village salad and fresh bread to enjoy with the pan juices.

steps: Preparing the meat: Pat the beef dry well with paper towels and pierce it in several places with a sharp knife to stuff the holes with garlic.
Marinating: Make a mixture of olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper and rub the meat well on all sides.
Searing the meat: Important: First sear the beef over high heat in a pot with a little oil until well browned on all sides, so the pores 'close' and the meat retains its juices during roasting.
Placing in the pan: Put the meat in a baking pan, add the bay leaves and water or stock, cover tightly with foil and roast in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 1.5-2 hours.
Adding the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut them into slices or chunks, season with salt, pepper, oregano and oil, and add them around the meat halfway through roasting.
Final roasting: Remove the foil for the last 30 minutes and raise the temperature to 200°C to brown the meat and potatoes, basting regularly with the pan juices.
Resting the meat: Important: Once out of the oven, let the beef rest covered for 10-15 minutes before carving, so the juices redistribute and it stays juicy.
Serving: Slice the meat against the grain and serve with the potatoes and the pan sauce on top.
mosxari_fournou_patates.wine: Xinomavro from Naoussa or another full-bodied dry red wine.
mosxari_fournou_patates.plate: Serve on a platter with the potatoes around the meat and plenty of sauce on top, accompanied by Greek village salad.

steps: Preparing the stuffing: Sauté the onion in a little olive oil until softened, add the ground beef and sauté until browned.
Adding the rice: Add the rice, chestnuts, raisins and pine nuts, mix well and deglaze with a little hot water or stock, cooking for 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Seasoning the stuffing: Add cinnamon, allspice, salt and pepper and let the stuffing cool completely before stuffing the chicken.

Important: The stuffing must be completely cold and the rice only half-cooked, since it will finish cooking inside the chicken, absorbing the meat's juices; if you stuff the chicken with hot filling you risk bacterial growth, while too much rice will swell and split the cavity.
Stuffing the chicken: Wash the chicken well, pat it dry and fill the cavity with the stuffing up to about 3/4 full, then sew the opening closed with kitchen string or seal it with toothpicks.

Basting and roasting: Season the chicken with salt and pepper on the outside, drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, and roast in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 2 hours, turning and basting it regularly with its own juices.
Checking doneness: The chicken is ready when you pierce the thigh and the juices run clear with no trace of blood, and the skin has turned golden and crisp.
Serving: Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before carving, so the juices redistribute, and serve it together with the stuffing.
kotopoulo_gemisto.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, crisp and with lively acidity that balances the richness of the meat.
kotopoulo_gemisto.plate: Serve carved into portions on a platter, with the stuffing alongside, accompanied by a green salad and a little lemon.

steps: Preparing the meat: Trim any silver skin from the pork tenderloin and let it come to room temperature for 20-30 minutes before cooking.
Marinade: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, mustard, honey, lemon, finely chopped garlic, thyme, salt and pepper.
Coating: Rub the meat well with the marinade on all sides and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes, ideally 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Important: First sear the meat over high heat in a non-stick or cast-iron pan for 1-2 minutes per side, so the pores close and it stays juicy, before putting it in the oven.
Roasting: Place the meat in a baking pan, pour over the wine and any remaining marinade, and roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes.
Checking doneness: Check the internal temperature with a meat thermometer — it should reach 63-65°C to stay tender and juicy without drying out.
Resting: Remove the tenderloin from the oven, cover it loosely with foil and let it rest for 8-10 minutes before slicing, so the juices redistribute.
Serving: Slice the meat on the diagonal and drizzle with the pan sauce.
psaronefri_fournou.wine: Dry white wine from Assyrtiko of Santorini or a light red Agiorgitiko.
psaronefri_fournou.plate: Serve with mashed potatoes or oregano-roasted potatoes and a fresh Greek village salad.

ing: Salt, pepper, fresh coriander for garnish
steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the chicken breast into medium cubes and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Sautéing the base: In a deep pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onion over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 6-7 minutes.
Aromatics: Add the garlic and ginger and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Important: Cook the curry powder in the oil for 1-2 minutes before adding any liquids, so the essential oils in the spices wake up and the final dish doesn't taste of raw powder.
Cooking the chicken: Add the chicken to the pot and sauté until the surface turns lightly white, then add the tomato paste and stir.
Simmering: Pour in the coconut milk, lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 15-18 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chicken is fully cooked.
Cooking the rice: Meanwhile, boil the basmati rice in salted water according to the package instructions, drain it and let it sit covered for a few minutes to fluff up.
Serving: Taste and adjust the salt and pepper, serve the curry over the rice and garnish with fresh coriander.
kotopoulo_kari.wine: A crisp off-dry white Moschofilero or a lager-style beer pairs beautifully with the curry spices.
kotopoulo_kari.plate: Serve in a deep plate with the rice as a base, the curry on top, and a little fresh coriander or parsley for color.

ing: Fresh cleaned sea bass 2 (about 600 g each)
steps: Preparing the fish: Clean the sea bass of scales and innards, rinse well under cold water and dry very thoroughly with paper towels, inside and out.
Stuffing: Fill the cavity of each fish with lemon slices, a garlic clove cut in half, and a little parsley to flavor it from the inside.
Seasoning: Season the fish with salt and pepper on the outside and make 2-3 diagonal cuts on the thickest part of the body so it cooks evenly through to the bone.
Important: The grill must be very well preheated and clean, and lightly oiled before placing the fish on it, so the skin doesn't stick and stays intact when you turn it.
Grilling: Grill the sea bass over medium-high heat for about 6-8 minutes per side, depending on size, without moving it too often so a nice crust forms.
Checking doneness: The fish is ready when the flesh near the bone is white and opaque and comes away easily with a fork.
Lemon-oil dressing: Mix the olive oil with the lemon juice, chopped parsley and oregano, and drizzle it over the fish as soon as it comes off the grill.
Serving: Serve immediately while hot, whole or filleted at the table, with the lemon-oil dressing on the side.
lavraki_sxaras.wine: White Assyrtiko wine from Santorini, crisp and dry, which highlights the delicacy of the fish.
lavraki_sxaras.plate: Serve the sea bass whole on a platter with lemon slices and sprigs of parsley, accompanied by boiled greens or Greek village salad and roast potatoes.

ing: Fresh mussels in the shell 500 g
steps: Cleaning the seafood: Peel the shrimp, keeping a few in the shell for garnish, scrub the mussels well and cut the squid into rings.
Stock: Prepare hot fish or seafood stock and keep it over low heat so you can gradually add hot liquid to the rice.
Sautéing the seafood: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and quickly sauté the squid, shrimp and mussels for 2-3 minutes until the mussels open, then remove them and set aside.
Sautéing the rice: In the same oil, sauté the onion and garlic until softened, add the rice and stir for 1-2 minutes until it turns glossy.

Important: Deglaze with the white wine and wait for the alcohol to evaporate, then add the hot stock gradually, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next — this is the secret to a creamy risotto.
Tomato: Halfway through cooking, add the grated tomato for color and flavor, and continue the slow simmer.
Finishing: When the rice is al dente (about 17-18 minutes total), return the seafood to the pot, add the lemon juice and parsley, stir gently and remove from heat.
Serving: Let the risotto rest covered for 2 minutes before serving, so it sets to a better creamy consistency.
rizoto_thalassinon.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko wine from Santorini, crisp and mineral.
rizoto_thalassinon.plate: Serve in a deep plate, garnished with a whole shrimp, fresh parsley and a lemon wedge on the side.

ing: Fresh or frozen cleaned squid 1 kg
steps: Cleaning: If the squid aren't already cleaned, remove the quill, innards and ink sac, rinse well under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.
Scoring: Lightly score the squid bodies in a diamond pattern with a knife, without cutting all the way through, so they cook evenly and become more tender.
Marinating: In a bowl, mix half the olive oil, the juice of one lemon, the garlic, oregano and pepper, pour it over the squid and let them marinate for 20-30 minutes at room temperature.

Important: Squid should be cooked either over very high heat for a very short time (2-3 minutes per side), or very slowly for a long time; the in-between cooking time makes them rubbery, so the grill must be scorching hot before you add the squid.
Grilling: Pat the squid lightly dry of marinade and place them on a very hot grill or griddle, cooking for 2-3 minutes per side until golden with light char marks, without drying out.
Salting: Salt the squid only after grilling, never before, because salt draws out moisture and toughens it during cooking.
Oiling: As soon as they come off the grill, drizzle them with the remaining olive oil and the juice of the second lemon while still hot, so they absorb the flavors.
Serving: Sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve immediately, hot, with lemon on the side.
kalamaria_sxaras.wine: White Assyrtiko wine from Santorini, crisp and dry, or ouzo on ice.
kalamaria_sxaras.plate: Serve on a plate with lemon slices and sprigs of parsley, accompanied by Greek village salad and fresh bread.

ing: Fresh or dried potato gnocchi 500 g
Ripe or canned chopped tomatoes 800 g
Grated Parmesan or kefalotyri cheese 60 g
steps: Preparing the sauce: Finely chop the onion and garlic. In a saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the onion until softened, about 4-5 minutes.
Adding the garlic: Add the garlic and sauté for just 1 minute, so it doesn't turn bitter.
Tomato: Add the chopped tomatoes, a pinch of sugar to balance the acidity, salt and pepper. Simmer over low heat for 20-25 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

Important: The gnocchi must be boiled in plenty of salted water that's already at a rolling boil. Drop them in and remove them IMMEDIATELY as soon as they float to the surface (30-90 seconds), because if they stay longer they fall apart and lose their texture.
Draining: Drain the gnocchi with a slotted spoon, keeping a little of the cooking water to thin the sauce if needed.
Combining: Add the gnocchi to the tomato sauce and stir gently over low heat for 1-2 minutes so they take on flavor without falling apart.
Basil: Turn off the heat and add the fresh basil torn by hand, so it keeps its aroma.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, sprinkled with grated Parmesan or kefalotyri and a drizzle of olive oil.
gnocchi_tomata.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko wine or a light rosé.
gnocchi_tomata.plate: Serve in a deep plate with fresh basil on top and grated cheese on the side, accompanied by freshly baked bread.

steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the chicken breast into small cubes or strips and season with salt and pepper.
Sautéing the chicken: In a large pan, heat the olive oil over high heat and sauté the chicken until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Mushrooms: In the same pan, add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened, then add the sliced mushrooms. Important: Don't stir the mushrooms constantly at first; let them sit undisturbed for a few minutes so they caramelize and release their liquid instead of just boiling.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the white wine and let the alcohol evaporate over high heat for 2 minutes.
Pasta: Meanwhile, boil the penne in plenty of salted water until al dente, according to the package instructions, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Combining the ingredients: Return the chicken to the pan with the mushrooms, add the heavy cream and simmer for 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Finishing: Drain the penne and add them to the pan, mixing well with the sauce, adding a little of the cooking water if needed for a creamier texture. Add the Parmesan and stir until melted.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, sprinkled with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.
pennes_kotopoulo_manitaria.wine: White Assyrtiko wine or a light Chardonnay pair excellently with the creamy sauce.
pennes_kotopoulo_manitaria.plate: Serve in a deep plate with grated Parmesan and fresh parsley on top, accompanied by fresh bread.

ing: Fresh dill, finely chopped, 1 small bunch
steps: Preparing the salmon: Cut the salmon fillet into medium cubes, removing any bones and skin, and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Sautéing the base: In a wide pan, heat the olive oil with the butter and sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic over low heat until softened, without letting them color.
Cooking the salmon: Add the salmon cubes to the pan and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they change color on the outside, turning them gently so they don't break apart.
Important: Deglaze with the white wine and let the alcohol evaporate completely over high heat for 1-2 minutes; if the wine doesn't evaporate properly, the sauce will keep a bitter, sharp taste.
Making the sauce: Lower the heat, add the cream and stir gently, letting it simmer for 4-5 minutes until it thickens slightly, without boiling hard so it doesn't split.
Boiling the pasta: Meanwhile, boil the pasta in plenty of salted water until al dente, according to the package instructions, and reserve a little of the cooking water.

Combining and serving: Drain the pasta and toss it into the pan with the sauce, adding the fresh dill and a little of the cooking water if needed to loosen it. Stir gently, sprinkle with Parmesan and serve immediately.
pasta_solomos_anithos.wine: A cool, crisp dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, with bright acidity that balances the creamy sauce
pasta_solomos_anithos.plate: Serve in a deep plate, garnished with a little fresh dill and a lemon wedge on the side

ing: Grated tomato, 2 tbsp (tomato paste) or 1 fresh tomato
steps: Pre-cooking the lentils: Wash the lentils well and boil them in plenty of water with the bay leaves for 12-15 minutes, until softened but not completely falling apart.
Sautéing the onion: In a pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the sliced onions until well golden, together with the garlic.
Combining the ingredients: Add the tomato paste to the onions, stir for a minute and add the half-cooked lentils along with a little of their cooking broth.

Important: The ratio of liquid is the secret of fakorizo - the rice must cook in lentil broth rather than plain water, since that's how it takes on all the flavor and color of the pulses. You need roughly double the amount of liquid to rice.
Adding the rice: Add the rice to the pot, season with salt and pepper, and top up with hot water or broth so the mixture is well covered.
Slow simmering: Lower the heat, cover the pot and let it simmer gently for 15-18 minutes, until the rice has absorbed all the liquid.
Resting: Remove from the heat and let the dish rest covered for 5-10 minutes before serving, so the cooking finishes with the residual steam.
Serving: Serve hot, drizzling with a little vinegar or lemon juice on the plate according to each person's preference.
fakoryzo.wine: A dry white wine, such as Assyrtiko, or plain tsipouro pairs perfectly with the flavor of fakorizo.
fakoryzo.plate: Serve in a deep plate with finely chopped onion, Kalamata olives and feta on the side, accompanied by vinegar.

ing: Water or vegetable broth as needed
steps: Soaking: Place the chickpeas in plenty of water overnight so they swell and soften before boiling.
Boiling the chickpeas: Drain the chickpeas and boil them in fresh water with the bay leaf for about 45-60 minutes, until softened but still holding their shape. Reserve the cooking broth.
Important: Do not add salt to the boiling water from the start, as it toughens the chickpea skins and delays softening; season with salt only toward the end of cooking.
Sofrito: In a pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onion until glossy, add the garlic for a minute and then the grated tomato, simmering for 5-6 minutes.
Combining: Add the cooked chickpeas to the sofrito along with a little of the cooking broth and let everything come to a boil together so the flavors meld.

Adding the rice: Add the rice and top up with broth or water in a ratio of roughly double the rice, season with salt and pepper, and simmer over low heat with the lid half-open until the liquid is absorbed, about 18-20 minutes.
Resting: Turn off the heat, cover the pot and let the dish rest for 10 minutes so the rice finishes cooking in the steam.
Serving: Drizzle generously with fresh lemon juice and raw olive oil before serving hot.
revithoryzo.wine: Dry white wine from Rhodes or Assyrtiko from Santorini
revithoryzo.plate: Serve in a deep plate with a lemon wedge on the side and a little fresh oregano sprinkled on top

ing: Seasonal greens (amaranth, dandelion greens, nettles or sow thistle) 1.5 kg
steps: Trimming: Separate the greens from the tough stalks and any yellow or damaged leaves, keeping only the tender parts.
Washing: Wash the greens in plenty of water, through 3-4 changes, as they often hide soil and grit between the leaves.
Important: Boil in plenty of boiling salted water, uncovered, so the greens keep their natural green color and lose their bitterness, especially if using dandelion greens or nettles.
Cooking time: Let them boil for 15-25 minutes depending on the type and tenderness of the greens, until softened but not mushy.
Draining: Drain the greens well in a colander, pressing gently to remove excess water.
Serving: Spread them on a platter and drizzle generously with olive oil and fresh lemon juice.
Final touch: Add salt and pepper to taste and serve warm or at room temperature, never cold from the fridge, so their flavor comes through.
xorta_vrasta.wine: Chilled retsina or dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini
xorta_vrasta.plate: Serve on an earthenware platter alongside grilled fish or feta and olives, with plenty of olive oil and lemon on the table

steps: Preparation: Wash all the vegetables well and pat them dry. Slice the eggplants and zucchini lengthwise into slices about 1 cm thick, halve the peppers and remove the seeds, and cut the onions into thick rounds, holding them together with a toothpick so they don't fall apart on the grill.
Salting the eggplant: Salt the eggplant slices lightly and let them sit in a colander for 15-20 minutes to release their bitter moisture, then pat them dry with paper towels.

Important: The grill must be well lit and the coals turned to white ash before adding the vegetables, so they cook evenly and take on that characteristic smoky flavor without burning outside while staying raw inside.
Oiling: Brush all the cut vegetables with olive oil using a pastry brush and sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper just before grilling.

Grilling: Place the vegetables on the grill starting with those that need more time, such as the peppers and onions, then add the eggplant, zucchini and tomatoes. Turn them with tongs at regular intervals so they cook on all sides and get nice grill marks.
Finishing the cooking: The vegetables are ready when they've softened and developed slightly browned, caramelized edges, usually within 8-15 minutes depending on the type and thickness.
Serving: Arrange the warm vegetables on a platter, drizzle with fresh lemon juice and a generous stream of olive oil, sprinkle with oregano and serve immediately.
laxanika_sxaras.wine: Pairs well with a white Assyrtiko or a cool rosé.
laxanika_sxaras.plate: Served on a platter with feta and fresh bread, as a side dish or main course.

ing: Fresh dill or parsley, 1 small bunch
steps: Preparing the zucchini: Wash the zucchini, trim the ends and cut them into thick rounds or lengthwise into four pieces, depending on their size.
Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion over medium heat until softened and glossy, without coloring.
Adding garlic and tomato: Add the garlic for a minute, then the grated tomatoes. Let it simmer briefly to mellow the acidity.
Important: Do not add water at the start; the zucchini release their own liquid when cooked covered over low heat, which is why the stew stays thick and flavorful without becoming watery.
Adding the zucchini: Place the zucchini in the pot, season with salt and pepper, stir gently so they're coated with the sauce, and cover.
Slow cooking: Cook over low heat for 30-40 minutes without stirring often, so the zucchini stay whole and don't fall apart.
Final touches: Toward the end, add the sugar if needed for balance and the chopped dill or parsley. Let the sauce thicken a little more with the lid half-open.
Serving: Let the dish rest for 10 minutes before serving, so the flavors meld together better.
kolokythakia_giaxni.wine: A light white wine, such as Assyrtiko or Moschofilero, well chilled.
kolokythakia_giaxni.plate: Serve hot with feta and fresh bread to mop up the sauce.

steps: Cleaning the fish: Clean the fish, rinse well and cut into portions, keeping the heads and bones for a richer broth.
Preparing the vegetables: Peel and cut the potatoes into thick slices, the carrots into rounds, the onions into slices, and finely chop the celery.
Boiling the broth: Place the vegetables, olive oil, salt and pepper in a large pot, cover with water and boil over medium heat for 20 minutes until softened.
Adding the fish: Gently add the fish pieces into the pot and continue boiling for another 15-20 minutes, without stirring vigorously so the fish doesn't break apart.
Important: The secret to kakavia is slow simmering over low heat without stirring with a spoon; just shake the pot by its handles so the fish doesn't fall apart and the broth stays clear.
Removing the fish and vegetables: Carefully remove the fish and vegetables onto a platter and keep them warm, keeping the broth in the pot.

Egg-lemon sauce (avgolemono): Beat the eggs with the lemon juice and gradually add a little hot broth while whisking constantly, so it doesn't curdle; then pour it back into the pot, stirring gently over very low heat until it thickens slightly.
Serving: Serve the broth with the avgolemono first in deep plates, followed by the fish and vegetables on a separate platter or together, with plenty of olive oil and lemon on top.
kakavia.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool and mineral, an ideal match for seafood.
kakavia.plate: Serve in a deep stoneware or white plate, with the egg-lemon broth first and the fish and vegetables alongside, accompanied by fresh village bread and olives.

ing: Heavy cream 100 ml (or almond milk for a fasting/vegan version)
Breadcrumbs or dried dill, for garnish
steps: Preparing the vegetables: Peel and slice the carrots into rounds, finely chop the onion and leek, and cut the potato into cubes.
Sautéing: In a pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the onion and leek for 4-5 minutes until softened, without coloring.
Adding the carrots: Add the carrots and potato to the pot and stir for 2-3 minutes so they pick up flavor from the oil.
Boiling: Pour in the broth until the vegetables are covered, add salt and pepper, and simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Important: The long, slow simmering is essential so the carrots break down easily when puréed and the soup comes out velvety with no lumps; check with a fork before proceeding.
Puréeing: Remove from the heat and purée with an immersion blender until smooth and creamy, adding a little broth if it's too thick.
Enriching with cream: Return the pot to low heat, add the cream and ginger, stir well and simmer for 5 minutes without letting it boil.
Serving: Serve hot in deep plates, garnishing with a drizzle of olive oil and toasted breadcrumbs or dill.
krema_karotou.wine: A fresh white Assyrtiko or a light Moschofilero pairs ideally with the sweetness of the carrot.
krema_karotou.plate: Serve in deep plates with a swirl of olive oil and a little fresh village bread on the side.

ing: Gruyère or Emmental cheese 120 g, grated
steps: Preparing the ingredients: Cut the ham into small cubes and grate the cheese, so they're ready for quick cooking.
Beating the eggs: In a bowl, crack the eggs and beat well with the milk, salt and pepper until combined and slightly frothy.
Heating the pan: Put the butter with the olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat until the butter melts without burning.
Important: Pour the egg into the pan and immediately lower the heat to very low; the omelet must cook slowly so it stays fluffy and moist, without the base burning.
Adding the filling: As soon as the surface starts to set, scatter the ham and cheese evenly over one half of the omelet.
Folding: With a spatula, fold the other half over the filling, forming a half-moon shape, and continue cooking over low heat for 2-3 more minutes so the cheese melts.
Finishing: Briefly cover the pan with a lid to help the cheese melt fully inside the filling.
Serving: Transfer the omelet to a plate, sprinkle with fresh parsley and serve immediately, hot.
omeleta_zampon_tyri.wine: Pairs well with a cool white Assyrtiko or a glass of fresh orange juice.
omeleta_zampon_tyri.plate: Serve with toasted bread, tomato slices and a seasonal green salad.

ing: Chicken thigh fillet 700 g, cut into bite-sized pieces
Red and green peppers, 3, cut into strips
