Grated tomato or tomato juice 3 tbsp
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the thigh fillet into 3-4 cm pieces and pat dry well with paper towels so it browns properly.

Frying the chicken: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan or wok over high heat and add the chicken pieces. Important: Don't overcrowd the pan - fry in batches if needed, so the meat sears and browns instead of stewing in its own juices.
Browning: Let the chicken brown well on all sides, about 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Adding the vegetables: Add the onion and peppers to the pan and sauté for 4-5 minutes until slightly softened while still keeping some crunch.
Garlic and deglazing with wine: Add the garlic, stir for 30 seconds and deglaze with the white wine, letting the alcohol evaporate.
Tomato and cooking: Add the grated tomato, oregano, salt and pepper. Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Final check: Taste and adjust the salt, making sure the chicken is cooked through without drying out.
Serving: Serve piping hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice on top, accompanied by fried potatoes or pilaf rice.
kotopoulo_tigania.wine: Dry white wine from Crete, such as Vidiano, cool and aromatic
kotopoulo_tigania.plate: Served on a plate with fried potatoes or pilaf rice, accompanied by a Greek village salad

steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the fillet into 2-3 cm pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Coating: Beat the egg and dip the chicken pieces in it, then roll them in cornstarch so they're well coated.
Important: Fry in hot oil (180°C) in two batches so you don't drop the oil temperature; this keeps the chicken crispy outside and juicy inside, without absorbing excess oil.
Vegetables: In a wok or large pan, sauté the sliced onion and peppers for 3-4 minutes over high heat, so they stay crunchy.
Sauce: In a bowl, mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, ketchup and a little pineapple juice until well combined.
Combining: Pour the sauce into the pan with the vegetables, add the pineapple and simmer for 2-3 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Final mixing: Add the fried chicken to the sauce and stir gently for 1-2 minutes so it's evenly coated without the coating going soft.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, over white rice.
kotopoulo_glykoksino.wine: White Moschofilero wine, cool and aromatic
kotopoulo_glykoksino.plate: Served in a deep plate over steamed white rice, with a little fresh chopped spring onion on top

ing: Bread crumb, soaked in milk, 2 slices
Grated tomato or tomato juice 800 g
steps: Preparing the mince: In a bowl, mix the two ground meats with the onion, garlic, egg, the soaked and squeezed bread crumb, mint, salt and pepper until well combined.
Resting: Cover the mixture with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes, so the flavors meld and the mixture firms up.
Shaping: Shape small round meatballs with wet hands and lightly coat them with flour, shaking off the excess.
Important: Frying must be done in well-heated oil so the surface of the meatballs seals immediately; this way they don't absorb oil and keep their juices inside, staying moist.
Frying: Fry the meatballs in batches over medium-high heat until browned on all sides, about 4-5 minutes, then drain on paper towels.
Sauce: In another pot, heat a little olive oil, add the grated tomato, a pinch of sugar to cut the acidity, salt and pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Combining: Add the fried meatballs to the sauce and let them simmer together for 15-20 minutes over low heat, so they take on the flavor of the sauce.
Serving: Remove from the heat and let stand a few minutes before serving hot.
keftedakia_saltsas.plate: Serve the meatballs with plenty of sauce over mashed potatoes or with fried potato slices and a piece of feta on the side

ing: Sugar 1 tsp (to offset the tomato's acidity)
steps: Desalting: If using salt cod, soak it in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water 3-4 times, so the excess salt is removed. Important: Taste a small bite before cooking; if it's still very salty, soak it for a few more hours, otherwise the dish will come out unbearably salty.
Preparing the vegetables: Peel and slice the onions thinly and finely chop the garlic. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick rounds or wedges.
Sautéing: In a wide pot, heat half the olive oil and sauté the onions over low heat until softened and glossy, without coloring. Add the garlic for a minute.
Tomato sauce: Add the grated tomatoes, bay leaf, sugar, salt and pepper and let the sauce simmer for 15-20 minutes until it thickens and the excess moisture cooks off.

Layering in the pan: Spread the potatoes over the bottom of a baking pan, season lightly with salt and pepper (less if the cod is salty) and pour over a little sauce. Place the cod pieces on top, skin-side down.

Baking: Cover with the remaining tomato sauce, drizzle with the rest of the olive oil and bake in a preheated oven at 190°C for 40-45 minutes, until the potatoes soften and the sauce caramelizes slightly at the edges. Important: Do not cover the pan with foil for the whole baking time, so the sauce reduces and develops depth of flavor.
Serving: Let the dish stand for 5-10 minutes out of the oven, sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley and serve hot.
bakaliaros_plaki.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini or well-chilled retsina
bakaliaros_plaki.plate: Serve on an earthenware plate with a slice of local bread to mop up the sauce and a little fresh cabbage-and-carrot salad on the side

steps: Preparing the marinade: In a bowl, mix the olive oil, mustard, honey, lemon, thyme, paprika, grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Marinating: Rub the turkey fillet well with the marinade on all sides and let it sit in the fridge for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, so it soaks up the flavors.
Preheating: Preheat the oven to 200°C, fan setting.
Placing in the pan: Put the fillet in a pan lined with parchment paper, pour over the wine and cover loosely with foil.
Baking: Bake for 25 minutes covered, then remove the foil and continue for another 20-25 minutes until the surface browns.
Important: Check the internal temperature with a meat thermometer - it must reach 74°C at the thickest point, so the meat is fully cooked without drying out.
Resting: Remove the fillet from the oven and let it rest covered for 10 minutes before slicing, so it retains its juices.
Serving: Slice and serve with the pan juices drizzled on top.
filero_galopoulas_fournou.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko or a light red Xinomavro
filero_galopoulas_fournou.plate: Served with mashed potatoes or roasted vegetables and a seasonal salad

ing: Fresh or frozen cuttlefish 1.2 kg (with their ink)
steps: Cleaning: Clean the cuttlefish, removing the cuttlebone, innards and eye, carefully setting aside the ink sacs in a bowl with a little water. Cut the cuttlefish into slices or pieces.
Sautéing the onion: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onions over low heat until softened and glossy, about 10-12 minutes, stirring often so they don't darken.
Adding the cuttlefish: Add the garlic and cuttlefish to the pot and sear over high heat for 5-6 minutes until they change color and release their liquid.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the white wine and let the alcohol evaporate for 2-3 minutes, then add the tomato paste, bay leaves, salt and pepper.

Important: Cuttlefish need slow, gentle simmering to become tender without turning rubbery; depending on their size they need 45-60 minutes over low heat with the pot covered, adding a little hot water if the liquid runs low.
Adding the ink: Shortly before the cooking finishes, dissolve the cuttlefish ink in a little of the cooking liquid and add it to the pot, stirring well so the sauce takes on a deep black color.
Final simmer: Let it simmer uncovered for another 10-15 minutes until the sauce thickens and takes on a velvety texture, adjusting the salt and pepper.
Serving: Serve the cuttlefish hot, sprinkled with chopped parsley, accompanied by white rice or pasta that will soak up the ink sauce.
soupies_melani.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool and mineral.
soupies_melani.plate: Served on a shallow plate over white rice or small pasta, with fresh parsley and a lemon wedge on the side.

steps: Preparing the octopus: Rinse the octopus well and beat it lightly to tenderize its fibers, if it's fresh.
Important: If the octopus is fresh, it's best to freeze it for 24 hours first and then thaw it, as freezing breaks down its fibers and makes it more tender without needing to beat it.
Slow cooking: Place the octopus in a pot without water, over medium heat, covered, and let it cook in its own juices for 35-45 minutes until tender, turning it occasionally.
Soaking the beans: The day before, soak the gigantes beans in plenty of cold water for at least 10-12 hours.
Boiling the beans: Drain the beans and boil them in lightly salted water for 40-50 minutes until softened but still holding their shape, then drain.
Sautéing: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion until softened, add the garlic and deglaze with the vinegar.

Combining the ingredients: Add the grated tomato, bay leaves, rosemary, the octopus cut into pieces, and the beans, season lightly with salt and pepper (being mindful of the octopus's saltiness) and simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Serving: Let the dish rest a few minutes before serving hot, so the beans absorb the flavors well.
xtapodi_gigantes.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool and mineral
xtapodi_gigantes.plate: Serve in a deep plate with a fan of fresh village bread and a drizzle of olive oil on top

steps: Preparing the spinach: Wash the spinach well, sauté it in a little olive oil for 2-3 minutes until wilted, drain and chop it finely.
Sautéing the base: In a wide pot, heat the olive oil with a little butter and sauté the onion over low heat until translucent, without coloring. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Toasting the rice: Add the rice to the pot and stir for 1-2 minutes until the grains turn glossy and become translucent at the edges. Important: This step seals the grain and helps the rice keep the right al dente texture without turning mushy during cooking.
Deglazing with wine: Add the white wine and stir until the alcohol evaporates and is absorbed by the rice.

Gradually adding the broth: Add the hot broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Important: Constant stirring releases the rice's starch and creates the creamy texture that defines risotto, so don't rush it or leave it unattended.
Incorporating the spinach: In the last 5 minutes of cooking, add the chopped spinach and stir so it's evenly incorporated into the risotto.

Mantecatura: When the rice is al dente, remove from the heat and add the remaining butter, the Parmesan and the crumbled feta, stirring vigorously until creamy. Let it stand covered for 2 minutes before serving.
Serving: Serve immediately in warm plates with a little extra grated feta and olive oil on top.
rizoto_spanaki_feta.wine: White Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool with bright acidity that balances the creamy texture of the risotto.
rizoto_spanaki_feta.plate: Serve in a deep plate, spreading the risotto lightly with the back of a spoon, with grated feta, a little freshly ground pepper and a drizzle of olive oil in the center.

ing: Gruyère or Emmental cheese, grated, 100 g
steps: Boiling the chicken: Boil the chicken fillets in lightly salted water for 15-18 minutes until softened, drain and let cool.
Making the béchamel: Melt the butter in a pot, add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes over low heat so the raw flour taste cooks off. Gradually pour in the hot milk, whisking.

Important: The béchamel must be very thick, almost paste-like, so it holds its shape when cold and doesn't melt during frying. Simmer over low heat, stirring constantly, until well thickened, about 10 minutes.
Enriching the sauce: Remove from the heat, add the grated cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper, stir to incorporate, and let the béchamel cool completely, preferably in the fridge for 1-2 hours.
Assembling: Slice the chicken, place a slice of ham between two chicken slices and spread the cold, thick béchamel generously over the whole surface as a coating.

Coating: Dip each piece first in the beaten egg and then in the breadcrumbs, pressing well so they stick all over. Repeat the egg-and-breadcrumb process for a double coating, so the crust doesn't break during frying.

Frying: Heat plenty of oil over medium-high heat and fry the pieces until evenly browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side, so the béchamel inside warms through without melting and leaking out.
Serving: Drain on paper towels and serve immediately, hot, while the crust is still crispy.
kotopoulo_vigeroua.wine: Dry white wine, Assyrtiko from Santorini or a light Roditis
kotopoulo_vigeroua.plate: Serve with mashed potatoes or cabbage-and-carrot salad and a little lemony mayonnaise on the side

ing: Hard-boiled eggs, 5 (4 for the filling, 1 for the meat mixture)
Bread crumb, soaked in milk, 2 slices
steps: Preparing the mince: In a large bowl, mix the ground beef and pork with the grated onion, garlic, bread crumb (well squeezed), cheese, parsley, one egg, salt, pepper and oregano until all ingredients are combined.
Boiling the eggs: Boil the 4 eggs in salted water for 9-10 minutes, transfer them immediately into ice water and peel carefully so they stay whole and smooth.
Spreading the mince: On a sheet of parchment paper, spread the meat mixture into a rectangular layer about 1.5 cm thick.

Important: Place the boiled eggs at one edge, in a row, side by side, and roll the meat tightly around them using the parchment paper, like a roulade, pressing well so there are no gaps and the eggs don't break during baking.
Sealing: Firmly close the seams and ends of the roll with your hands, so the filling doesn't leak out during baking, and carefully transfer it to a baking pan.
Baking: Drizzle the roll with olive oil, add a little water to the pan and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 50-60 minutes, turning it once, until evenly browned.
Resting and slicing: Let the roll rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing, so it firms up and cuts cleanly, revealing the eggs in the center.
Serving: Serve the slices hot with the pan juices on top, accompanied by mashed potatoes or risotto.
rolo_kima_avga.plate: Serve sliced over mashed potatoes with the pan juices, accompanied by a seasonal salad

ing: Chili flakes or hot pepper 1/2 tsp
steps: Preparing the lobster: Boil the lobster in salted water for 8-10 minutes until the shell turns red, let it cool and carefully remove the meat from the tail and claws, keeping the shell for the stock.
Lobster stock: Sauté the shells in a little olive oil for 5 minutes until fragrant, deglaze with a little water and simmer for 15 minutes, then strain and reserve the stock.
Sauce: In a wide pot, sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until softened, deglaze with the wine and let the alcohol evaporate.

Important: Add the grated tomato and the lobster stock and simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes uncovered, so the sauce thickens and the flavors concentrate - slow simmering is the secret to a deep taste of the sea.
Boiling the pasta: Boil the linguine in plenty of salted water until al dente, reserving half a glass of the cooking water.
Combining: Add the lobster meat, cut into pieces, to the sauce and warm through for 2-3 minutes without boiling hard, so the meat doesn't toughen.
Finishing: Add the drained pasta to the sauce, toss well, adding a little pasta water if needed, and serve immediately with parsley and chili flakes.
Serving: Divide among warm plates, placing the whole claws on top for an impressive presentation.
astakomakaronada.wine: White Assyrtiko from Santorini, cool and mineral, brings out the sweetness of the lobster.
astakomakaronada.plate: Serve in a deep white plate with the lobster claws on top, a little fresh parsley and a lemon wedge on the side.

ing: Unsalted butter 120 g, at room temperature
steps: Preparing the butter: Mix the softened butter with the chopped garlic, parsley, salt and pepper until well combined. Wrap the mixture in parchment paper into a cylinder shape and freeze for 30-40 minutes until firm.

Opening the fillets: Cut each chicken breast horizontally almost all the way through, open it like a book, and gently pound it between two sheets of plastic wrap until it has an even thickness of about 0.5 cm.
Filling: Cut the cold butter into 4 cylinder-shaped pieces. Place one piece in the center of each fillet and roll the meat tightly around it, sealing all the edges well so the butter cannot leak out.

Important: Sealing the chicken tightly around the butter is the most critical step - if even a small gap remains, the melted butter will leak out during frying. For extra security, freeze the wrapped rolls for 20-30 minutes before breading.

Breading: Dip each roll first in flour, then in the beaten egg, and finally in the breadcrumbs, pressing gently so they adhere well. Repeat the egg-and-breadcrumb step for a double coating and a better seal.
Chilling before frying: Place the breaded rolls in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes so the coating sets and the butter stays frozen.

Frying: Heat plenty of sunflower oil to 170°C in a deep pan. Fry the rolls for 5-6 minutes, turning them, until evenly golden, then finish them in a preheated oven at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, so the chicken cooks through without burning the coating.
Serving: Let the Chicken Kiev rest for 2-3 minutes before cutting so the butter doesn't spill out all at once, and serve immediately while hot.
kotopoulo_kiev.wine: Pairs well with a crisp white Assyrtiko or a light dry rosé.
kotopoulo_kiev.plate: Serve with mashed or fried potatoes and a fresh seasonal salad.

steps: Puff pastry: Roll out the puff pastry sheet on parchment paper and prick it well with a fork so it doesn't puff up unevenly.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, placing a second sheet of parchment paper and a baking tray on top to keep it flat.
Important: The pastry must be baked all the way through and cooled completely before cutting, otherwise it will shatter badly and won't form clean layers.
Pastry cream: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar and cornstarch until pale.
Cooking the cream: Heat the milk with the vanilla and gradually add it to the mixture, stirring constantly over low heat until it thickens.
Finishing the cream: Remove from the heat, add the butter, stir, and cover with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Whipping the cream: Whip the heavy cream to soft peaks and gently fold it into the cooled pastry cream.
Assembly: Cut the pastry into three equal pieces and layer alternately: pastry-cream-pastry-cream-pastry.
Finishing: Dust the top with powdered sugar or decorate with melted chocolate drizzled in stripes.
Chilling: Let the mille-feuille chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting, so it sets properly.
milfey.plate: Serve cold on a platter, cut into square pieces, dusted with powdered sugar

ing: Almond extract (a few drops) for aroma
A few whole almonds, for decoration
steps: Preparing the almonds: Blanch the almonds, peel them, and grind them finely in a mill or food processor until they become almost flour-like.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, mix the ground almonds with the powdered sugar and lemon zest.
Whipping the egg whites: Whisk the egg whites with the granulated sugar until they form a meringue with a firm, glossy texture.
Combining the mixture: Gradually add the meringue to the almond mixture along with the orange blossom water and almond extract, gently kneading until the ingredients are well combined.
Important: The dough should be soft but not sticky to the touch; if it's too wet, add a little more powdered sugar, so the almond cookies hold their shape and don't spread during baking.
Shaping: Take small portions of dough and shape them into pears or crescents, placing an almond on top of each for decoration.
Baking: Place them on a parchment-lined baking tray and bake in a preheated oven at 150°C for 15-18 minutes, until lightly golden on the outside while staying soft inside.
Cooling and dusting: Let them cool completely and dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.
amygdalota.plate: Serve on a platter lined with doily paper, dusted with powdered sugar

ing: Oil for hands and parchment paper
steps: Toasting the sesame seeds: Spread the sesame seeds in a non-stick pan and toast over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant.
Preparing the surface: Line a baking tray or marble surface with parchment paper and brush lightly with oil.
Honey syrup: In a saucepan, combine the honey, sugar and water and boil over medium heat without stirring.

Important: The syrup must reach about 150°C (hard-ball stage) - drop a little into ice water, and if it forms a hard ball, the syrup is ready. If boiled less, the pasteli will stay soft; if boiled more, it will harden and turn bitter.
Mixing: Remove from the heat, immediately add the lemon juice, zest and cinnamon, and stir quickly.
Adding the sesame: Pour the toasted sesame seeds into the hot syrup and stir quickly with a wooden spoon until the mixture is homogeneous.
Spreading: Pour the mixture onto the oiled surface and, using an oiled rolling pin or your oiled palms, spread it into a layer about 1 cm thick before it cools and sets.
Cutting: While still warm, cut it into rectangles or diamonds with a knife; if it hardens too quickly, warm the knife slightly.
Cooling and storing: Let it cool completely at room temperature before peeling it off, and store in an airtight container.
pasteli.plate: Serve cut into small pieces on a platter, accompanied by Greek coffee

ing: Dark chocolate couverture for shavings 100 g
steps: Preparing the oven: Preheat to 180°C and butter two 22 cm cake pans.
Whipping the eggs: Whisk the eggs with the sugar over a slightly warmed bain-marie until tripled in volume and pale.
Mixing the dry ingredients: Sift the flour, cocoa and baking powder and gently fold them into the egg mixture with a spatula, using bottom-to-top motions to avoid deflating the batter.
Baking: Divide the batter between the pans and bake for 25-30 minutes. Important: Do not open the oven for the first 20 minutes, as a sudden draft will cause the sponge to sink and stay dense.
Cooling and slicing: Let the sponge cakes cool completely and slice each horizontally into 2-3 layers.
Soaking: Brush each layer with the cherry syrup mixed with the kirsch, so the cake becomes moist and aromatic.
Whipped cream: Whip the chilled heavy cream with the powdered sugar until firm. Important: The bowl and whisk must be very cold, otherwise the cream will curdle and fail to gain volume.
Layering: Spread whipped cream on each layer, scatter cherries over it, and repeat until the cake is assembled, finally covering the whole surface and sides.
Decoration: Cover with chocolate shavings, whole cherries and a little whipped cream on top, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours before serving.
black_forest.plate: Serve chilled in slices, with a spoonful of cherry sauce alongside and grated chocolate

ing: Hazelnuts, toasted and finely chopped, 150 g
steps: Base: Crush the biscuits in a food processor into crumbs and mix with the melted butter.
Layering: Spread the mixture into a springform pan, pressing down firmly with the back of a spoon, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to set.
Hydrating the gelatin: Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.
Hazelnut cream: Beat the cream cheese with the powdered sugar until fluffy, add the spread and mix well.

Important: Whip the heavy cream to soft peaks at a low speed in a chilled bowl, so it gains volume without curdling; fold it into the hazelnut mixture with gentle bottom-to-top motions to avoid losing air.
Gelatin: Melt the drained gelatin in a little warm cream and quickly stir it into the rest of the mixture so the cake sets evenly.
Filling: Spread the cream over the base, scattering chopped hazelnuts and pieces of praline chocolate in between for texture in every bite.
Chilling: Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight, so it sets well before unmolding.
Topping: Melt the milk chocolate over a bain-marie and pour it over the surface, decorating with whole praline chocolates and hazelnuts.
ferrero_torta.plate: Serve on a plate with a little chocolate sauce and a whole praline chocolate alongside each slice.

ing: Dark chocolate couverture (for the glaze) 150 g
steps: Preparation: Preheat the oven to 170°C and butter a 24 cm cake pan.
Melting the chocolate: Melt the couverture together with the butter over a bain-marie until combined.
Whisking the yolks: Whisk the egg yolks with half the sugar until pale, then fold in the melted chocolate.
Meringue: Whisk the egg whites with the salt until frothy, gradually adding the remaining sugar until a meringue forms.
Important: Fold the meringue into the chocolate mixture with gentle bottom-to-top motions, alternating with the sifted flour, so as not to lose air and to keep the cake light.
Baking: Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 40-45 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Let it cool completely.
Filling: Cut the cake into two layers and spread warmed apricot jam on one surface, join the layers together, and brush a thin layer of jam over the outside as well.
Glaze: Melt the glaze chocolate with the cream over a bain-marie until it becomes a smooth ganache, and cover the entire cake in one pour, letting it set in a cool place before serving.
sacher_torte.plate: Serve on a plate with a spoonful of whipped cream alongside and a light dusting of cinnamon around the edge

steps: Preheating: Heat the oven to 175°C and butter two 20 cm pans, lining the bottoms with parchment paper.
Dry ingredients: In a bowl, mix the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt.
Wet ingredients: In another bowl, whisk the oil with the sugar, add the eggs one at a time, then the buttermilk, red coloring, vinegar and vanilla.
Mixing: Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the wet ones, mixing gently until combined, without overworking the batter.
Important: Do not overmix the batter; overmixing develops the gluten and the cake will come out dense instead of light and velvety.
Baking: Divide the batter between the two pans and bake for 25-30 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cooling: Let the cakes cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then turn them out onto a rack to cool completely before filling.
Frosting: Beat the cream cheese with the butter until fluffy, gradually add the powdered sugar and vanilla until the frosting is smooth.
Assembly: Cut the cakes into even layers, spread frosting between them and cover the whole cake, decorating the top with cake crumbs.
Serving: Chill the cake for 30 minutes before cutting so the frosting sets and it slices cleanly.
red_velvet.plate: Serve on a white plate with a spoonful of cream and a few red cake crumbs on top

steps: Preheating: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a shallow baking tray with parchment paper.
Whipping the eggs: Whisk the eggs with the sugar in a mixer for 8-10 minutes until tripled in volume, light and pale.
Mixing the dry ingredients: Sift the flour, cocoa and baking powder and gently fold them into the egg mixture with a rubber spatula, using bottom-to-top motions so as not to lose air.
Baking: Spread the batter evenly on the tray in a thin layer and bake for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden.

Important: As soon as it comes out of the oven, roll the warm sponge together with the parchment paper into a log and let it cool rolled up like this; this way it takes the shape of the log without cracking when unrolled again for filling.
Preparing the filling: Beat the room-temperature butter with the powdered sugar until fluffy, add melted couverture and vanilla, and beat until smooth.
Filling and rolling: Carefully unroll the sponge, spread half the filling evenly, and roll it up again tightly without the parchment paper into a log shape.
Coating: Cover the entire log with the remaining chocolate filling and use a fork to score lines resembling tree bark.
Chilling: Place the log in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours so the filling firms up and holds its shape.
Serving: Dust with powdered sugar just before serving for a snow-covered look, and cut into slices with a knife dipped in hot water.
kormos_xristougennon.plate: Serve in slices on a white plate, dusted with powdered sugar and a few raspberries alongside

ing: Powdered sugar for the icing 150 g
steps: Preparing the pastry: Unroll the puff pastry sheets and place them on parchment-lined baking trays, pricking them well with a fork so they don't puff up excessively.
Baking: Bake the sheets in a preheated oven at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, until golden and crisp. Let cool completely on a rack.
Important: To keep the pastry flat and crisp, place a second tray on top during baking, so it is pressed lightly and doesn't rise unevenly.
Pastry cream: Heat the milk in a saucepan. In a bowl, whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch until the mixture turns pale.

Cooking the cream: Slowly pour the hot milk into the egg mixture, stirring constantly, return to the heat and stir until the cream thickens. Add the vanilla and let cool covered with plastic wrap pressed onto the surface.
Whipping the cream: Whip the heavy cream and gently fold it into the cold pastry cream to make it lighter.
Assembly: Cut the pastry sheets into equal rectangles. Layer one sheet, spread cream generously, place a second sheet, more cream, and finish with a third sheet.

Icing and decoration: Make an icing by mixing powdered sugar with a few drops of lemon juice and water until slightly thickened. Spread it over the surface and pipe stripes of melted chocolate, dragging a toothpick through for the classic pattern.
Chilling: Place the dessert in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before cutting, so the cream sets and it slices cleanly.
millefeuille_franc.plate: Serve cold on a plate with a little powdered sugar and fresh forest berries on the side

steps: Base: Crush the biscuits in a food processor into crumbs and mix with the melted butter and a pinch of salt.
Shaping the base: Spread the mixture into a 22 cm ring lined with parchment paper on the bottom, pressing down firmly with the back of a spoon. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Hydrating the gelatin: Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes, squeeze out the excess water, and melt them in a little warm cream.
Important: The gelatin must be just lukewarm when folded into the hazelnut spread and cream cheese mixture, so it neither curdles the cream nor sets prematurely into lumps.
Hazelnut cream: Beat the cream cheese with the powdered sugar until fluffy, add the spread and mix until smooth, then stir in the gelatin.
Whipping the cream: Whip the remaining heavy cream to a medium-firm texture and gently fold it into the hazelnut mixture with bottom-to-top motions so as not to lose air.
Filling: Spread the cream over the base, smooth the surface with a spatula, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Decoration: Carefully unmold, dust the surface with cocoa, and scatter coarsely chopped toasted hazelnuts around the edge.
Serving: Cut with a knife dipped in hot water for clean slices.
tourta_fountoukiou.plate: Serve on a plate with a little cocoa dusted around and a spoonful of whipped cream alongside

steps: Preparing the oven: Preheat the oven to 175°C (fan) and butter two 22 cm round pans.
Beating the butter and sugar: Beat the butter with the sugar in a mixer until light and pale, about 5 minutes.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition so they are fully incorporated.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a separate bowl, sift the flour with the baking powder and add the shredded coconut.
Important: Alternately fold the dry ingredients and the milk into the butter mixture, starting and ending with the dry ingredients, mixing gently so as not to lose air and to keep the batter light.
Baking: Divide the batter between the two pans and bake for 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Filling cream: Whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar and coconut milk until firm and whipped.
Assembly: Once the sponge layers have cooled completely, fill and cover them with the coconut cream.
Decoration: Sprinkle generously with extra shredded coconut over the whole surface and sides of the cake.
Chilling and serving: Let the cake chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before cutting, so the cream sets.
tourta_karydas.plate: Serve on a platter with a little extra shredded coconut and fresh fruit on the side

steps: Preheating: Preheat the oven to 120°C (fan) and line a tray with parchment paper, drawing a 20 cm circle on it as a guide.
Whisking the egg whites: Whisk the egg whites in a clean, dry bowl with a mixer at medium speed until frothy and forming soft peaks.
Adding the sugar: Add the sugar gradually, one tablespoon at a time, whisking continuously at high speed until the meringue is glossy and thick.
Important: The meringue is ready when, rubbing a little between your fingers, you feel no sugar granules; otherwise the pavlova will 'weep' syrup during baking.
Folding in: Carefully fold in the cornstarch, lemon juice and vanilla with a spatula, using gentle bottom-to-top motions so the meringue doesn't lose volume.
Shaping: Spread the meringue within the drawn circle, creating a slight hollow in the center to hold the filling later.
Baking: Bake for 75-90 minutes without opening the oven door, until the surface is hard and crisp. Turn off the oven and let the meringue cool completely inside with the door ajar.
Whipped cream: Whip the heavy cream with the powdered sugar until it thickens slightly, without becoming too stiff.
Assembly: Spread the whipped cream on the cooled meringue base and garnish generously with strawberries, kiwi and passion fruit pulp just before serving.
pavlova.plate: Serve on a flat platter, cut into slices, with an extra spoonful of fresh seasonal fruit

steps: Preheating: Heat the oven to 150°C on conventional (top and bottom heat), without fan.
Cream: Place the cream in a saucepan with the vanilla (seeds and pod) and heat over low heat until steaming, without boiling.
Yolks: In a bowl, whisk the yolks with the white sugar and salt until the mixture turns slightly pale.
Important: Slowly pour the hot cream into the yolks, stirring constantly, so the eggs don't curdle from the sudden heat (tempering).
Straining: Pass the mixture through a sieve to remove any bits of egg or vanilla pod and leave the cream smooth.
Filling: Divide the mixture among ramekins and place them in a deep baking dish.
Bain-marie: Fill the dish with hot water halfway up the sides of the ramekins and bake for 35-40 minutes, until the custard is set at the edges but still slightly wobbly in the center.
Chilling: Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Caramelizing: Just before serving, sprinkle brown sugar evenly over the surface and torch it with a kitchen blowtorch until it forms a crisp, golden crust.
creme_brulee.plate: Serve in the ramekin, with a few fresh berries (blueberries or strawberries) and a mint leaf

steps: Preparing the oven: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line two baking trays with parchment paper, drawing 22 cm circles on them.
Almond meringue: Whisk the egg whites into a firm meringue, gradually adding the sugar, until glossy and stiff.
Folding in the dry ingredients: Gently fold the sliced almonds and flour into the meringue, using bottom-to-top motions so as not to lose volume.
Baking the layers: Spread the mixture within the drawn circles and bake for 20-25 minutes until lightly golden.
Important: The layers must cool completely before peeling them off the parchment paper, otherwise they will break due to their thin, delicate texture.
Chocolate ganache: Heat the cream and pour it over the chocolate broken into pieces, stirring until evenly melted.
Assembly: Place the first layer, spread ganache, add the second layer, and cover the entire cake with the remaining ganache.
Decoration: Press the toasted almonds around the sides of the cake and refrigerate for 3-4 hours before serving.
kopenxagi.plate: Serve in slices with a little cocoa powder and a cup of espresso.

steps: Choux pastry: Bring the water to a boil with the butter, salt and sugar, add the flour all at once, and stir vigorously.
Important: Dry out the dough over the heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, otherwise the eclairs won't rise properly.
Eggs: Remove from the heat, let cool slightly, and add the eggs one at a time, beating well each time.
Piping: Pipe 10-12 cm strips onto a parchment-lined tray using a piping bag.
Baking: Bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes without opening the oven door.
Pastry cream: Heat the milk, whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch, combine, and cook over heat until thickened.
Cooling the cream: Cover with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface and chill in the refrigerator.
Filling: Split open the cooled eclairs and fill them using a piping bag.
Glaze: Melt the couverture with the cream and dip the top of each eclair.
Serving: Let the glaze set for 15 minutes in the refrigerator.
eclair.plate: On an elongated plate side by side, with a little cream alongside

steps: Dough: Mix the flour with the sugar, add the butter, and rub in with your fingers until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Shaping the dough: Gradually add the wine and vinegar and knead until you get a smooth, elastic dough. Wrap in plastic wrap and let rest for 1 hour.
Rolling and cutting: Roll the dough out very thin and cut into 10 cm circles, wrap them around metal cannoli tubes, sealing with egg.
Important: The oil must be at exactly 175°C - if it's cooler, the cannoli shells absorb oil and become greasy; if it's hotter, they burn on the outside while staying raw inside.
Frying: Fry the shells until evenly golden, remove onto paper towels, and carefully slide off the tubes once slightly cooled.
Ricotta cream: Beat the ricotta with the powdered sugar until smooth and fluffy, fold in the chocolate chips.
Filling: Fill the shells with the ricotta cream at the moment of serving using a piping bag, starting from one end.
Decoration: Dip the ends in chopped pistachios and dust with powdered sugar before serving.
cannoli.plate: Serve immediately after filling on a platter, so the shell stays crisp.

steps: Drying the almond flour: Sift the almond flour thoroughly with the powdered sugar so no lumps remain.
Italian meringue: Boil water with sugar to 118°C and slowly pour it into half the whisked egg whites, whisking continuously until the meringue cools.
Macaronage: Mix the remaining egg whites with the almond mixture, then add the meringue, folding gently in circular motions.

Important: The batter must reach a lava-like consistency - when it falls from the spatula it should form a ribbon that disappears within 20 seconds, otherwise the macarons will crack or fail to form 'feet'.
Piping: Fill a piping bag with the batter and pipe even circles 3-4 cm across onto a parchment-lined tray, tapping the tray lightly to release air bubbles.
Resting: Let the macarons rest at room temperature for 30-45 minutes until a thin, firm skin forms on top.
Baking: Bake at 150°C for 13-15 minutes, rotating the tray halfway through for even baking.
Filling and assembly: Beat butter with powdered sugar to make a cream, fill half the shells and top with the other half.
macarons.plate: Serve on a platter in vivid colors, ideally after 24 hours in the refrigerator to mature.

steps: Joconde sponge: Whisk the eggs with the almond flour and powdered sugar until light, add the flour and melted butter.
Meringue: Whisk the egg whites with the granulated sugar into a stiff meringue and gently fold it into the almond mixture.
Baking the thin sponge: Spread thinly on a parchment-lined tray and bake at 220°C for 6-8 minutes. Cut into three equal rectangles.
Coffee syrup: Make strong espresso and sweeten it lightly; use it to soak the sponge.
Coffee buttercream: Beat the butter until fluffy and add espresso until it takes on coffee flavor and color.
Chocolate ganache: Heat the cream and pour it over the chocolate, stirring until it becomes a smooth ganache.
Important: Assembly must be done with the layers chilled between each level, so the layers stay straight and clearly defined when the cake is sliced.
Coating and finishing: Cover the surface with a thin layer of ganache, smooth with a spatula, and pipe the signature 'Opéra' lettering with chocolate.
opera_cake.plate: Cut into small rectangles and served with a touch of gold leaf.

steps: Biscuit base: Crush the biscuits and mix with the melted butter. Spread on the bottom of a ring mold and refrigerate.
Hydrating the gelatin: Soak the gelatin sheets in cold water for 5-10 minutes until softened.
Dark chocolate mousse: Melt the dark chocolate, whip 1/3 of the cream to soft peaks, and fold in with 2 sheets of drained, melted gelatin.
First layer: Spread the dark chocolate mousse over the base and freeze for 30 minutes until set.
Milk chocolate mousse: Repeat the same process with the milk chocolate and spread it as the second layer, freeze again.
Important: Each mousse layer must be well set in the freezer before adding the next, otherwise the layers will blend together and the three chocolate levels won't be clearly visible.
White chocolate mousse: Make the third mousse with white chocolate the same way and spread it as the final layer, smoothing the surface well.
Sealing and unmolding: Freeze the cake for at least 4 hours or overnight, then run a hot knife around the edge to remove the ring.
tria_sokolata.plate: Served in slices with a little chocolate sauce and shavings of the three chocolates on top.

steps: Beating the base: Beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy, then add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Incorporating the dry ingredients: Mix the flour with the cocoa and baking powder and add them to the mixture alternately with the milk.
Baking: Pour the batter into a 22 cm round pan and bake at 175°C for 35-40 minutes, until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Slicing into layers: Let the cake cool completely, then cut it horizontally into three equal layers.
Soaking with coffee: Sprinkle each layer with a little espresso so it moistens lightly without becoming soggy.
Mocha buttercream: Beat the butter with the powdered sugar until pale, then gradually add the remaining espresso until smooth.
Important: The buttercream must be whipped at a cool room temperature; if the butter is too soft the cream will 'split' and won't hold its shape on the sides of the cake.
Assembling and finishing: Spread buttercream between the layers and cover the entire cake, dusting the surface with cocoa.
tourta_moka.plate: Serve in slices with a light dusting of cocoa powder and coffee beans as garnish.

steps: Beating the base: Beat the butter with the sugar until fluffy, then add the eggs one at a time along with the lemon zest.
Incorporating wet and dry ingredients: Add the flour with the baking powder alternately with the lemon juice, folding in gently.
Baking: Pour the batter into a 22 cm round pan and bake at 175°C for 35-40 minutes, until golden and a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Slicing into layers: Let cool completely, then cut the cake horizontally into two or three layers.
Cream cheese-lemon filling: Beat the cream cheese with the butter and powdered sugar until light and smooth.
Important: The lemon curd must be completely cold before spreading it on the layers, otherwise it will melt the cream cheese filling and the cake won't hold its shape.
Filling: Spread cream cheese filling and lemon curd alternately between the layers, pressing lightly to set the layers.
Coating and decorating: Cover the entire cake with the remaining cream cheese filling and decorate with lemon slices or zest.
tourta_lemoniou.wine: Sweet Muscat wine or lemon tea
tourta_lemoniou.plate: Serve in slices, chilled, with a lemon slice on the edge of the plate.

ing: Ready-made or homemade sponge cake, 1 (22 cm)
Amaretto liqueur or vanilla liqueur 2 tbsp
steps: Slicing the sponge cake: Cut the sponge cake horizontally into two or three layers of equal thickness.
Soaking: Mix the milk with the liqueur and lightly sprinkle each layer so it softens without becoming soggy.
Whipping the cream: Whip the chilled heavy cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla until it forms stiff whipped cream.
Incorporating the mascarpone: Add the mascarpone to the whipped cream, folding in gently with a spatula until smooth.
Important: The grated chocolate must be very cold and dry before being folded into the cream, so it forms the characteristic small flecks of stracciatella instead of melting and streaking the cream.
Adding the chocolate: Gently fold two-thirds of the grated chocolate into the mascarpone cream with light movements.
Assembling: Spread cream between each sponge cake layer and cover the entire cake with the remaining mixture.
Finishing: Sprinkle the top and sides with the remaining grated chocolate and chill in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours before serving.
stratsiatela.plate: Serve in slices with extra grated chocolate on top.

steps: Dough: Roll out the dough on a round baking sheet or pizza stone to a thickness of 0.5 cm.
Sauce: Spread the tomato sauce evenly, leaving a 1 cm border for the crust.
Mushrooms: Lightly sauté the mushrooms in a little olive oil before adding them to the pizza, so they don't release water during baking.
Toppings: Spread the mozzarella, then the ham, mushrooms, artichokes halved, and olives.
Important: The oven must be preheated to 250°C for at least 20 minutes beforehand, ideally with a pizza stone, so the dough bakes quickly and stays crisp without the toppings drying out.
Baking: Bake on the lowest rack of the oven for 10-12 minutes, until the crust is well browned.
Drizzling: As soon as it comes out of the oven, drizzle with a thread of olive oil.
Serving: Sprinkle with oregano and cut into slices immediately.
pizza_capricciosa.plate: Serve whole on a wooden board, cut into slices.

steps: Dough: Roll the dough out thin on a round baking sheet or pizza stone.
Sauce: Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce over the surface.
Cheese: Add the mozzarella in pieces, evenly distributed.
Important: Prosciutto crudo is NEVER baked with the pizza, as it toughens and loses its flavor; it is always added raw after baking.
Baking: Bake at 250°C for 8-10 minutes, until the dough is golden and the cheese has melted well.
Arugula: Toss the arugula with a little olive oil and lemon juice in a bowl.
Serving: As soon as the pizza comes out of the oven, arrange the prosciutto slices and arugula on top.
Finishing: Sprinkle with Parmesan shavings and a final drizzle of olive oil.
pizza_prosciutto_rucola.plate: On a wooden board, cut into diagonal slices.

steps: Dough: Divide the dough into 2 balls and roll out each one into a disc about 25 cm in diameter.
Filling: In a bowl, mix the ricotta, the mozzarella cut into cubes, the ham, and the Parmesan.
Filling the dough: Place the filling on one half of each dough disc, leaving a 2 cm border at the edge.
Important: Seal the edges well by folding the dough into a half-moon shape and pressing with a fork, so the filling doesn't leak out during baking.
Egg wash: Brush the surface with beaten egg so it browns evenly.
Baking: Bake in a preheated oven at 220°C for 20-25 minutes, until the dough is well browned.
Sauce: Warm the tomato sauce with a little olive oil and oregano to serve alongside.
Serving: Let cool for 5 minutes before cutting, so the filling doesn't spill out.
calzone.plate: Serve whole with the warm tomato sauce alongside in a bowl.

steps: Dough: Roll the dough out thin on a round baking sheet or pizza stone.
Sauce: Mix the tomato sauce with the finely chopped garlic and spread it evenly.
Cheese: Add the mozzarella in pieces over the whole surface.
Salami: Arrange the spicy salami slices evenly over the pizza.
Important: Use piccante (spicy) salami rather than plain salami, as this gives the characteristic hot 'diavola' flavor during baking, letting its fat render and melt over the cheese.
Baking: Bake at 250°C for 10-12 minutes, until the salami sizzles lightly at the edges.
Heat: Sprinkle with hot pepper flakes as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Serving: Drizzle with olive oil and serve immediately while hot.
pizza_diavola.plate: On a wooden board, cut into slices, with extra pepper flakes on the side.

steps: Soaking: Soak the chickpeas in plenty of water with the baking soda for 10-12 hours or overnight.
Important: The baking soda helps soften the chickpea skins so they cook faster and the soup becomes creamy without needing a long boiling time.
Rinsing: Drain and rinse the chickpeas well before cooking.
Sautéing: Sauté the finely chopped onion and carrot in olive oil until softened.
Boiling: Add the chickpeas, bay leaves, and water, bring to a boil, then cook over low heat for 1.5-2 hours until completely tender.
Thickening: Remove a few chickpeas, mash them with a fork, and return them to the pot to thicken the soup.
Lemon: At the end of cooking, add the lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.
Serving: Serve hot with a drizzle of raw olive oil on top.
revithosoupa_lemoni.plate: In a deep clay bowl with olive oil and toasted bread on the side.

steps: Base: Put the mayonnaise in a bowl and add the ketchup, mixing well until the colors combine.
Acidity: Add the lemon juice to balance the sweetness of the ketchup.
Important: Finely chop the pickle and onion very small so the sauce stays smooth and its texture doesn't break when serving.
Aroma: Add the paprika and the drops of Worcestershire sauce for depth of flavor.
Mixing: Whisk all the ingredients together until the sauce is uniform and a soft pink color.
Tasting: Taste and adjust with salt and pepper to your liking.
Resting: Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavors meld.
Serving: Serve cold as a dip or sauce for seafood and vegetables.
rosiki_saltsa.plate: Serve in a small bowl as a dip.

steps: Soaking the peppers: Soak the dried peppers in hot water for 20-30 minutes until softened, removing the stems and seeds.
Important: Remove most of the seeds if you want a milder heat, keeping a few for extra intensity.
Draining: Drain the peppers well, pressing them to remove excess water.
Toasting the spices: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Blending: Blend the peppers with the garlic, spices, salt, and lemon juice in a food processor until you get a smooth paste.
Binding with oil: Gradually add the olive oil, blending continuously until the paste becomes velvety.
Checking the flavor: Taste and add tomato paste if you want a deeper red color and a touch of sweetness.
Storing: Transfer the harissa to a glass jar and cover the surface with a little extra oil to preserve it.
harissa.plate: Serve in a jar or small bowl as a condiment.

steps: Fine chopping: Finely chop the parsley and garlic very well with a knife, not in a food processor.
Important: Chopping by hand keeps texture in the ingredients — a food processor turns the sauce into a puree and loses its character.
Mixing the dry ingredients: In a bowl, combine the parsley, garlic, oregano, and pepper flakes.
Liquids: Add the wine vinegar and stir it in on its own first, so the garlic 'cooks' slightly in the acidity.
Oil: Gradually pour in the olive oil, stirring until it comes together into a slightly loose sauce.
Seasoning: Add salt and pepper and stir again.
Resting: Let the sauce sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour before using, so the flavors develop.
Serving: Serve at room temperature over grilled meat.
chimichurri.plate: Serve in a small bowl alongside grilled meat.

steps: Preparation: Peel and slice the carrots into rounds, finely chop the onion, and grate the ginger.
Sautéing: Sauté the onion in the olive oil over low heat until softened, without browning.
Adding the ginger: Add the ginger and sauté for 1-2 minutes until its aroma comes through.
Cooking the carrots: Add the carrots and vegetable stock and simmer over medium heat for 20-25 minutes until completely tender.
Important: The carrots need to be very soft so the pureed soup comes out perfectly velvety with no lumps.
Blending: Blend the soup with an immersion blender until it becomes a smooth cream.
Cream: Add the heavy cream and stir over low heat for 2-3 minutes without letting it boil.
Seasoning: Season with salt and pepper and taste, adding a little extra ginger if you want a more intense flavor.
Serving: Serve hot, garnished with fresh spring onion and a drizzle of olive oil.
karotosoupa_tzitzer.wine: Off-dry white wine or ginger tea
karotosoupa_tzitzer.plate: Serve hot in a deep bowl with a drizzle of olive oil on top.

steps: Preparing the meat: Put the ground beef in a bowl with salt and freshly ground pepper, and knead lightly just enough to combine, without overworking it, so it stays tender.
Shaping the patties: Divide the meat into 4 equal balls and flatten them into patties about 2 cm thick, slightly wider than the buns since they will shrink during cooking.
Important: Press a small indentation in the center of each patty with your thumb, so it doesn't puff up during cooking and stays flat.
Heating the pan: Heat the pan or grill well over high heat with a little olive oil before adding the patties, so they caramelize immediately.
Cooking: Cook the patties for 3-4 minutes per side for medium doneness, flipping only once to keep their juices.
Cheese: One minute before removing the patties, place a slice of cheese on top and cover the pan so it melts gently.
Buns: Split the buns in half and toast them briefly on the grill, cut side down, until lightly browned.
Assembling: Spread mustard and ketchup on the bottom bun, add lettuce, the cheese-topped patty, tomato slices, onion, and pickles, then close with the top bun.
mpourger_spitiko.wine: Ice-cold lager beer or a light dry red wine
mpourger_spitiko.plate: Serve with french fries and barbecue sauce on the side.

steps: Cleaning the shrimp: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails on, and devein them with a small knife.
Sautéing: In a wide skillet, heat the olive oil and sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic until softened.
Shrimp in the pan: Add the shrimp and sauté for 1-2 minutes over high heat until they change color on the outside.

Important — flambéing with ouzo: Remove the pan from the heat, warm the ouzo separately in a small saucepan, pour it over the shrimp, and carefully ignite it with a long match, keeping your face at a distance; wait for the flame to burn out on its own before continuing. Never pour ouzo directly from the bottle onto an open flame.
Tomato sauce: Add the grated tomatoes, salt, pepper, and the hot pepper, lower the heat, and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Feta: Crumble the feta into large pieces and scatter it over the top, then cover for 2-3 minutes until it softens slightly without melting completely.
Dill: Sprinkle with finely chopped fresh dill just before serving for freshness.
Serving: Serve immediately, hot, in the same skillet, with fresh bread to mop up the sauce.
garides_saganaki_ouzo.wine: Ice-cold ouzo or a dry white Assyrtiko wine
garides_saganaki_ouzo.plate: Serve in the skillet with freshly cut village bread.

steps: Preparation: Cut the broccoli into florets and the potato into small cubes, and finely chop the onion and garlic.
Sautéing the base: In a pot, melt the butter with the olive oil and sauté the onion and garlic until glossy, without browning.
Adding the vegetables: Add the potato and broccoli and stir for 2-3 minutes so they absorb the aromas.
Boiling: Add the vegetable stock, salt, and pepper, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender.
Important: Do not cook longer than necessary, as prolonged boiling darkens the broccoli and it loses its bright green color.
Blending: Remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth and velvety, with no lumps.
Heavy cream: Return to low heat, add the heavy cream, and stir for 2 minutes until incorporated, without letting it boil.
Tasting and adjusting: Taste and adjust the salt and pepper; if too thick, add a little hot stock.
Serving: Serve hot in bowls with a swirl of cream on top and a few croutons.
krema_brokolou.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko wine or tsipouro
krema_brokolou.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with a spiral of cream and croutons in the center.

steps: Preparing the meat: Rinse the kid goat and pat it dry thoroughly with paper towels, then cut it into portion pieces. Kid goat is leaner than lamb, so it needs fat and moisture to stay tender.
Studding with garlic: Pierce the meat in several spots with a sharp knife and push a sliver of garlic into each hole, so the aroma reaches the inside.
Marinating: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper and rub the mixture over the meat on all sides. Let it stand for 30 minutes.
Preparing the potatoes: Peel the potatoes and cut them into thick wedges, season with salt, pepper, oregano and a little oil and spread them in the roasting pan.
Assembling the pan: Place the meat among the potatoes, add the bay leaves and pour in the water so it comes about a finger deep in the pan.
Covered roasting: Important: Cover the pan tightly with foil and roast at 180°C for 1 hour and 30 minutes. The trapped steam is what makes kid goat fall off the bone instead of drying out.
Browning: Remove the foil, raise the heat to 200°C and roast for another 30-40 minutes until the meat and potatoes are golden, basting twice with the pan juices.
Resting: Let the meat rest for 10 minutes out of the oven before serving, so the juices settle back into it.
katsikaki_fournou.wine: An aged red Xinomavro or a robust Agiorgitiko stands up to the intense flavour of the goat.
katsikaki_fournou.plate: Serve on a large platter with the potatoes around the meat, lemon wedges and a sprinkle of fresh oregano.

steps: Cutting the meat: Cut the kid goat into serving pieces and pat them completely dry, so they can brown rather than boil in the pot.
Searing: Heat the oil in a wide pot over high heat and sear the pieces in batches until golden on all sides. Do not crowd the pot or the meat will steam.
Aromatics: Lower the heat, add the chopped onion and the crushed garlic and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Deglazing: Pour in the hot water, scraping the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon so the caramelised bits dissolve into the sauce — this is where most of the flavour lives.
Slow cooking: Season with salt and pepper, cover and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, until the meat is nearly tender.
Adding the lemon: Important: Add the lemon juice and the oregano only in the last 20 minutes. Lemon added early toughens the meat fibres and turns bitter.
Reducing the sauce: Uncover and let the sauce reduce for 10 minutes over medium heat until it thickens and glazes the meat.
Resting: Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 10 minutes so the lemon settles into the meat.
katsikaki_lemonato.wine: A crisp Assyrtiko or Robola matches the lemon without fighting it.
katsikaki_lemonato.plate: Serve in a deep dish with plenty of the lemon sauce spooned over, alongside rice or crusty bread.

steps: Preparing the meat: Cut the kid goat into serving pieces, dry them well and season with salt and pepper.
Searing: Sear the meat in a pot with the oil over high heat until deeply browned on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sautéing the aromatics: In the same oil sauté the chopped onion and garlic for 4 minutes, then add the tomato paste and cook it for 1 minute so it loses its raw edge.
Building the sauce: Return the meat, add the grated tomato, cinnamon and bay leaf, cover and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour and 15 minutes until the meat is tender.

Transferring to the pan: Move the meat and its sauce into a wide baking dish and pour in the hot water or stock. Important: the liquid must be about double the volume of the orzo, or it will come out dry.
Adding the orzo: Stir in the orzo, spread it evenly around the meat and check the seasoning — the orzo absorbs a lot of salt.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for about 30 minutes, stirring once halfway through so the orzo cooks evenly and does not stick to the edges.
Finishing with cheese: Scatter the grated kefalotyri over the top and return it for 5-8 minutes until it melts and lightly browns.
Resting: Let it stand for 10 minutes before serving, so the orzo absorbs the last of the sauce.
katsikaki_giouvetsi.wine: A red Agiorgitiko from Nemea, whose soft tannins suit the tomato.
katsikaki_giouvetsi.plate: Serve straight from the baking dish with extra grated cheese on the table and a spoon for the sauce.

katsikaki_ladorigani.n: Kid Goat with Oregano in Parchment
steps: Cutting the meat: Cut the kid goat into fairly large pieces — small pieces dry out during the long slow bake.
Making the ladolemono: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper into a thick emulsion.
Marinating: Coat the meat in the mixture and leave it for at least 1 hour in the fridge, ideally overnight.
Preparing the parchment: Lay two large sheets of parchment paper crosswise in a roasting pan, leaving plenty of overhang to fold over the top.

Wrapping: Place the meat in the centre with all the marinade, tuck in the cheese if using, and fold the parchment into a sealed parcel. Important: the seal must be tight — the steam trapped inside is what cooks the goat in its own juices.
Slow baking: Bake at 160°C for 2 hours and 30 minutes. Low and slow is what breaks down the connective tissue of goat meat.
Opening the parcel: Open the parchment carefully — the escaping steam is scalding — and return it uncovered for 15 minutes at 200°C to colour the surface.
Serving: Serve straight in the opened parcel so none of the aromatic juices are lost.
katsikaki_ladorigani.wine: A rustic Cretan Kotsifali or Liatiko echoes the oregano and olive oil.
katsikaki_ladorigani.plate: Bring the opened parchment parcel to the table on a wooden board, with lemon halves and fresh bread for the juices.

katsikaki_frikase.n: Kid Goat Fricassee with Lettuce & Dill
steps: Preparing the meat: Cut the kid goat into serving pieces, rinse and dry it well and season with salt and pepper.
Searing: Sauté the meat in a pot with the oil over medium-high heat until lightly golden — you want colour, not a hard crust.
Adding the spring onions: Add the chopped spring onions and sauté for 3-4 minutes until they wilt and sweeten.
Simmering: Pour in the hot water, cover and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour, until the meat is almost tender.
Adding the greens: Add the shredded lettuce and most of the dill and cook for another 20 minutes, until the lettuce collapses into the sauce.
Reducing: Uncover and let the liquid reduce until only about 1.5 cups remain — the avgolemono needs a concentrated broth to cling to.

Making the avgolemono: Important: Beat the eggs well, add the lemon juice, then ladle in hot broth a spoonful at a time while beating constantly. Tempering slowly is the only way to stop the eggs from scrambling.
Finishing: Pour the avgolemono back into the pot, swirl the pot gently — never boil it again — and let it sit off the heat for 5 minutes to thicken.
Serving: Scatter the remaining fresh dill over the top just before serving.
katsikaki_frikase.wine: A Moschofilero or a barrel-aged Assyrtiko keeps up with the avgolemono.
katsikaki_frikase.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with plenty of avgolemono, fresh dill on top and crusty bread on the side.

steps: Preparing the fillet: Tie the fillet with kitchen string every 3-4 cm so it holds an even cylindrical shape, and season it generously with salt and pepper.

Searing: Sear the fillet in a very hot pan with oil for 1-2 minutes per side, until a dark crust forms all over. Important: the pan must be smoking hot — this crust is pure flavour and it also seals the surface.
Brushing with mustard: While the fillet is still warm, brush it all over with the Dijon mustard and let it cool completely. A warm fillet would melt the pastry later.
Making the duxelles: Blitz the mushrooms and shallots in a food processor until finely minced, then cook them in the butter over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Drying the duxelles: Important: Keep cooking until every drop of moisture has evaporated and the mixture pulls away from the pan. Any remaining water will turn the pastry to mush.
Flavouring: Add the brandy and the thyme leaves, cook for 2 more minutes to burn off the alcohol, season and let it cool completely.
Building the layers: Lay out cling film, arrange the prosciutto slices overlapping into a rectangle, spread the duxelles evenly over them and place the fillet at one edge.
Rolling: Roll tightly using the cling film into a firm cylinder, twist the ends like a sweet wrapper and chill for 30 minutes so it sets its shape.
Wrapping in pastry: Unwrap the cylinder onto the puff pastry sheet, roll it up, seal the edges well and place it seam-side down on a lined baking tray.
Chilling: Chill the parcel for another 20 minutes. Cold pastry rises higher and crisper in the oven.
Baking: Brush with the egg yolk, score the surface lightly with a knife and bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes for medium doneness.
Resting: Important: Let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Cutting immediately would let all the juices run out onto the board.
mosxari_wellington.wine: A serious red — aged Bordeaux, Nemea Grande Reserve or a full-bodied Xinomavro.
mosxari_wellington.plate: Slice into thick rounds with a serrated knife and serve on warm plates with a red wine sauce and glazed vegetables.

steps: Marinating: Cut the rooster into serving pieces and marinate it overnight in the red wine with the bay leaves, thyme and garlic. Important: this long marinade is not optional — rooster is tough meat and the wine begins breaking it down.
Draining: Remove the pieces from the marinade and dry them very well with paper towels. Keep the wine — it becomes the sauce.
Rendering the bacon: Cook the diced bacon in a heavy pot until its fat renders out and it turns crisp, then remove it with a slotted spoon.
Searing the meat: Sear the rooster pieces in the bacon fat with the oil, in batches, until deeply browned on all sides.
Sautéing the vegetables: Add the onions and sliced carrots and sauté for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and cook it for 1 minute.
Adding flour: Sprinkle over the flour and stir for 2 minutes so it toasts lightly — this is what will thicken the sauce later.
Deglazing: Pour in the reserved marinade, scraping the bottom of the pot thoroughly, and bring it to a boil.
Slow cooking: Return the meat and bacon, cover and simmer over very low heat for 2 hours, until the meat is falling off the bone.
Sautéing the mushrooms: Meanwhile sauté the mushrooms separately in the butter until golden, and add them in the last 15 minutes so they keep their texture.
Finishing the sauce: If the sauce is thin, remove the meat and reduce it over high heat for 10 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.
Resting: Let it rest off the heat for 15 minutes — like all wine stews, it tastes better after it settles.
kokoras_krasatos.wine: The same red you cooked with — a Burgundy Pinot Noir or a Naoussa Xinomavro.
kokoras_krasatos.plate: Serve in a deep dish with plenty of sauce, alongside mashed potato or wide noodles.

steps: Cutting the meat: Cut the beef into large 4-5 cm cubes. Important: do not cut them small — long cooking shrinks them and small pieces fall apart into threads.
Drying: Pat the cubes completely dry and season with salt and pepper. A wet surface will never brown.
Rendering the bacon: Cook the diced bacon in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift it out and reserve.
Searing the beef: Sear the cubes in the bacon fat in small batches, so the pot stays hot and each piece gets a dark crust. This step defines the final colour of the dish.
Sautéing the vegetables: Add the carrots and onions, sauté for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute more.
Adding flour: Dust with the flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out its raw taste.
Deglazing with wine: Pour in the wine, scrape the bottom of the pot and let it boil for 5 minutes to drive off the alcohol.
Slow cooking: Add the stock, the bay leaves, the thyme and the bacon, cover and cook over very low heat for 2 hours and 30 minutes, or in the oven at 160°C.
Adding the mushrooms: Sauté the mushrooms in butter until golden and stir them in for the last 20 minutes.
Checking: The dish is ready when a piece of meat gives way under a fork with no resistance at all.
Reducing: If needed, uncover and reduce over medium heat until the sauce is glossy and clings to the meat.
beef_bourguignon.wine: A Burgundy Pinot Noir, or the same wine used in the pot.
beef_bourguignon.plate: Serve in a deep bowl over mashed potato, with the onions and mushrooms arranged on top.

steps: Preparing the shanks: Score the outer membrane of each shank in 3-4 places with a knife. Important: without this, the membrane contracts in the heat and curls the meat out of shape.
Dusting with flour: Season the shanks and dust them lightly with flour, shaking off the excess — a thin coat browns beautifully, a thick one turns gluey.
Searing: Sear them in a wide pot with oil and a knob of butter, 4 minutes per side, until well coloured, then remove.
Sofrito: Sauté the finely diced onion, carrot and celery in the same pot for 8 minutes over medium heat until soft and sweet.
Deglazing: Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate almost completely, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Braising: Return the shanks, add the grated tomato and enough stock to come two thirds up the meat, cover and simmer over low heat for 2 hours.
Starting the risotto: Toast the rice in butter in a separate pan for 2 minutes, until the grains turn translucent at the edges.

Cooking the risotto: Add the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before the next. Important: never add cold stock — it stops the cooking and the rice turns chalky.
Adding the saffron: Dissolve the saffron in a little hot stock and stir it in halfway through, for the colour and aroma of Milanese risotto.
Finishing the risotto: After about 18 minutes, off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the parmesan until creamy and glossy.
Gremolata: Mix finely chopped lemon zest, parsley and garlic — this fresh topping cuts through the richness of the dish.
Serving: Plate the risotto, set a shank on top, spoon over its sauce and finish with the gremolata.
osobuco.wine: A Barolo or Barbaresco, or a Greek Xinomavro of good age.
osobuco.plate: Serve on a wide flat plate: risotto underneath, the shank on top with the marrow bone visible, gremolata scattered over.

steps: Preparing the meat: Keep the beef in one whole piece, dry it thoroughly and season it heavily with salt and pepper on every side.
Searing: Sear it in the pot over high heat with oil until dark brown all over, about 3 minutes per side.
Sautéing the aromatics: Add the whole onions, the garlic and the carrots cut into thick chunks and sauté for 5 minutes.
Deglazing: Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the grated tomato, the rosemary and the bay leaves.
Sealing the pot: Important: The gastra works because it is completely sealed — if the lid is not tight, lay a sheet of foil under it so no steam escapes.
Slow cooking: Cook over very low heat, or in the oven at 160°C, for 2 hours without opening the pot. Every time you lift the lid you lose the steam that is doing the work.
Adding the potatoes: Add the potatoes cut into large chunks, season, reseal and cook for another 45 minutes.
Checking: The meat is done when a fork slides in and out with no resistance and the potatoes have absorbed the sauce.
Resting and carving: Let it rest for 15 minutes, then carve the meat into thick slices against the grain.
mosxari_gastra.wine: A rustic red — Agiorgitiko, Mavrodaphne dry or a Naoussa Xinomavro.
mosxari_gastra.plate: Serve family-style straight from the pot, with the meat sliced in the centre and the vegetables around it.

steps: Preparing the racks: Trim the fat cap down to a thin layer and scrape the rib bones clean, so they stay white and presentable after roasting.

Seasoning: Season the racks generously with salt and pepper and let them come to room temperature for 30 minutes. Important: cold meat straight from the fridge cooks unevenly — the outside overcooks before the centre warms.
Searing: Sear them in a very hot pan, fat side down first, for 2-3 minutes per side until golden. Do not cook them through — the oven will finish them.
Making the crust: Blitz the breadcrumbs with the parsley, rosemary, thyme and garlic in a food processor until bright green and fine.
Binding the crust: Melt the butter and mix it into the crumbs so the crust holds together and browns instead of burning dry.
Brushing with mustard: Brush the fat side of each rack with a thick layer of mustard — this is the glue that holds the crust on.
Coating: Press the herb crust firmly onto the mustard so it adheres in an even layer.
Roasting: Roast at 200°C for 20-22 minutes for pink meat, or 25-28 minutes for medium.
Resting: Important: Rest for 10 minutes under loose foil. Lamb especially needs this — carved straight from the oven it bleeds out and goes grey.
Carving: Cut between the bones into individual chops with a sharp knife.
kare_arniou.wine: An elegant red — Bordeaux blend, aged Agiorgitiko or a Syrah with soft tannins.
kare_arniou.plate: Arrange the chops leaning against one another with the bones upward, on a purée or roasted vegetables, with pan juices around.

steps: Scoring the skin: Score the skin in a close diamond pattern with a very sharp knife, cutting through the skin but not into the meat. Important: this is what lets the fat escape and the crackling form.
Drying the skin: Pat the skin bone dry and leave the belly uncovered in the fridge overnight. Dry skin crackles; damp skin turns to leather.
Salting: Rub the coarse salt firmly into the scored skin and brush off the excess just before roasting.
Seasoning the meat: Turn it over and rub the meat side with garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, pepper and oil.
Slow roasting: Place it skin-side up in a pan, pour the wine into the bottom of the pan without touching the skin, and roast at 150°C for 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Checking the wine: Top up with a little water if the pan runs dry — the meat must braise gently in steam from below while the skin dries above.
Crackling: Raise the heat to 230°C for the last 20-25 minutes, watching constantly, until the skin puffs and blisters into crackling.
Glazing: Brush the honey over the skin in the last 5 minutes for colour and shine — any earlier and it burns.
Resting: Rest for 15 minutes, then cut with a serrated knife so the crackling shatters cleanly instead of dragging.
panseta_sigopsimeni.wine: A dry Assyrtiko or a lightly oaked white with acidity to cut the fat.
panseta_sigopsimeni.plate: Cut into thick fingers and stand them upright with the crackling on top, next to apple purée or braised greens.

steps: Preparing the salmon: Check the fillet for pin bones with your fingers and pull out any you find with tweezers. Pat it completely dry and season it.
Wilting the spinach: Sauté the sliced leek in butter for 3 minutes, add the spinach and cook until it collapses.

Draining: Important: Tip the spinach into a sieve and press hard to squeeze out every bit of liquid, then let it cool. Wet filling is the single reason this dish fails — it steams the pastry from the inside.
Making the filling: Mix the drained spinach with the cream cheese, the chopped dill, the lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Assembling: Roll out the pastry, spread half the filling in the centre in the shape of the fillet, lay the salmon on top and cover it with the rest.
Wrapping: Fold the pastry over, sealing the edges well, and place it seam-side down on a lined tray. Trim any thick overlaps — doubled pastry stays raw.
Chilling: Chill for 20 minutes so the pastry firms up before it meets the heat.
Decorating: Brush with egg yolk and score a light pattern on the surface, cutting only the top layer.
Baking: Bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, until deep golden and crisp all over.
Resting: Let it stand for 5 minutes, then cut with a serrated knife into thick slices.
solomos_krousta.wine: A Chardonnay with light oak, or a Greek Malagousia.
solomos_krousta.plate: Serve in thick slices showing the green filling around the pink salmon, with a lemon-dill sauce on the side.

steps: Choosing the potatoes: Use floury potatoes, not waxy ones. Waxy varieties hold their shape and give a gluey purée instead of a fluffy one.
Cutting: Peel the potatoes and cut them into evenly sized chunks, so they all finish cooking at the same moment.
Boiling: Start them in cold salted water and bring to the boil. Important: starting in cold water cooks them evenly from the outside in — dropping them into boiling water leaves raw centres.
Testing: Simmer for about 20 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk and it falls off on its own.
Draining: Drain them well and return them to the hot empty pot for 1 minute over low heat, shaking it, so the surface moisture steams off.
Mashing: Mash them while still hot with a potato masher or pass them through a ricer. Important: never use a blender or food processor — the blades break the starch and turn the purée into glue.
Adding the butter: Work in the cold butter in pieces first, before any liquid, so the fat coats the starch and keeps the texture silky.
Adding the milk: Pour in the warm milk gradually, beating with a spoon until you reach the consistency you want. Cold milk would seize the purée.
Seasoning: Season with salt, white pepper and a pinch of nutmeg, and serve immediately while hot and airy.
poures_patatas.wine: Not applicable — it accompanies the main dish and follows its wine.
poures_patatas.plate: Serve in a warm bowl, smooth the surface with the back of a spoon and drop a knob of butter in the hollow.

steps: Preparing the tomatoes: Crush the canned tomatoes by hand or with a fork, leaving them a little rough. A blender would aerate them and turn the sauce pale orange.

Infusing the oil: Warm the oil over low heat with the lightly crushed garlic cloves for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant but not coloured. Important: browned garlic turns bitter and the whole sauce follows it.
Starting the sauce: Remove the garlic, add the tomatoes, season with salt, pepper and the sugar to balance the acidity.
Simmering: Simmer gently uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and the oil separates at the edges.
Adding basil: Tear in most of the basil leaves in the last 5 minutes, so the aroma stays fresh instead of cooking away.
Boiling the pasta: Cook the spaghetti in plenty of well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet says.
Reserving pasta water: Important: Save a cup of the cooking water before draining. Its starch is what binds the sauce to the pasta.
