Melt the butter and mix with the sugar. Add the egg.
Add the flour, baking soda, and chocolate chips.
Bake at 175°C for 10-12 minutes — keep them soft!
Beat the butter and sugar. Add the eggs.
Sift in the flour and cocoa. Knead into a dough.
Bake at 175°C for 15 minutes.
Beat the butter and sugar. Add the egg and ground almonds.
Sift in the flour. Knead into a dough.
Top with sliced almonds and bake at 170°C for 18 minutes.
Warm the honey and butter together, then let cool.
Sift in the flour, spices, and baking soda.
Shape into small balls and bake at 170°C for 15 minutes.
Beat the butter and sugar. Add the eggs and vanilla.
Sift in the flour. Knead into a dough.
Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs and sugar, then add the olive oil and orange juice.
Mix in the flour. Shape into logs.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, slice, then return to the oven for another 10 minutes.
Mix the dry ingredients separately. Combine gently with the wet ingredients — a few lumps should remain!
Let rest 5 minutes. Heat a buttered pan over medium heat.
Pour 1 ladleful per pancake. Flip when small bubbles appear on top. Cook 2-3 minutes per side.
Prepare the pancake batter.
Fold the blueberries gently into the batter.
Cook as usual. Serve with honey and extra blueberries.
Mash the bananas with the egg and milk.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon, and mix.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side. Serve with honey.
Whisk eggs, flour and sugar. Add the milk gradually, then the butter. Let the batter rest 30 minutes.
Heat the pan and add a little butter.
Cook 1-2 minutes, flip and cook 30 seconds on the other side.
Make the crêpe batter and cook the crêpes one by one in a nonstick pan.
Spread the hazelnut spread generously over each crêpe.
Add the fruit, fold into a triangle and dust with powdered sugar.
Beat the eggs with the milk. Add the flour with the baking powder and mix until smooth.
Drop spoonfuls into hot olive oil. Fry 2 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with honey, cinnamon or fruit preserve.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, sugar and cinnamon. Dip the bread slices until they soak it up.
Melt butter in the pan. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with maple syrup or honey.
Whisk the egg whites separately into a stiff meringue.
Mix the batter with the yolks, then fold in the meringue gently.
Cook in a preheated waffle maker for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Butter the phyllo sheets in alternating layers, sprinkling chopped walnuts with cinnamon between them.
Cut into diamond shapes. Bake at 175°C for 45-50 minutes.
Pour cold syrup over the hot baklava right away.
Make the custard by cooking the milk, sugar, semolina, eggs and vanilla over low heat, stirring until thickened.
Layer buttered phyllo sheets, spread the custard, and cover with more sheets. Butter the top well. Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes.
Pour hot syrup over the cooled galaktoboureko right away — this contrast gives it its signature flavor.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and lukewarm water. Let rise for 1 hour.
Fry spoonfuls of the batter in hot, deep oil for 2-3 minutes until golden all over.
Serve immediately with plenty of honey and cinnamon!
Beat the eggs with the sugar until fluffy. Add the yogurt and melted butter.
Add the semolina with the baking powder and fold in gently.
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes. Pour cold syrup over it as soon as it comes out hot.
Boil the water with the sugar and cinnamon in a 1-2-3-4 ratio. Keep hot.
Sauté the semolina in the olive oil, stirring constantly, until golden.
Slowly pour in the hot syrup (it will spatter!). Stir for 5 minutes. Spoon into a mold, let stand 15 minutes, then turn out.
Soak the rice in water for 10 minutes. Drain.
Cook the milk, sugar, vanilla and rice over low heat for 25-30 minutes until the rice pudding thickens.
Serve in small bowls. Dust with cinnamon on top.
Divide the kataifi into portions and butter each one. Prepare a filling of chopped walnuts and cinnamon.
Place the filling at one edge, roll up tightly and butter well all over. Bake at 175°C for 50 minutes.
Pour cold syrup over the hot kataifi right away. Let it absorb before serving.
Mix everything together well.
Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes.
Pour rosewater syrup over it.
Mix the olive oil, orange juice, sugar and spices. Sift in the flour with the baking soda. Knead into a dough.
Shape into ovals. Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Dip in honey syrup and top with chopped walnuts.
Beat the butter with the powdered sugar until completely pale and fluffy. Add the egg yolk, sifted flour and almonds.
Shape into small domes or star shapes.
Bake at 170°C for 20 minutes. Dust generously with powdered sugar while still hot!
Knead the ingredients well and let the dough rise for 1 hour.
Hide the lucky coin inside the dough and place it in a round baking pan.
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes. Dust with powdered sugar and decorate with patterns.
Activate the yeast for 30 minutes. Knead all the ingredients well for 10 minutes until the dough becomes elastic.
Let rest for 2 hours until doubled in size. Braid into three strands.
Place a red egg in the middle. Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes.
Knead the flour, yeast, olive oil, water and salt. Let rise for 1 hour.
Spread on parchment paper flat and thin. Make dimples with your fingers.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake at 220°C for 20-25 minutes until it gets a golden crust.
Blind bake for 15+5 minutes at 180°C. Let cool completely.
Spread the pastry cream evenly and arrange the strawberries decoratively.
Brush with fruit glaze for a glossy finish. Chill in the fridge for 1 hour. Dust with powdered sugar just before serving.
Make a caramel from the sugar and spread it over the bottom of the mold.
Beat the eggs with the sugar, hot milk and vanilla. Strain and pour over the caramel.
Bake in a water bath at 160°C for 55 minutes. Chill 4 hours in the fridge before turning out.
Mix the grated pumpkin with the eggs, sugar and olive oil.
Add the flour, cinnamon and baking powder. Mix until you get a uniform batter.
Pour into a baking pan and bake at 175°C for 50 minutes.
